AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 58
Document N ° MAX VIZ Series
139G0290X002 IR Camera
GENERAL INFORMATION
The MAX VIZ Series IR Camera system provides an IR external
image forward of the helicopter which may be displayed on the MFD
and/or central (5th) display or other displays depending on the
customer requirements for the system. The IR external image is a
visual aid in conditions of reduced visibility.
The system consists of Long Wave Infrared camera mounted either on
top of the cockpit roof EVS 1500 Part No. 4G9750F00311 (Figure 1) or
under the aircraft nose, below the pilots seat, EVS 1500 Part No.
4G9750F00312 or EVS 2300 Part No 4G9750F00313 (Figure 2)
facing forward, a power supply with processing electronics and
necessary cabling.
The power supply is integrated with the processing electronics and
necessary cabling for the EVS 2300 Part No 4G9750F00313.
The IR camera circuit breaker and the system ON/OFF switch are
located on the Auxiliary Circuit Breaker panel. When switched ON and
selected on MFD and/or the central (5th) display a video test pattern is
displayed for approximately 5 seconds followed by an OK message.
After approximately 20 seconds from power on an IR image is
presented on the display. When switched ON the IR camera carries
out an automatic recalibration of the IR sensor every 4 minutes. This
recalibration is noted by a 1 second blanking of the screen with the
message CAL displayed. Depending on customization this calibration
can be inhibited when the NUC switch, on the overhead Auxiliary
Circuit Breaker Panel, is set to NUC OFF selection.
The EVS display may be presented as full size on the VIDEO page of
the MFD and/or central (5th) display. By selecting the WFOV/NFOV
switch, located on the overhead Auxiliary Circuit Breaker panel, it is
possible to choose from Narrow or Wide field of view. When the
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
system is OFF, the switch position is set to WFOV. On the MAX VIZ
EVS 2300 system P/N 4G9750F00313, Narrow or Wide field of view
selection affects both the IR and Color Images.
The brightness and contrast can be adjusted on the 5th display as
required.
The camera is automatically anti-iced with its own internal heaters
when the camera is ON.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S58-1
Rev. 23

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 60
Document N ° Night Vision Goggle
139G0290X002 Operations
DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
Abbreviations and acronyms used throughout this Supplement are
defined as follows:
— IR : Infra Red
— NVG : Night Vision Goggles
— NVIS : Night Vision Imaging System
GENERAL INFORMATION
For NVG operations the NVIS compatible lighting systems,
P/N 4G3360F00111 and EPIC software Phase 4, or subsequent, are
required. The NVIS compatible lighting consists of internal and
external lighting modifications to make the aircraft compatible for the
use with NVG systems.
The aircraft configuration involving internal/external emitting/reflecting
equipment approved for use with NVG is described in the Report
139G3360A001 AW139 NVG COMPATIBILITY REFERENCE
HANDBOOK. Any internal/external emitting/reflecting equipment and
NVG types not defined in the above AW report does not permit NVG
Operations.
Internal Lighting
The NVIS compatible cockpit and cabin installation consists of
compatible controller panels and lighting. See Document
139G3360A001 AW139 NVG COMPATIBILITY REFERENCE
HANDBOOK.
The cockpit lights are controlled by the standard instrument LT panel
(Figure 4) and display DIM panel (Figure 3) and the NVG LT panel
(Figure 1), all mounted in the interseat console. The NVG LT panel
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
includes the MODE NVG/NORM switch which is used to select the
brightness of the displays. When selected to NORM full brightness is
available, via the standard dimmers, for the displays, instruments and
master warning/caution panels. When NVG is selected the displays
maximum brightness is limited to a prefixed level, however, full
brightness is available for the instruments and brightness may still be
adjusted by the standard dimmers. The master warning/caution lights
are reduced to the fixed night operation brightness level.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S60-1
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2428 ===
Supplement 60 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Night Vision Goggle Document N°
Operations 139G0290X002
The cockpit dome light (flood light) is also controlled from the standard
LT panel and is a white NVG compatible light.
The cabin lights, controlled by the CABIN dimmer on the NVG LT
panel. If white, non NVG compatible, lights are mounted in the cabin
roof they are automatically switched OFF when the MODE switch on
the LT panel is selected to NVG. If NVG compatible lights are mounted
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
they remain ON and their brightness may be adjusted.
The STORM ON/OFF switch on the NVG LT panel, controls the
cockpit STORM lights, which are non NVG compatible and are
mounted on the overhead panel. When the NVG LT panel MODE
switch is selected to NVG these lights are made inoperative
independent of the position of the STORM switch.
The EMERG light ON/ARM/OFF gated switch controls the cabin and
external emergency lights (an EMERG light pushbutton is also
available in the cabin, Figure 2). These are non NVG compatible and
function regardless of the position of the MODE switch. In ARM
position the emergency lights come on only when the aircraft electrical
power is removed.
The cockpit utility lights are NVG compatible.
Additionally a cockpit cabin dividing curtain or panel may be installed
to prevent inadvertent entry of non NVG compatible light from the
cabin, (See 139G3360A001 AW139 NVG COMPATIBILITY
REFERENCE HANDBOOK). An equivalent curtain, which prevent
light leakage from the cabin to the cockpit, approved by the competent
authority, may be installed.
External Lighting
The NVIS compatible external lighting consists of:
— An anti-collision light which is NVIS friendly normal light
— Position lights which are NVIS friendly normal light
— Secondary landing light (searchlight) with selectable normal (white
light) and IR light options.
Page S60-2 E.A.S.A. Approved

External lights are controlled by the standard EXTERNAL LIGHTS
overhead panel.
In NORMAL or NVG MODE the anticollision (ACOLL) and position
(POSLT) lights, when switched ON, operate with visible light but are
NVIS compatible. In NORMAL MODE the landing lights, when
switched ON using either collective switch, operate in non NVIS com-
patible white light mode. The secondary landing light (LDG LT2) only
can be switched to IR using the SRCH/LDG switch WHITE/IR selec-
tion located in the overhead DC Generation and Distribution panel. In
NVG MODE the landing light (LDG LT) is automatically switched OFF,
the LDG LT2 remains available and selectable to white non NVIS
compatible or IR by the WHITE/IR selector.

139G0290X002 Operations
SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
GENERAL
Any change to the aircraft configuration involving light emitting or
reflective equipment or NVG model types not included in document
139G3360A001 AW139 NVG COMPATIBILITY REFERENCE
HANDBOOK makes the aircraft NOT NVG COMPATIBLE and NVG
operations are not permitted.
TYPE OF OPERATION
— The Operator must receive NVG operations approval by the
Competent Authority in accordance with the applicable National
Operating Regulations.
MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW
For two pilot operations both pilots must be equipped with the same
type of NVGs (Green phosphor or white phosphor, mixing of phosphor
screen is not permitted).
For Single pilot operations (see Supplement 24 or Supplement 32 FAA
Only):
— an additional, trained, crew member must be equipped with and
use the same phosphor screen of NVGs as the pilot during
take-off and landing, on unimproved sites, to assist in obstacle
identification and clearance.
— an additional crew member using NVG’s is not required during
Take Off and Landing on improved sites and when the aircraft is
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters above 300 ft AGL and in cruise.
All crew members must be familiar with NVG operating procedures
and, if using NVGs they must be of the same phosphor screen as the
pilot’s.
WEIGHT AND CG LIMITATIONS
After NVIS compatible internal and external lighting installation, the
new empty weight and CG location must be determined.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S60-5
Rev. 30

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 61
Document N ° Additional Secondary
139G0290X002 Landing Light
GENERAL INFORMATION
The additional secondary landing light (RH LDG LT2) installation P/N
4G3340F01811 (NVG Compatible) or P/N 4G3340F01812 (Non NVG
Compatible), introduces an additional secondary landing light (search-
light) which is an identical unit as the standard LH LDG LT2 but
mounted under the aircraft on the right hand side (See Figure 1).
The control of the two secondary landing lights is via the LT control
panel installed in the interseat console (See Figure 2 or Figure 4) and
the standard five way switch mounted on each collective.
(See Figure 3).
When the SELECT switch on the LT panel is set to NONE neither of
the two LDG LT2 can be operated. When selected to RH, (and the
UNSTOW STOW/OFF switch is in STOW/OFF position the RH LDG
LT2 remains stowed and unpowered and a white status message RH
LDG LT2 SEL illuminates on the CAS. Selecting the UNSTOW STOW/
OFF switch to UNSTOW the RH light remains stowed but is powered.
By pressing the five way switch, on either collective, in the central
position the RH light is turned on, the green advisory message
SEARCH LT ON illuminates on the CAS and the RH ON indicator light
on the LT panel illuminates. The light remains stowed until the collec-
tive five way switch is moved to EXT which extends the light. The light
may then be directed left (L) or right (R) and down (RETR) or up (EXT)
by pushing on the beep switch. Pressing the central position again
turns the light off but leaves it extended. With the light switched off it is
not possible to move the light. At any time selecting the RH UNSTOW
STOW/OFF switch to STOW/OFF will stow and switch off (if on) the
light.
The same procedure is used for the LH LDG LT2 secondary landing
light mounted on the left hand side.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
A further characteristic of the system is that if one secondary landing
light is extended and on, then the LT panel SELECT switch is selected
to the other LDG LT2 this second light may then be switched on,
extended and moved as required by the five position switch on either
collective. The first light will then remain on, and in the last set posi-
tion, giving increased illumination. Both lights may then be controlled
one at a time by selecting the SELECT switch.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S61-1

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 62
Document N ° Radio Equipment
139G0290X002 V/UHF TALON RT-8108
GENERAL INFORMATION
The V/UHF TALON RT-8108 is an AM/FM analog/digital radio commu-
nication system.The system comprises of the RT-8108 transceiver, the
RCU-8150 control panel and dedicated antenna with Logic Converter
Unit.
The ICS panel is used to access the radio system, either COM 3 or
COM 4 depending on the configuration. Control of the radio is via the
TALON RCU-8150 Control Panel, mounted in the interseat console.
The control panel incorporates the controls used to switch the radio
ON/OFF, configure the radio frequecies or carry out a BIT check. See
Figure 1.
The TALON Radio System provides AM and FM electronic
counter-countermeasure (ECCM) modes HAVE QUICK, HAVE
QUICK II and TALON. The tranceiver also provides the capability for
combinations of secure, jamresistent or non-jam resistent, and voice
or data communications. The RT-8108 can tune 25-kHz channels in
2.5 kHz increments over the frequency range 30.000 to 399.9925
MHz (AM), and can transmit and receive voice on 8.33kHz channels in
the ATC band 118.000 to 136.975, using non ECCM mode.
The RT-8108 inhibits transmissions from 108.000 to 117.9975 MHz, in
non-ECCM modes of operation.
The Talon Radio can support up to 250 preset channels including
ECCM channels, two Guard Receiver Frequencies (121.5 MHz/243.0
MHz) and 57 permanently stored Maritime channels.
For completed details of V/UHF TALON Radio refer TALON VHF/UHF/
EP Communications System RT-8108, Operators Guide Doc No
523-0806336-002117, latest issue.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S62-1

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 64
Document N ° Talon FLIR
139G0290X002
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Talon FLIR P/N 4G9350F00511 is a remote controlled day/night
high resolution, infrared (IR) imaging system with colour video.
The system consists of a Turret Sensor Unit (TSU) with IR camera,
colour Charged Coupled Device (CCD) camera, laser range finder
and optional laser pointer mounted on the left hand side of the helicop-
ter (Figure 1 & Figure 2). A Joystick Control Unit (JCU) mounted in the
interseat console and operated from the right hand seat, contains all
the controls necessary to operate the FLIR (Figure 4) and a Control
Electronics Unit (CEU) which processes the electronics for the sys-
tem.
The TSU is gyro stabilized and its azimuth and elevation are controlled
by the JCU. The TSU can be rotated 360° in both azimuth and eleva-
tion and internal rate gyros sense platform motion and vibrations and
remove unwanted effects. The TSU has an automated anti-ice system
that engages at temperatures below 0° C.
The IR camera produces images in total darkness or in low visibility or
low contrast ambient condition. The IR camera has a selectable 1.8X
optical extender to increase stand off capability. The CCD camera pro-
vides images in visible and low light ambient conditions.
The eye safe laser range finder (ESLRF) is a Class 1 device.
The IR and CCD cameras provide video outputs that can be moni-
tored on either pilot or copilot MFD. Either IR or CCD images can be
selected independently on pilot and copilot MFD or both images in
miniature. If a digital map is installed the copilot and pilot MFD will
only display the same source data, either FLIR or digital map.
The optional central 5th display can be used to display either image
but only the selected (active) FLIR camera image will be displayed.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The optional Laser Pointer is eye unsafe Class 3b device. When
installed a series of 4 safety interlocks including a Laser Safety Switch
(Figure 3) must be met which provides an interlock to stop the laser
being activated inadvertently.
For full information on the use of the Talon FLIR refer to Talon Imaging
Systems Operator’s Manual P/N 23393-000 Rev 1 or latest issue.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S64-1

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 65
Document N ° Cabin Comp Ext with
139G0290X002 Long Aux Fuel Tank
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Longitudinal Auxiliary Fuel Tank is a single additional fuel tank.
The tank consists of a fuel cell installed on the left hand side of the bay
above the standard fuel tanks. (See Figure 1)
The tank is connected to the left hand part of the main fuel tank and
forms an extension to the main fuel tank through one connector. It is
filled via the main tank and feeds the main tank by gravity. A fuel vent
line from the tank is connected to the main tank vent line system and
an electrical connection provides Fuel Gauging Control Unit informa-
tion. The Fuel Gauging System automatically compensates for the
additional fuel quantity.
The Longitudinal Auxiliary Fuel Tank is compatible with Supplement
54 Cabin Compartment Extension, however, only the Full Cabin
Extension P/N 4G5340F00111 may be utilised, with the following
restrictions (See Figure 2):
• No floor panel mounted in the tunnel
• Loading Area 1 and 2 cannot be used for loads
• Rails on the tunnel walls are not fitted.
For Full Cabin Extension procedures not covered in this supplement
see Supplement 54 Cabin Compartment Extension.
Note
The Loading Area 3 modifications in this Supplement are
identical to the modifications described in Supplement
54. For the Loading Area 3 configurations and restraint
net P/N refer to Supplement 54.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S65-1
Rev. 1

GENERAL INFORMATION
This supplement provides information for the cabin configured with
two vertically sliding windows.
The sliding windows replace the forward passenger windows on the
left and right hand side of the aircraft. The windows, when unlocked,
can be opened vertically downward and when up (closed) they can be
locked in the closed position.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director (FD) provides commands that are
normally coupled to the autopilot (AP) for automatic flight path control
around the three axes of the aircraft plus collective. At Power Up one
of the two FD is automatically selected and configured as Master
(priority). At every Power Up the FD selected as Master (priority) is
alternated.
The 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director requires either EPIC Phase 5,
(software release EB7030191-00107) or Phase 6 (software release
EB7030191-00108 & 109) or Phase 7 (software release EB7030191-
00110/00111/00112/00114/00115/00117/00118) or Phase 8 (software
release EB7030191-00113/00120). The system contains all the
functions of the 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director and in addition the
improvements of the Phase 5 and later software.
When coupled, both autopilots drive the actuators to satisfy the
references provided by the priority FD.
When uncoupled the pilot can manually fly the commands.
In either case, pitch, roll command bars/collective cue are presented
on each PFD, depending on the mode selected.
The FD uses the Navigation source and data reference presented on
the selected PFD. The selected PFD is indicated by the green PFD
couple arrow which is controlled by the PFD button on the Guidance
Controller (See Figure 2). The SAR Guidance Controller (See
Figure 3) is an alternative controller and has SAR mode buttons,
however, the extra pushbuttons are not active. Either Guidance
Controller can be used with the 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director
system Phase 5. (For Phase 5 and later installation that includes SAR
mode functions see Supplement 69).
A green couple arrow is also presented on the side of the PFD
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
pushbutton on the Guidance Controller. When a FD mode is engaged
the coupled function is automatically engaged. The FD may be
uncoupled by pressing the CPL pushbutton on the Autopilot Controller
(See Figure 1). The coupled function is automatically forced to
uncoupled whenever the AP ATT mode is off or becomes inoperative.
Armed and captured FD modes are displayed with messages along
the top line of the PFD: Collective and pitch mode messages on the
left of the selected PFD arrow and lateral mode on the right. Armed
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S67-1

Armed lateral modes messages are: VOR, VAPP, LOC, BC, LNAV
and captured VOR, VAPP, OS, LOC, BC, LNAV, HDG, HOV.
Armed collective modes are: GS, VGP, VRT (Phase 8 and later) and
captured ALT, GS, VS, GA, ALTA, ALVL, RHT, VGP, TU, VRT (Phase
8 and later).
Engaged vertical pitch modes are IAS, HOV, DCL, GA, TU.
A chime sounds whenever either a lateral, vertical (pitch), or vertical
(collective) FD mode changes from its previous state, i.e.:
— a mode changes from engaged to disengaged or vice-versa
— a mode changes from arm to captured
— a mode changes from coupled to uncoupled.
An aural tone (“bip-bip”) sounds for any change in altitude or radar
height mode reference datum.

SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
WEIGHT LIMITATIONS
— For weights up to 6400 kg see basic RFM.
— For weights between 6400 kg and 6800 kg see Supplement 50.
— For weights between 6800 kg and 7000 kg see Supplement 90.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR MODES LIMITATIONS
• The following FD modes are inoperative on the SAR Guidance
Control panel:
— TD/H — MOT — WTR — VNAV
• Collective modes must not be engaged if either or both engines are
in MANUAL MODE
• The RHT and TU modes can only be engaged over flat surfaces
which are clear of obstructions.

SECTION 2 - NORMAL PROCEDURES
FLIGHT DIRECTOR - GENERAL
For full details of FD operation and use see “PRIMUS EPIC Integrated
Avionics and Flight Control System for the AW/AB139 Helicopter -
Pilot’s Guide” latest issue and FMS Pilot’s Guide latest issue.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR MODES ENGAGEMENT
The AFCS Flight Director function provides 4 axis guidance modes.
Selection of most FD modes is carried out using pushbuttons on the
Guidance Controller. HOV mode may also be engaged using the
th
cyclic beep trim centre position (5 position). Each mode may be de-
selected by pressing the associated pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller. However GA and TU modes may only be engaged by
either collective GA button and disengaged by engaging a different
mode for pitch and collective axis. All engaged modes may be
deselected simultaneously by using the FD STBY button located on
the cyclic sticks or the STBY button on the Guidance Controller.
The Guidance Controller pushbuttons include a green annuciator that
illuminates when the mode is selected. FD mode annuciations (green
when captured and white when armed) also appear on the PFD.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR COUPLED AND UNCOUPLED OPERATIONS
Selecting a FD mode by pressing the pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller will couple the FD whenever the AP is in ATT hold.
Selecting a FD mode by pressing the pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller with the ATT OFF (i.e. SAS or no stabilisation), the FD will
be engaged in the uncoupled mode.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
During coupled operation the FD may be uncoupled by pressing the
CPL pushbutton on the Autopilot Controller which will cause a white
UCPL caption to appear on the PFD.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S67-13
Rev. 26

CAUTION
• Whenever the FD is coupled and the AP reverts to SAS
or has a complete loss of autostabilization, the FD will
revert to uncoupled mode.
• When the AP reverts to SAS no UCPL caption will Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
appear on the PFD.
With the FD engaged, in coupled or uncoupled mode, the following is
displayed:
— Navigation source and reference data in magenta colour on the
selected PFD
— Navigation source and reference data in cyan colour on the non
selected PFD
— Navigation source in amber on both PFD’s when both PFD’s have
the same navigation data source.
During coupled operation the HDG, ALT, IAS, VS, ALTA, RHT, HOV,
TU, VRT modes may be controlled by either pilot. When engaged in
coupled mode, the reference data may be adjusted by using the
Display Controller (HDG, ALT SEL), collective beep trim/FTR (ALT,
ALTA, VS, RHT, TU, VRT) or cyclic beep trim/FTR (IAS, HOV , HDG,
TU).
During uncoupled operation changes of reference data for IAS, HDG
and HOV modes are carried out by pressing the cyclic FTR button,
which updates the reference data to the actual values at the time the
button is released. Changes of reference data for ALT, VS and RHT
are carried out by the collective beep trim. Collective FTR does not
modify the collective modes reference.
For IAS, HDG, RHT and VS on the selected PFD, a magenta digital
readout reference datum is displayed above the appropriate flight
instrument and a magenta bug at a position corresponding to the
selected reference. For ALT, only the magenta bug is displayed
permanently while the digital readout is displayed for 5 seconds
whenever the reference is modified and the ALTA reference is
present.

Whenever a collective mode is engaged (ALT, VS, ALTA, GS, VGP,
GA, ALVL, RHT, TU) a collective position cue appears on the PFD
beside the ADI. There are some collective FD modes (e.g. RHT, VRT,
etc.) based upon RadAlt. When one of them is engaged, a magenta
bug is displayed on the Rad Alt tape and the radalt readout is
displayed in magenta. See Figure 2-1 (S/W Phase 5, 6 & 7) and
Figure 2-2 & Figure 2-3 (S/W Phase 8 and later).
COLLECTIVE PI LIMITING FUNCTION
During collective coupled operation the collective movement is limited
by the following PI values:
— Maximum 97% AEO (95% at altitudes above 10000 ft (3050 m) Hp)
— Maximum 106% AEO for airspeed less than 60 KIAS (5 MIN
message displayed beside collective cue, see Figure 2-1)
— Maximum 140% OEI
— Minimum 5% AEO
— Minimum 10% OEI.
When PI limiting function is active and is limiting maximum collective
movement, an amber LIM caption is displayed beside the collective
cue. See Figure 2-1.
If PI limiting is active with IAS engaged and the required reference for
VS, ALTA, RHT, GA, or ALT cannot be achieved the airspeed will
automatically reduce as necessary to achieve the collective mode
reference. If the collective mode reference cannot be maintained,
when the airspeed has reached a minimum of 80 KIAS this airspeed
will be maintained and the collective mode reference will be reduced.
While the mode reference values cannot be maintained or achieved
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters that mode caption is displayed in amber on the PFD.
CAUTION
If PI limiting is active with ALT/RHT engaged and the
reference height cannot be maintained the aural warning
“Altitude Altitude” will warn the pilot when the maximum
allowed deviation from the reference height has been
exceeded.

SAFETY FLY-UP FUNCTIONALITY WHEN FD MODES ENGAGED
The Fly-Up Collective Safety Function is a height protection function
which is always active when at least one Rad Alt is valid. The function
is activated when any collective FD mode is engaged and coupled and
the Safety Height is passed. When the function is activated the aircraft
is automatically flown back up to the Safety Height. The Safety Height
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
is a function of the Rad Alt Reference (or a fixed height for Barometric
modes) and depends on the actual collective mode engaged.
Further to the Safety Height there is also an Ultimate Fly-Up Limit, a
fixed height (not adjustable) which, if passed, will automatically cause
the aircraft to fly back up to this height or the Safety Height, if higher.
The following table gives the Safety Height Rad Alt limits and Ultimate
Fly-Up Limit for the different collective modes:

When the collective Fly Up safety function is activated, due to an
height excursion below the Safety Height or Ultimate Fly-Up limit, the
aural message ‘ALTITUDE ALTITUDE’ is triggered and a HTLM
message is displayed on the PFD on the top left of the attitude indica-
tor. When the collective is automatically driven up, it is normally limited
by the PI limiting function. Should the relevant MUH limits be
exceeded the PI limits will be moved up as follows:
— Maximum 121% AEO for airspeeds below 60 KIAS
— Maximum 176% OEI for airspeeds below 60 KIAS
— Maximum 110% AEO for airspeeds above 60 KIAS
— Maximum 160% OEI for airspeeds above 60 KIAS.
CAUTION
When voice message “Altitude Altitude” is triggered with
a HTLM message then the aircraft has descended
below the safety height. Ensure separation from terrain
visually or, if not possible, establish a positive rate of
climb to a safe height.
CAUTION
(Applicable only for Phase 5 or 6)
When descending over terrain, with a collective mode
engaged and after a continuous descent of at least

MODE DESCRIPTIONS
The following descriptions assume the modes are coupled, unless
stated otherwise.
HDG Heading Hold Mode. This mode steers the aircraft to the
heading reference bug displayed on the PFD. The
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
heading bug can be adjusted using the HEADING knob
on the Remote Instrument Controller and can be
synchronized with the actual heading by pressing the
HEADING knob (PUSH SYNC). The heading reference
bug can be synchronized to the actual heading by
pressing the cyclic FTR button or modified using the
cyclic beep trim switch left or right. In HDG mode turns
are performed at standard rate 1 (3 deg/sec.).
ALT Barometric Altitude Hold Mode. This mode maintains the
barometric altitude existing at the time of engagement.
The altitude reference is displayed as a set bug on the
PFD altitude tape. If the ALT SEL knob has not been
previously moved (i.e. no ALTA activation) the ALT
reference will also be displayed as a magenta digital
readout. The altitude reference can be adjusted using the
collective beep trim (aft to increase altitude) or by
pressing FTR button, flying to desired altitude, and
releasing. An audio tone is produced when the altitude
reference is changed. The collective PI limiting function is
enabled when ALT mode is coupled.
CAUTION
In ALT mode the voice message “Altitude Altitude” is
triggered when altitude exceeds the reference altitude by
±150 ft (46 m) .
Note
ALT mode can be engaged with HOV mode (as an
alternative to the RHT mode).
Page S67-20 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2529 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 67
Document N ° 4 Axis Enhanced
139G0290X002 FD (Phase 5 and later)
IAS Airspeed Hold Mode. This mode maintains the airspeed
existing at the time of engagement. When engaged the
airspeed reference is displayed as a set bug and a digital
readout on the PFD. The airspeed reference bug is
adjusted by either using the cyclic beep fore/aft or
repositioning the cyclic, with the FTR button depressed,
to the required airspeed and releasing FTR button. The
airspeed reference is adjustable via the cyclic beep
switch between 50 KIAS (60 KIAS for Phase 5 and 6)
and Vne less 5 KIAS. If airspeed, at time of engagement,
is higher than Vne less 5 KIAS then it is automatically
reduced to Vne less 5 KIAS.
ALTA Altitude Acquire Mode. This mode, when engaged with
a barometric altitude preselect reference set (through
ALT SEL knob), will automatically engage the IAS mode
and the aircraft is flown towards the preset altitude. The
final altitude reference is displayed as a cyan bug and
digital readout above the altitude scale. The vertical
speed reference is displayed as a bug and digital readout
on the PFD. The preset vertical speeds are +1000 fpm or
-750 fpm in the direction of the preset altitude. The
vertical speed reference can be changed by either using
the collective beep trim (aft to increase) or with collective
FTR button depressed, moving to the required vertical
speed and releasing. When the preset altitude is
achieved the mode will transition to ALT mode and the
IAS mode will remain engaged. The collective PI limiting
function is enabled when ALTA mode is coupled. When
collective PI limiting is active the airspeed is reduced to
maintain vertical speed reference.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Note
(Applicable only for Phase 5 or 6)
Engaging ALTA while climbing with a rate of climb greater
than 1500 fpm or descending with a rate of descent
greater than 1500 fpm, the system may erroneously
transition to ALT. The aircraft will, however, reach the
selected final altitude.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S67-21

APP or DCL button, while below 2400 ft AGL. Intercepting
the projected glidepath, the VRT mode is automatically
captured. Flying above 2500 ft AGL will result in VRT
mode disarming or disengagement.

FMS target speed. If, however, the speed is less or equal
to the FMS target speed, the DCL mode arms.

engaged, engages and the aircraft starts to decelerate to

and transition will occur at a climb rate of 200 fpm

reaching the reference value 200 ft when the RHT is
automatically engaged. The aircraft then accelerates to
the airspeed reference of 80 KIAS and the IAS mode is
engaged. The reference height can be modified by the

RHT Radar Height Hold Mode. This mode maintains the
aircraft at the radar height at the time of engagement
when the radar altimeter indications are within the
threshold limits. A reference bug on the radar altimeter
tape and a digital readout above the radar altimeter tape
are presented. The reference height can be changed by
depressing the collective FTR switch flying to the Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
required height and releasing the FTR switch or by using
the collective beep trim switch (aft to increase). An audio
tone is produced when the height reference is changed.
The collective PI limiting function is enabled when RHT
mode is coupled.
HOV Hover/velocity Hold Mode. HOV mode can be engaged
by pressing HOV mode on Guidance Controller or the
cyclic beep trim centre position (5th position). The HOV
mode utilizes the AHRS ground velocities to maintain
hover or low speed flying. At engagement of this mode
the helicopter groundspeed reference is set to zero and
the RHT is automatically engaged if a valid radar
altimeter signal is available and within the threshold
limits. RHT mode can be subsequently disengaged
independently and replaced by ALT if required. A hover
symbology with the ground velocity vector bug is also
displayed on the HSI. See Figure 2-4. When the mode is
engaged, the velocity vector reference can be changed
by pressing the cyclic FTR switch, flying to the desired
lateral and longitudinal speed and releasing, or by using
the cyclic beep trim to move the bug to the desired
velocities. If the cyclic beep trim switch is pressed in the
th
centre position (5 position) the longitudinal and lateral
velocity references are set to zero.
CAUTION
The HOV mode maintains a groundspeed reference
therefore pilot must ensure that crosswind and rearwind
speed limits are not exceeded (see Section 1 Basic Flight
Manual). If wind limits are exceeded directional control
may not be maintained.

FMS FUNCTIONAL INCONSISTENCIES ONLY FOR EPIC
SOFTWARE PHASE 5 OR PHASE 6 INSTALLED
1. When the destination runway/helipad is changed, without an
arrival or approach entered, and the runway/helipad is the TO
waypoint, the FMS incorrectly places the runway/helipad behind
the helicopter, shows it as the FROM waypoint, disengages LNAV Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
(if engaged) and the deviation bar is shown as INVALID.
Recommended corrective action if problem scenario encountered:
• Perform ‘Direct To’ to destination runway/helideck
• Select desired runway/helipad and activate
• Re-engage LNAV mode.
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201002000030 for
further information.
Problem not present for software version EB7030191-00109
(Phase 6.5)
2. The ‘Direct-To Recovery’ procedure should not be used in any
phase of flight.
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201001000021 for
further information.
3. Approach and/or Star procedures which contain a certain
geometry of consecutive AT altitude constraints exhibit a TOD
misplacement and premature descent.
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201010000078 for
further information.
Problem not present for software version EB7030191-00109
(Phase 6.5)
4. Software version EB7030191-00109 (Phase 6.5) only, Activating
vectors during an FMS approach may result in below-glide path
VGP indications at the FAF. The crew should monitor VGP
indications during glide path capture and execute a missed
approach if VGP indications are not consistent with normal glide
path capture.

CYCLIC FORCE TRIM RELEASE FAILURE
Cyclic FTR failure, due to a fault which removes electric power to the
clutches of the longitudinal and lateral trim, will result in cyclic
longitudinal and lateral clutches becoming permanently engaged. This
will require the pilot to fly the aircraft against the cyclic force spring feel
to manoeuvre the aircraft, or use the cyclic beep trim, as cyclic FTR
button does not function.
In this case it is suggested that a cyclic FD mode (i.e. IAS) is engaged
and the cyclic beep trim used to maintain the required flight condition.
COLLECTIVE FORCE TRIM OFF OR FAIL
When a FD mode is engaged, and coupled, and the collective trim is
switched OFF (Miscellaneous Control Panel) or fails, a chime sound is
generated, the collective may not maintain its selected position, the
CLTV annunciation will illuminate on the top left of the ADI display, and
the CLTV/YAW OFF green advisory will illuminate on the CAS window.
Collective modes are available uncoupled only.
COLLECTIVE FORCE TRIM RELEASE FAILURE
Collective force trim release failure, due to a fault which removes
electric power to the clutch of the collective trim will result in the
collective clutch becoming permanently engaged. This will require the
pilot to fly the aircraft against the collective force spring feel to
manoeuvre the aircraft, or use the collective beep trim, as the
collective FTR button does not function.
In this case when large collective movements are not required, it is
suggested that a collective FD mode (i.e. ALT) is engaged and the
collective beep trim used to maintain the required flight condition.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S67-37
Rev. 26

FLIGHT DIRECTOR FAILURE
No CAS Warning or Caution messages are generated to indicate FD
malfunctions. However indication on both PFD displays indicate the

GENERAL INFORMATION
The following functions are introduced and operational with the
installation of EPIC Phase 5 (software release EB7030191-00107) or
Phase 6 (software release EB7030191-00108 & 109) or Phase 7
(software release EB7030191-00110/00111/00112/00114/00115/
00117/00118) or Phase 8 (software release EB7030191-00113/
00120).
New FMS Functions
— SAR Search Patterns (Optional, but included with Supplement 69)
— Helicopter Performance pages.
New Basic Display Functions
— CAS caution ‘GEN OVLD’ added and generator load display
modified.
— Aural ‘Check Height’ and ‘Low Speed’ alerts.
— OAT sensor miscompare indication.
— AHRS G/S velocity miscompare indication.
— Wind indication.
— CAT A symbology indications on PFD’s.
Optional Functions
— Support of SBAS GNSS Receivers.

Additional Functions 139G0290X002
FMS NEW FUNCTIONS
SAR SEARCH PATTERNS
— SAR type Search Patterns are available in the FMS which, when
inserted in a flight plan using the MCDU, are displayed on the
MFD. The following Search Patterns are available (in brackets are Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
the legends on the MCDU):
• Expanding Square (SQUARE)
• Sector (SECTOR)
• Creeping Ladder (LADDER)
• Parallel (PARALLEL).
— Search Pattern selection and activation are performed on the
MCDU starting from the PATTERNS page, see Figure 1, that can
be accessed from NAV INDEX.
When SEARCH is selected, the active (or stored) Flight Plan page
is shown. At this point, inserting SEARCH on a valid waypoint the
SEARCH PATTERNS page is presented, see Figure 2, and the
selection of the required Search Pattern can be carried out.
Once a Search Pattern has been defined it can be flown
automatically by coupling to the FD. To fly the Search Pattern
coupled select NAV on the Guidance Controller. See Supplement
69.
— A search pattern is calculated from parameters input into the
MCDU and/or default values (which can be modified). The search
pattern waypoints are also entered into the Active Flight Plan
depending on the type of pattern selected:
• Search pattern approach waypoints are named SPAPx
• The initial fix or Start Position is named SPSTx
• The last waypoint in search pattern is named SPEXx
• Each search pattern in the Active Flight Plan uses matching
numbers (x=1, x=2 x=3 etc.) for approach, start position and
exit waypoints
Page S68-2 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2571 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 68
Document N ° EPIC S/W Phase 5 and later
139G0290X002 Additional Functions
• Waypoints between the SAR start and exit waypoints are
numbered sequentially i.e. SP001, SP002 etc.
— When flying a Search Pattern, the Search Pattern parameters can
be modified on the appropriate search pattern page. Any
parameter modified will take effect from the end of the current leg.
Note
Leg modification of Search Pattern parameters shall be
entered during the second half of the leg.
— A search pattern can be suspended at anytime by pressing PPOS
SUSP on the ACTIVE FLT PLAN page. The Search Pattern may
be resumed by pressing RESUME, on the ACTIVE FLT PALN
page, which will continue the Search Pattern after the aircraft has
returned to the previously suspended point.
— When flying a Search Pattern, if MOT is pressed the Search
Pattern is suspended. It may be resumed by pressing RESUME at
the end of the MOT.
Note
CHECK SAR SPEED will appear on MCDU scratchpad
(with no MSG on PFD) any time actual IAS is more than
5 KIAS with respect to the IAS selected within the SAR
Pattern Page.
Note
The search pattern airspeed should be adjusted as
required to guarantee that the pattern is flown correctly,
based on pattern geometry, taking into account the wind
direction and speed.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S68-3
Rev. 26

PERFORMANCE PAGES
For full information of performance data available refer to FMS Pilots
Guide latest issue. If any conflict exists between the FMS performance
data and that presented in the RFM, the RFM shall take precedence.
The following information is available in the MCDU performance
pages:
— PERFORMANCE INIT page 3/3 is used to initialize aircraft weight,
according to the actual configuration (See Figure 7). Weight data
are in kg.
PERFORMANCE INIT page comprised of:
• BOW and Basic CG
• Fuel Gauge - by default this is the actual fuel
• STR F/A - Stretcher weight (if installed) - fore and aft
• PILOTS - Total weight of pilot and co-pilot
• ROW 1/2/3 - Passenger weight, divided in 3 rows of seats
• Baggage - Total weight of baggage
• HOIST/HOOK - Load on hoist (if used)
Load on cargo hook (if used)
If GROSS WEIGHT is outside the authorized value, a dedicated
message will appear on the scratch pad:
“BELOW GROSS WEIGHT” aircraft weight less than 4400 kg
“CHECK GROSS WEIGHT” aircraft weight greater than 6400 kg *
“EXCEEDS MAX GROSS WEIGHT” aircraft weight greater than
6800 kg (PERF INIT not allowed)
Or when Weight Extension 7000 kg (Supplement 90) installed:
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
“EXCEEDS MAX GROSS WEIGHT” aircraft weight greater than
7000 kg (PERF INIT not allowed)
* For Operations above 6400 kg see Supplement 50 and 90 as
appropriate.
— The GROSS WEIGHT data is the value used for performance
computation in pages PERF DATA 1,2 & 3.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S68-9

— PERF DATA pages 1/4 and 2/4 (Figure 8 & Figure 9) gives

• Hover (Hover capability - Hover Ceiling - Height Velocity high

• Level flight (Best Range and Best Endurance information - page
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
1/4, Current Range and Current endurance - page 2/4).
Data for Hover Ceiling are assuming MCP rating and data for HV
are assuming OEI 2.5 min rating.
• No fuel reserve is calculated.
• PALT/OAT values of pressure altitude and OAT may be the
actual (digits in small font) or pilot entered (digits in large font).
According to these values the system calculates the
corresponding density altitude (DENS ALT).
Values are presented in inverse video when:
• Hover ceiling density altitude is lower than calculated (actual or
pilot entered) density altitude
• HT LOSS value is higher than actual aircraft height.
Note

Range and Best Endurance values are not available.

CAT A performance capability.
Data presented is, for different profiles, the CAT A ceiling
expressed in density altitude for the current or pilot selected GW.
Values are presented in inverse video if the ceiling is less than the
DENS ALT value.
— PERF DATA page 4/4 (Figure 11) displays the status of the
configuration for those components that can affect aircraft
performance. Performance data in pages 1/4, 2/4, 3/4 are relative
to the status shown on page 4/4.

Additional Functions 139G0290X002
NEW BASIC DISPLAY FUNCTIONS
‘GEN OVLD’ CAS CAUTION AND GENERATOR DISPLAY
A generator overload CAS caution has been added, 1(2) GEN OVLD
for overload conditions of the generators.
The MFD generator load display has been modified to indicate the
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
linear reduction in the permitted maximum loads for altitudes between
15000 ft Hp and 20000 ft Hp.
AURAL ‘CHECK HEIGHT’ ALERT
An Aural message ‘CHECK HEIGHT CHECK HEIGHT’ associated
with a MIN message in the attitude area of the PFD is generated
when the Radio Altitude is less than or equal to the DH set on the
selected PFD. The PFD message will still be presented, even after
AWG system failure and consequent loss of aural warnings.
Note
If the FD fails (amber FD FAIL on PFD) the DH selected
on the RH pilot’s PFD is taken as the CHECK HEIGHT
reference.
Note
The Aural message is heard again if the aircraft has
climbed at least 20 ft above the selected DH then subse-
quently descends below the DH.
AURAL ‘LOW SPEED’ ALERT
An Aural message ’LOW SPEED LOW SPEED’ is generated when the
FD mode has automatically disengaged (announced by a chime) due
to the IAS dropping below the minimum speed for the applicable
speed range.
OAT SENSOR MISCOMPARE INDICATION
When a temperature difference of 6° C or greater is being experienced
between the two OAT systems the OAT indication changes to amber.
The OAT indication is the average between the two OAT sensors.
Page S68-14 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2583 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 68
Document N ° EPIC S/W Phase 5 and later
139G0290X002 Additional Functions
When the difference returns to below 6 °C the OAT indication reverts
back to white.
VELOCITY (GS) MISCOMPARE
A velocity miscompare indication VEL has been added to inform
the pilot that the velocity output from the two AHRS differs by 2 kts, or
more, for groundspeed below 20 kts.
WIND INDICATION SYMBOLOGY
The wind symbology has been modified to change to amber when the
wind value has been frozen due to the TAS being less than 40 kts or
for a period of six minutes if, crossing 40 kts, the roll attitude was
greater than 3°.

Additional Functions 139G0290X002
CAT A SYMBOLOGY INDICATIONS ON PFD
CAT A symbology can be presented on the PFD to aid the pilot when
performing CAT A published Take-Off and Landing manoeuvres. The
symbology is displayed when the NR is set to 102% and the collective
CAT A pushbutton is pressed.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
— Take-Off symbology is presented when the aircraft is on the
ground. Subsequent pressing of the CAT A pushbutton toggles
through the following TAKE OFF profiles:
• Ground Level Heliport HELIPAD
• Short Field SHORT FIELD
• Clear Area CLEAR AREA
• Elevated Heliport/Helideck ELEV HELIPAD
• Ground Level and Elevated
Heliport/Helideck Back-Up BKUP HELIPAD
The selected profile label is displayed above the radio/nav
frequency panel on the PFD. See Figure 13.
— Landing symbology is presented when the aircraft is in flight above
400 ft AGL. Subsequent pressing of the CAT a pushbutton toggles
between the following LANDING profiles:
• Ground Level Heliport HELIPAD
• Short Field SHORT FIELD
• Clear Area CLEAR AREA
• Elevated Heliport/Helideck ELEV HELIPAD
The selected profile label is displayed above the radio/nav
frequency panel on the PFD. See Figure 13.
If an engine failure occurs, and a Balked Landing procedure is
required, the collective CAT A pushbutton may be pressed, to
activate the balked landing symbology, (prior to commencing the
balked landing procedure).
Page S68-16 E.A.S.A. Approved

Take-Off Symbology - Vertical Profile
The Take-Off profiles indicated on the PFD are to be used with the
following Supplement 12 CAT A Operation PARTs:
— HELIPAD - PART A - Ground Level and Elevated
Heliport/Helideck Vertical Take Off Procedure
— SHORT FIELD - PART B - Shortf Field Take Off Procedures
— ELEV HELIPAD - PART A - Ground Level and Elevated Heli
port/Helideck Vertical Take Off Procedure
— BKUP HELIPAD - PART C Ground Level and Elevated Heliport/
Helideck Back-Up Procedure
When on the ground after selection of any vertical Take-Off profile the
TDP height magenta bug is presented on the Rad Alt tape at the
default value of 35 ft (85 ft for BKUP HELIPAD). This value should be
modified, as required, for the profile being carried out using the DH
rotary knob.
CAUTION
The ELEV HELIPAD displays a default TDP value of
20 ft which is lower than the PART A - Ground Level and
Elevated Heliport/Helideck Vertical Take Off Procedure
TDP minimum so requires adjustment.
Once airborne in a 5 ft HIGE pressing the CAT A pushbutton acquires
the actual PI value and hover pitch attitude. The Target PI (HIGE
PI+Delta PI), with a magenta bug on the PI scale, and the hover
attitude, with a magenta bar on the attitude indicator, are presented.
The T-O may then be started by increasing PI to the indicated bug
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
position while climbing vertically. When the indicated TDP value is
achieved an audio warning “TDP TDP” is generated and the magenta
pitch attitude line moves to 10° nose down in 1”, it maintains the
attitude for 1” then moves back to 0° in 1”. The V magenta bug is
TOSS
indicated on the IAS tape and when this is achieved, the pitch attitude
magenta line moves to 5° nose up. After achieving Vy all the magenta
Take-Off bugs disappear.

Take-Off Symbology - Clear Area Profile
The Take-Off profile indicated on the PFD is to be used with the
following Supplement 12 CAT A Operation PART:
— CLEAR AREA - PART F - Clear Area Take Off Procedure
After selection of the Take-Off profile for the Clear Area the TDP
height magenta bug is presented on the Rad Alt tape at 30 ft. When in
a 5 ft HIGE pressing the CAT A pushbutton acquires the actual PI
value and hover pitch attitude. The Target PI (HIGE PI+Delta PI) with
a magenta bug on the PI scale, a magenta bar at 5° nose down on the
pitch attitude indicator and the TDP are then presented. The T-O may
be started by moving the aircraft pitch to the magenta line then
increasing PI to the indicated bug position to transition forward. When
the indicated TDP is achieved the magenta pitch attitude line moves to
5° nose up and airspeed bug of 50 KIAS is presented on the IAS tape.
After achieving Vy all the magenta Take-Off bugs disappear.
Note
If the aircraft pitch does not reach -5° nose down, within 3
seconds of the TDP aural warning, a ‘CHECK PITCH’
message is displayed on the attitude indicator and a
CHECK PITCH’ aural warning is generated.
Note
Take-Off symbology for all profiles (PI bug, labels and
pitch reference line) will be removed when the aircraft
reaches a height 200 ft greater than the TDP, while the
IAS bug will be removed when crossing Vy.

Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters Balked Landing bugs disappear.

OPTIONAL FUNCTIONS
SBAS GNSS Receivers
SBAS GPS kits 3G3450F00112/113 or P/N 3G3450F00412/413 (long
nose variant) can be installed as an option. They include the GNSS
receivers P/N 245-604067-100/101 (respectively), which are qualified
per TSO C145/C146, and the GPS Antenna P/N S67-1575-145, which
is qualified per TSO C190. These kits provide SBAS capability.
A second GNSS SBAS receiver is also supported (see
Supplement 37).
When operating under SBAS coverage, the navigation mode
displayed on GPS 1 (or 2) STATUS page of the MCDUs is
‘DIFFERENTIAL’.
Note
System P/N 3G3450F00112/412 is compatible with
Primus EPIC Phase 5 and subsequent SW releases.
System P/N 3G3450F00113/413 is compatible with
Primus EPIC Phase 7 and later SW only and is required
to conduct LPV approaches. It is mandatory with SW
EB7030191-00110/00111/00112 (see Supplements 79,80
& 101).
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

GENERAL INFORMATION
The 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director (FD) provides commands that are
normally coupled to the autopilot (AP) for automatic flight path control
around the three axes of the aircraft plus collective. At Power Up one
of the two FD is automatically selected and configured as Master
(priority). At every Power Up the FD selected as Master (priority) is
alternated.
The 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director with SAR Modes system is the
complete version of the FD system and requires either EPIC Phase 5,
(software release EB7030191-00107) or Phase 6 (software release
EB7030191-00108 & 109) or Phase 7 (software release EB7030191-
00110/00111/00112/00114/00115/00117/00118) or Phase 8 (software
release EB7030191-00113/00120). The system contains all the
functions of the 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director, SAR modes and in
addition the improvements of the Phase 5 and later software.
When coupled, both autopilots drive the actuators to satisfy the
references provided by the priority FD.
When uncoupled the pilot can manually fly the commands.
In either case, pitch, roll command bars/collective cue are presented
on each PFD, depending on the mode selected.
The FD uses the Navigation source and data reference presented on
the selected PFD. The selected PFD is indicated by the green PFD
couple arrow which is controlled by the PFD button on the SAR
Guidance Controller (See Figure 2).
A green couple arrow is also presented on the side of the PFD
pushbutton on the Guidance Controller. When a FD mode is engaged
the coupled function is automatically engaged. The FD may be
uncoupled by pressing the CPL pushbutton on the Autopilot Controller
(See Figure 1). The coupled function is automatically forced to
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
uncoupled whenever the AP ATT mode is off or becomes inoperative.
Armed and captured FD modes are displayed with messages along
the top line of the PFD: Collective and pitch mode messages on the
left of the selected PFD arrow and lateral mode on the right. Armed
modes are in small white characters and captured or engaged modes
are in medium size green characters. When transitioning from no
mode to engaged, from armed to captured or change from one mode
to another mode the message flashes for 6 seconds then become
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S69-1
Rev. 31

SAR Modes (Phase 5 and later) 139G0290X002
steady. When changing from captured to no mode the message
flashes for 6 seconds then extinguishes.
Armed lateral modes messages are: VOR, VAPP, LOC, BC, LNAV
and captured VOR, VAPP, OS, LOC, BC, LNAV, HDG, HOV, WTR.
Armed collective modes are: GS, VGP, VRT (Phase 8 and later) and
captured ALT, GS, VS, GA, ALTA, ALVL, RHT, VGP, TD, TDH, TU, Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
VRHT, VPTH, PTH, VRT (Phase 8 and later).
Engaged vertical pitch modes are IAS, HOV, DCL, GA, TD, TDH, TU,
VIAS, WTR.
A chime sounds whenever either a lateral, vertical (pitch), or vertical
(collective) FD mode changes from its previous state, i.e.
— a mode changes from engaged to disengaged or vice-versa
— a mode changes from arm to captured
— a mode changes from coupled to uncoupled.
An aural tone (“bip-bip”) sounds for any change in altitude or radar
height mode reference datum.

SECTION 2 - NORMAL PROCEDURES
FLIGHT DIRECTOR - GENERAL
For full details of FD operation and use see “PRIMUS EPIC Integrated
Avionics and Flight Control System for the AW/AB139 Helicopter -
Pilot’s Guide” latest issue and FMS Pilot’s Guide latest issue.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR MODES ENGAGEMENT
The AFCS Flight Director function provides 4 axis guidance modes.
Selection of most FD modes is carried out using pushbuttons on the
Guidance Controller. HOV mode may also be engaged using the
th
cyclic beep trim centre position (5 position). Each mode may be de-
selected by pressing the associated pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller. However GA and TU modes may only be engaged by
either collective GA button and disengaged by engaging a different
mode for pitch and collective axis. All engaged modes may be
deselected simultaneously by using the FD STBY button located on
the cyclic sticks or the STBY button on the Guidance Controller.
The Guidance Controller pushbuttons include a green annuciator that
illuminates when the mode is selected. FD mode annuciations (green
when captured and white when armed) also appear on the PFD.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR COUPLED AND UNCOUPLED OPERATIONS
Selecting a FD mode by pressing the pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller will couple the FD whenever the AP is in ATT hold.
Selecting a FD mode by pressing the pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller with the ATT OFF (i.e. SAS or no stabilisation), the FD will
be engaged in the uncoupled mode.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
During coupled operation the FD may be uncoupled by pressing the
CPL pushbutton on the Autopilot Controller which will cause a white
UCPL caption to appear on the PFD.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S69-13
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2618 ===
Supplement 69 AW139 - RFM - 4D
4 Axis Enhanced FD with Document N°
SAR Modes (Phase 5 and later) 139G0290X002
CAUTION
• Whenever the FD is coupled and the AP reverts to SAS
or has a complete loss of autostabilization, the FD will
revert to uncoupled mode.
• When the AP reverts to SAS no UCPL caption will Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
appear on the PFD.
With the FD engaged, in coupled or uncoupled mode, the following is
displayed:
— Navigation source and reference data in magenta colour on the
selected PFD
— Navigation source and reference data in cyan colour on the non
selected PFD
— Navigation source in amber on both PFD’s when both PFD’s have
the same navigation data source.
During coupled operation the HDG, ALT, IAS, VS, ALTA, RHT, HOV,
TD, TDH, TU, MOT, VRT modes may be controlled by either pilot.
When engaged in coupled mode, the reference data may be adjusted
by using the Display Controller (HDG, ALT SEL), collective beep trim/
FTR (ALT, ALTA, VS, RHT, TD, TDH, TU, VRT) or cyclic beep trim/
FTR (IAS, HOV , HDG, TD, TDH,TU). See Mode Description for
details.
During uncoupled operation changes of reference data for IAS, HDG
and HOV modes are carried out by pressing the cyclic FTR button,
which updates the reference data to the actual values at the time the
button is released. Changes of reference data for ALT, VS and RHT
are carried out by the collective beep trim. Collective FTR does not
modify the collective modes reference.
For IAS, HDG, RHT and VS on the selected PFD, a magenta digital
readout reference datum is displayed above the appropriate flight
instrument and a magenta bug at a position corresponding to the
selected reference. For ALT, only the magenta bug is displayed
permanently while the digital readout is displayed for 5 seconds
whenever the reference is modified and the ALTA reference is
present.

Rev. 26

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 69
Document N ° 4 Axis Enhanced FD with
139G0290X002 SAR Modes (Phase 5 and later)
Whenever a collective mode is engaged a collective position cue
appears on the PFD beside the ADI. There are some collective FD
modes (e.g. RHT, VRT etc.) based upon RadAlt. When one of them is
engaged, a magenta bug is displayed on the RadAlt tape and the
radalt readout is displayed in magenta. See Figure 2-1 (S/W Phase 5,
6 & 7) and Figure 2-2 (S/W Phase 8 and later).
SAR OPERATIONS
— Satisfactory operation of the SAR modes has been demonstrated
up to 40 kts wind speed (20 kts tail wind) and wave heights up to
5.5 m (18 ft).
— Before performing a MOT pattern, confirm that the FMS PERF
INIT function on the MCDU has been initialized.
— When performing a MOT, both PFD barometric altimeters should
be set to the same baro-altimeter setting.
COLLECTIVE PI LIMITING FUNCTION
During collective coupled operation the collective movement is limited
by the following PI values:
— Maximum 97% AEO (95% at altitudes above 10000 ft (3050 m) Hp)
— Maximum 106% AEO for airspeed less than 60 KIAS (5 MIN
message displayed beside collective cue, see Figure 2-1)
— Maximum 140% OEI
— Minimum 5% AEO
— Minimum 10% OEI.
When PI limiting function is active and is limiting maximum collective
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
movement, an amber LIM caption is displayed beside the collective
cue. See Figure 2-1.
If PI limiting is active with IAS engaged and the required reference for
VS, ALTA, RHT, GA, or ALT cannot be achieved the airspeed will
automatically reduce as necessary to achieve the collective mode
reference. If the collective mode reference cannot be maintained,
when the airspeed has reached a minimum of 80 KIAS this airspeed
will be maintained and the collective mode reference will be reduced.

SAFETY FLY-UP FUNCTIONALITY WHEN FD MODES ENGAGED
The Fly-Up Collective Safety Function is a height protection function
which is always active when at least one Rad Alt is valid. The function
is activated when any collective FD mode is engaged and coupled and
the Safety Height is passed. When the function is activated the aircraft
is automatically flown back up to the Safety Height. The Safety Height
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
is a function of the Rad Alt Reference (or a fixed height for Barometric
modes) and depends on the actual collective mode engaged.
Further to the Safety Height there is also an Ultimate Fly-Up Limit, a
fixed height (not adjustable) which, if passed, will automatically cause
the aircraft to fly back up to this height or the Safety Height, if higher.
The following table gives the Safety Height Rad Alt limits and Ultimate
Fly-Up Limit for the different collective modes:

When the collective Fly Up safety function is activated, due to an
height excursion below the Safety Height or Ultimate Fly-Up limit, the
aural message ‘ALTITUDE ALTITUDE’ is triggered and a HTLM
message is displayed on the PFD on the top left of the attitude
indicator. When the collective is automatically driven up, it is normally
limited by the PI limiting function. Should the relevant MUH limits be
exceeded the PI limits will be moved up as follows:
— Maximum 121% AEO for airspeeds below 60 KIAS
— Maximum 176% OEI for airspeeds below 60 KIAS
— Maximum 110% AEO for airspeeds above 60 KIAS
— Maximum 160% OEI for airspeeds above 60 KIAS.
The aural ‘ALTITUDE ALTITUDE’ and HTLM message will also be
generated if flying uncoupled.
CAUTION
When voice message “Altitude Altitude” is triggered with
a HTLM message then the aircraft has descended
below the safety height. Ensure separation from terrain
visually or, if not possible, establish a positive rate of
climb to a safe height.
CAUTION
(Applicable only for Phase 5 or 6)
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
When descending over terrain, with a collective mode
engaged and after a continuous descent of at least
2500 ft, at approximately 2500 ft Rad Alt height, the Fly
Up safety function may erroneously intervene and
increase the PI to above the MCP level. This condition
should be controlled manually with the collective to
maintain the PI within the MCP limits until the HTLM
message on the PFD extinguishes.

MODE DESCRIPTIONS
The following descriptions assume the modes are coupled, unless
stated otherwise.
HDG Heading Hold Mode. This mode steers the aircraft to the
heading reference bug displayed on the PFD. The
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
heading bug can be adjusted using the HEADING knob
on the Remote Instrument Controller and can be
syncronized with the actual heading by pressing the
HEADING knob (PUSH SYNC). The heading reference
bug can be syncronized to the actual heading by
pressing the cyclic FTR button or modified using the
cyclic beep trim switch left or right. In HDG mode turns
are performed at standard rate 1 (3 deg/sec).
ALT Barometric Altitude Hold Mode. This mode maintains the
barometric altitude existing at the time of engagement.
The altitude reference is displayed as a set bug on the
PFD altitude tape. If the ALT SEL knob has not been
previously moved (ie. no ALTA activation) the ALT
reference will also be displayed as a magenta digital
readout. The altitude reference can be adjusted using the
collective beep trim (aft to increase altitude) or by
pressing FTR button, flying to desired altitude, and
releasing. An audio tone is produced when the altitude
reference is changed. The collective PI limiting function is
enabled when ALT mode is coupled.
CAUTION
In ALT mode the voice message “Altitude Altitude” is
triggered when altitude exceeds the reference altitude by
±150 ft (46 m) .
Note
ALT mode can be engaged with HOV mode (as an
alternative to the RHT mode).
Page S69-20 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2625 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 69
Document N ° 4 Axis Enhanced FD with
139G0290X002 SAR Modes (Phase 5 and later)
IAS Airspeed Hold Mode. This mode maintains the airspeed
existing at the time of engagement. When engaged the
airspeed reference is displayed as a set bug and a digital
readout on the PFD. The airspeed reference bug is
adjusted by either using the cyclic beep fore/aft or
repositioning the cyclic, with the FTR button depressed,
to the required airspeed and releasing FTR button. The
airspeed reference is adjustable via the cyclic beep
switch between 50 KIAS (60 KIAS for Phase 5 and 6)
and Vne less 5 KIAS. If airspeed, at time of engagement,
is higher than Vne less 5 KIAS then it is automatically
reduced to Vne less 5 KIAS.
ALTA Altitude Acquire Mode. This mode, when engaged with
a barometric altitude preselect reference set (through
ALT SEL knob), will automatically engage the IAS mode
and the aircraft is flown towards the preset altitude. The
final altitude reference is displayed as a cyan bug and
digital readout above the altitude scale. The vertical
speed reference is displayed as a bug and digital readout
on the PFD. The preset vertical speeds are +1000 fpm or
-750 fpm in the direction of the preset altitude. The
vertical speed reference can be changed by either using
the collective beep trim (aft to increase) or with collective
FTR button depressed, moving to the required vertical
speed and releasing. When the preset altitude is
achieved the mode will transition to ALT mode and the
IAS mode will remain engaged. The collective PI limiting
function is enabled when ALTA mode is coupled. When
collective PI limiting is active the airspeed is reduced to
maintain vertical speed reference.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Note
(Applicable only for Phase 5 or 6)
Engaging ALTA while climbing with a rate of climb greater
than 1500 fpm or descending with a rate of descent
greater than 1500 fpm, the system may erroneously
transition to ALT. The aircraft will, however, reach the
selected final altitude.

NAV VOR/LOC/LNAV FD functions. These functions are

APP 1) VOR/ILS Approach FD functions. The VOR non-precision

vertical deviation between current aircraft barometric
altitude and FMS glidepath. The glide path is anchored at

FMS glide path, but alter the height at which the aircraft
will level - off after VRT mode transitions to RHT
mode.The VRT mode is armed (white caption) by pushing
the APP or DCL button, while below 2400 ft AGL.
Intercepting the projected glidepath, the VRT mode is
automatically captured. Flying above 2500 ft AGL will
result in VRT mode disarming or disengagement.

PRV The PRV mode is a way to preselect ILS or VOR
approach functions while FD is still engaged in LNAV.
PRV is selected by pressing the PRV pushbutton on the
Display Controller. If the APP pushbutton is pressed the
FD will arm LOC and GS or VAPP functions depending

FD disengages LNAV and engages LOC-GS or VAPP
functions. Selected PRV course will be displayed as thin
cyan, while armed, and as normal magenta when
captured.
DCL 1) ILS Deceleration Mode. The deceleration mode
decreases the aircraft speed from its present speed down
to approximately 80 KIAS at a height not below 200 ft
AGL. When the DCL pushbutton is pushed the LOC, GS
and DCL modes are armed and the IAS and HDG modes
are engaged. After GS capture and at a computed
condition for correct approach and deceleration the IAS
mode is disengaged and the DCL mode engaged. The
airspeed reference bug moves to 80 KIAS and the digital
reference is set to 80 KIAS. These values can be
adjusted using the cyclic beep trim at which time the IAS
mode automatically engages replacing the DCL mode.
2) VGP/VRT Deceleration Mode.
When the DCL pushbutton is pushed, during a VGP or
VRT approach, if the present speed is greater than the
FMS target speed (Ref MCDU PERF INIT page 2/3) the
DCL mode engages and the aircraft decelerates to the
FMS target speed. If, however, the speed is less or equal
to the FMS target speed, the DCL mode arms.
At the Initial Distance the DCL mode, if not already
engaged, engages and the aircraft starts to decelerate to
the initial speed. At the appropriate distance the aircraft
will start to decelerate to achieve the final speed at the
final distance from the MAP. For Phase 5 and 6 only the
DCL mode must be engaged within 10 NM from the
missed approach point. The initial and final speed targets
and distances are provided and can be modified in:

GA 1) Go Around Mode. The mode may be selected from either
collective GA pushbutton and will give, when the

or 70 KIAS (80 KIAS for Phase 5 and 6), whichever is

2) Transition Up Mode. The mode may be selected from
either collective GA pushbutton and will give, when the
conditions for a TU are met i.e. airspeed less than
41 KIAS (60 KIAS for Phase 5 and 6) or one of the

aircraft then accelerates to the airspeed reference of
80 KIAS and the IAS mode is engaged. The reference
height can be modified by the collective beep switch and
the airspeed by the cyclic beep switch. The TU Mode can
be exited by selecting another vertical FD mode (or FD to
STBY).

RHT Radar Height Hold Mode. This mode maintains the
aircraft at the radar height at the time of engagement
when the radar altimeter indications are within the
threshold limits. A reference bug on the radar altimeter
tape and a digital readout above the radar altimeter tape
are presented. The reference height can be changed by
depressing the collective FTR switch flying to the Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
required height and releasing the FTR switch or by using
the collective beep trim switch (aft to increase). An audio
tone is produced when the height reference is changed.
The collective PI limiting function is enabled when RHT
mode is coupled.
HOV Hover/velocity Hold Mode. HOV mode can be engaged
by pressing HOV mode on Guidance Controller or the
th
cyclic beep trim centre position (5 position). The HOV
mode utilizes the AHRS ground velocities to maintain
hover or low speed flying. At engagement of this mode
the helicopter groundspeed reference is set to zero and
the RHT is automatically engaged if a valid radar
altimeter signal is available and within the threshold
limits. RHT mode can be subsequently disengaged
independently and replaced by ALT if required. A hover
symbology with the ground velocity vector bug is also
displayed on the HSI. See Figure 2-4. When the mode is
engaged, the velocity vector reference can be changed
by pressing the cyclic FTR switch, flying to the desired
lateral and longitudinal speed and releasing, or by using
the cyclic beep trim to move the bug to the desired
velocities. If the cyclic beep trim switch is pressed in the
th
centre position (5 position) the longitudinal and lateral
velocity references are set to zero.
CAUTION
The HOV mode maintains a groundspeed reference
therefore pilot must ensure that crosswind and rearwind
speed limits are not exceeded (see Section 1 Basic Flight
Manual). If wind limits are exceeded directional control
may not be maintained.

a position 150 ft (46 m) to the left and 150 ft (46 m)
downwind of the marked waypoint.
The MOT sequence is divided in three basic phases:
- Approach to FHAF ((Final Hover Approach Fix)
First phase after MOT engagement, during which the
aircraft, following FMS commands, will be headed into
the wind at the FHAF.
FHAF is a point located approximately 0.8 nautical
miles (1.5 km) downwind from the target waypoint.
Aircraft height at FHAF is approximately 250 ft AGL,
with a target speed of 60 kt GS.
- Approach to Final Hover Fix
Second phase, to acquire the hover waypoint from
FHAF, aircraft will descend following a 3 degree slope
vertical path.
- Approach to Final Target
Final phase, with pilot taking the aircraft from hover
waypoint to the target location.
During the approach to hover:
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters - The final hover reference height can be modified by the
collective beep switch. After Final Hover Approach Fix
(FHAF) pressing the collective FTR button the final
hover height synchronizes to the actual height with
RHT engagement.
- After the FHAF the reference groundspeed can be
modified laterally and longitudinally by pressing the
cyclic FTR button to synchronize to the actual ground-
speed and to engage HOV.

During the sequence of manoeuvres the collective mode
VRHT message indicates the level flight phase to
intercept the vertical path, if required, when the aircraft
starts to descend. The message changes to VPTH when
on the 3° slope to the FHAF. The message changes to
PTH for the last portion of the descent after the FHAF. If
the aircraft is flying above the 3° slope at MOT
engagement the collective axis will directly engage the
VPTH. On the pitch axis the message VIAS appears
anytime before the FHAF, indicating the aircraft is
reducing the IAS, if necessary, to obtain 60 kts
groundspeed at the FHAF. At the FHAF the message
changes to DCL indicating the aircraft is decelerating
from 60 kts groundspeed to 0 kts groundspeed.
A vertical path indicator, in magenta, is presented on the
PFD to the right of the GS deviation scale (See
Figure 2-5). This pointer is centered when the aircraft is
following the 3° path to the hover point.
Roll mode LNAV will be presented on the PFD.
Note

audio message ‘LANDING GEAR’ is inhibited.

FMS FUNCTIONAL INCONSISTENCIES ONLY FOR EPIC
SOFTWARE PHASE 5 OR PHASE 6 INSTALLED
1. When the destination runway/helipad is changed, without an
arrival or approach entered, and the runway/helipad is the TO
waypoint, the FMS incorrectly places the runway/helipad behind
the helicopter, shows it as the FROM waypoint, disengages LNAV
(if engaged) and the deviation bar is shown as INVALID.

• Select desired runway/helipad and activate
• Re-engage LNAV mode.

further information.
Problem not present for software version EB7030191-00109
(Phase 6.5)

phase of flight.

geommetry of consecutive AT altitude constraints exhibit TOD
misplacement and premature descent.
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201010000078 for

indications during glide path capture and execute a missed

SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER
GENERAL
The height loss during a single engine failure flyaway from hover for
combinations of weight, altitude and temperature conditions is shown
in Figure 4-1 for weights up to 6400 kg and Figure 4-2 for aircraft
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
configured for operation between 6400 kg and 6800 kg (See
Supplement 50). The chart does not include any ground clearance
height. If the hover height is greater than the height loss plus the
ground clearance height required (15 ft (5 m) minimum) then a flyaway
capability exists and the Flyaway Procedure should be followed. The
height loss is valid provided the flyaway manoeuvre is initiated within 1
second from engine failure recognition.
If a flyaway capability does not exist the landing/ditching procedure
should be followed.
Note
If the helicopter weight, at the time of engine failure, is
less or equal to the Hover OGE 2.5 min OEI weight, an
engine failure in the hover will result in no height loss
provided that the pilot does not intervene on the flight
controls.
FLYAWAY PROCEDURE
1. Collective/Cyclic control — Rotate nose down in 1 second to
an attitude of -20°. Recover pitch
attitude to 5° nose up in
approximately 5 seconds.
Maintain this attitude while using
the collective to droop the NR to a
minimum of 90% NR, if
necessary, to arrest the descent.
2. Acceleration — Maintain pitch attitude at 5° nose
up and accelerate to V TOSS
(40 KIAS).
Page S69-38 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2643 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 69
Document N ° 4 Axis Enhanced FD with
139G0290X002 SAR Modes (Phase 5 and later)
3. Climb — When the aircraft has achieved
V TOSS (40 KIAS) and a positive
rate of climb lower collective to
recover initial hover NR to
continue climb.
LANDING/DITCHING PROCEDURE
1. Collective/Cyclic control — Rotate nose down in 1 second
to an attitude of no more than
-20° while decreasing
collective to maintain NR at
100%.
Note
The nose down rotation should be commensurate with
hover height. An engine failure at low height will not allow
a large pitch attitude change prior to water/ground
impact. Engine failures at higher hover heights will permit
greater pitch attitude change to gain airspeed energy that
is subsequently used during the flare.
2. Cyclic — At 50 ft (15 m) AGL rotate nose
up as necessary (maximum
20°) to decelerate.
3. Approach/ Touchdown — Continue deceleration to attain
landing attitude (level or 5°
nose up) prior to touchdown or
ditching at the slowest forward
speed possible. Use collective
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
to cushion touchdown.
4. Landing/Ditching — After touchdown, centralize
cyclic and simultaneously
reduce collective to MPOG.
Apply brakes as required for
ground landing or initiate the
Ditching Procedure described
in Supplement 9.

CYCLIC FORCE TRIM RELEASE FAILURE
Cyclic FTR button failure, due to a fault which removes electric power
to the clutches of the longitudinal and lateral trim, will result in cyclic
longitudinal and lateral clutches becoming permanently engaged. This
will require the pilot to fly the aircraft against the cyclic force spring feel
to manoeuvre the aircraft, or use the cyclic beep trim, as cyclic FTR
button does not function.
In this case it is suggested that a cyclic FD mode (i.e. IAS) is engaged
and the cyclic beep trim used to maintain the required flight condition.
Coupled SAR mode operations are not affected.
COLLECTIVE FORCE TRIM OFF OR FAIL
When a FD mode is engaged, and coupled, and the collective trim is
switched OFF (Miscellaneous Control Panel) or fails, a chime sound is
generated, the collective may not maintain its selected position, the
CLTV annuciation will illuminate on the top left of the ADI display, and
the CLTV/YAW OFF green advisory will illuminate on the CAS window.
Collective modes are available uncoupled only.
COLLECTIVE FORCE TRIM RELEASE FAILURE
Collective force trim release failure, due to a fault which removes
electric power to the clutch of the collective trim will result in the
collective clutch becoming permanently engaged. This will require the
pilot to fly the aircraft against the collective force spring feel to
manoeuvre the aircraft, or use the collective beep trim, as the
collective FTR button does not function.
In this case when large collective movements are not required, it is
suggested that a collective FD mode (i.e. ALT) is engaged and the
collective beep trim used to maintain the required flight condition.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters Coupled SAR mode operations are not affected.
