SECTION 4 - PERFORMANCE DATA
HOVER CEILING OGE
For Hover Ceiling OGE OEI MCP and 2.5 min refer to Section 4 Basic
Manual or appropriate Supplement for aircraft configuration.
FLYAWAY PERFORMANCE
The Flyaway chart defines the height loss which will occur during a
flyaway manoeuvre from the hover condition to level flight after a
single engine failure in a zero wind hover. The height loss is given for
varying combinations of weight, initial hover Pressure Altitude, OAT
and the main rotor speed at 100%NR or 102%. The chart does not
include any clearance height which must be added (minimum 15 ft) to
the height loss.
The height loss is valid provided the flyaway manoeuvre is initiated
within 1 second from engine failure recognition.
See Basic RFM Section 4 PERFORMANCE DATA for details of
procedures.
Note
Following the flyaway procedure the height loss indicated
on chart Figure 4-1 and Figure 4-2, for ambient condition
and aircraft weight, guarantees that V TOSS (40 KIAS) will
be achieved and, after accelerating to V y a subsequent
minimum Rate Of Climb of 150 fpm is assured.
Note
If the helicopter weight, at the time of engine failure, is
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters less or equal to the Hover OGE 2.5 min OEI weight, an
engine failure in the hover will result in no height loss
provided that the pilot does not intervene on the flight
controls.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The 4 Axis Basic Flight Director (FD) provides commands that are
normally coupled to the autopilot (AP) for automatic flight path control
around the three axes of the aircraft plus collective. At Power Up one
of the two FD is automatically selected and configured as Master
(priority). At every Power Up the FD selected as Master (priority) is
alternated.
The 4 Axis Basic Flight Director system is a simplified version of the
4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director system (Supplement 67) as it does
not include Hover Mode (HOV) or TU modes. The system requires
Phase 5 (software release EB7030191-00107) or Phase 6 (software
release EB7030191-00108 & 109) or Phase 7 (software release
EB7030191-00110/00111/00112/00114/00115/00117/00118) or Phase
8 (software release EB7030191-00113/00120).
When coupled, both autopilots drive the actuators to satisfy the
references provided by the priority FD.
When uncoupled the pilot can manually fly the commands.
In either case, pitch, roll command bars/collective cue are presented
on each PFD, depending on the mode selected.
The FD uses the Navigation source and data reference presented on
the selected PFD. The selected PFD is indicated by the green PFD
couple arrow which is controlled by the PFD button on the Guidance
Controller (See Figure 2). The SAR Guidance Controller (See Figure
3) is an alternative controller and has SAR mode buttons, however,
the extra pushbuttons are not active. Either Guidance Controller can
be used with the 4 Axis Enhanced Flight Director system Phase 5,6,7
& 8. (For Phase 5 and later installations that includes SAR mode
functions see Supplement 69).
A green couple arrow is also presented on the side of the PFD
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
pushbutton on the Guidance Controller. When a FD mode is engaged
the coupled function is automatically engaged. The FD may be
uncoupled by pressing the CPL pushbutton on the Autopilot Controller
(See Figure 1). The coupled function is automatically forced to
uncoupled whenever the AP ATT mode is off or becomes inoperative.
Armed and captured FD modes are displayed with messages along
the top line of the PFD: Collective and pitch mode messages on the
left of the selected PFD arrow and lateral mode on the right. Armed
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S70-1
Rev. 31

modes are in small white characters and captured or engaged modes
are in medium size green characters. When transitioning from no
mode to engaged, from armed to captured or change from one mode
to another mode the message flashes for 6 seconds then become
steady. When changing from captured to no mode the message
flashes for 6 seconds then extinguishes.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Armed lateral modes messages are: VOR, VAPP, LOC, BC, LNAV
and captured VOR, VAPP, OS, LOC, BC, LNAV, HDG.
Armed collective modes are: GS, VGP, VRT (Phase 8 and later) and
captured ALT, GS, VS, GA, ALTA, ALVL, RHT, VGP, VRT (Phase 8
and later).
Engaged vertical pitch modes are IAS, DCL, GA.
A chime sounds whenever either a lateral, vertical (pitch), or vertical
(collective) FD mode changes from its previous state, i.e.
— a mode changes from engaged to disengaged or vice-versa
— a mode changes from arm to captured
— a mode changes from coupled to uncoupled.
An aural tone (“bip-bip”) sounds for any change in altitude or radar
height mode reference datum.

SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
WEIGHT LIMITATIONS
— For weights up to 6400 kg see basic RFM.
— For weights between 6400 kg and 6800 kg see Supplement 50.
— For weights between 6800 kg and 7000 kg see Supplement 90.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR MODES LIMITATIONS
• The following FD modes are inoperative on the SAR Guidance
Control panel:
— TD/H — MOT — WTR — VNAV
• Collective modes must not be engaged if either or both engines are
in MANUAL MODE.
• The RHT mode can only be engaged over flat surfaces which are
clear of obstacles.
• The HOV mode is not available.

SECTION 2 - NORMAL PROCEDURES
FLIGHT DIRECTOR - GENERAL
For full details of FD operation and use see “PRIMUS EPIC Integrated
Avionics and Flight Control System for the AW/AB139 Helicopter -
Pilot’s Guide” latest issue and FMS Pilot’s Guide latest issue.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR MODES ENGAGEMENT
The AFCS Flight Director function provides 4 axis guidance modes.
Selection of most FD modes is carried out using pushbuttons on the
Guidance Controller. Each mode may be de-selected by pressing the
associated pushbutton on the Guidance Controller. However GA
mode may only be engaged by either collective GA button and disen-
gaged by engaging a different mode for pitch and collective axis. All
engaged modes may be deselected simultaneously by using the FD
STBY button located on the cyclic sticks or the STBY button on the
Guidance Controller.
The Guidance Controller pushbuttons include a green annuciator that
illuminates when the mode is selected. FD mode annuciations (green
when captured and white when armed) also appear on the PFD.
FLIGHT DIRECTOR COUPLED AND UNCOUPLED OPERATIONS
Selecting a FD mode by pressing the pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller will couple the FD whenever the AP is in ATT hold.
Selecting a FD mode by pressing the pushbutton on the Guidance
Controller with the ATT OFF (i.e. SAS or no stabilisation), the FD will
be engaged in the uncoupled mode.
During coupled operation the FD may be uncoupled by pressing the
CPL pushbutton on the Autopilot Controller which will cause a white
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters UCPL caption to appear on the PFD.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S70-11
Rev. 26

COLLECTIVE PI LIMITING FUNCTION
During collective coupled operation the collective movement is limited
by the following PI values:
— Maximum 97% AEO (95% at altitudes above 10000 ft (3050 m) Hp)
— Maximum 106% AEO for airspeed less than 60 KIAS (5 MIN
message displayed beside collective cue, see Figure 2-1)
— Maximum 140% OEI
— Minimum 5% AEO
— Minimum 10% OEI.
When PI limiting function is active and is limiting maximum collective
movement, an amber LIM caption is displayed beside the collective
cue. See Figure 2-1.
If PI limiting is active with IAS engaged and the required reference for
VS, ALTA, RHT, GA, or ALT cannot be achieved the airspeed will
automatically reduce as necessary to achieve the collective mode
reference. If the collective mode reference cannot be maintained,
when the airspeed has reached a minimum of 80 KIAS this airspeed
will be maintained and the collective mode reference will be reduced.
While the mode reference values cannot be maintained or achieved
that mode caption is displayed in amber on the PFD.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

If PI limiting is active with ALT/RHT engaged and the
reference height cannot be maintained the aural warning
“Altitude Altitude” will warn the pilot when the maximum
allowed deviation from the reference height has been
exceeded.

SAFETY FLY-UP FUNCTIONALITY WHEN FD MODES ENGAGED
The Fly-Up Collective Safety Function is a height protection function
which is always active when at least one Rad Alt is valid. The function
is activated when any collective FD mode is engaged and coupled and
the Safety Height is passed. When the function is activated the aircraft
is automatically flown back up to the Safety Height. The Safety Height
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
is a function of the Rad Alt Reference (or a fixed height for Barometric
modes) and depends on the actual collective mode engaged.
Further to the Safety Height there is also an Ultimate Fly-Up Limit, a
fixed height (not adjustable) which, if passed, will automatically cause
the aircraft to fly back up to this height or the Safety Height, if higher.
The following table gives the Safety Height Rad Alt limits and Ultimate
Fly-Up Limit for the different collective modes:

When the collective Fly Up safety function is activated, due to an
height excursion below the Safety Height or Ultimate Fly-Up limit, the
aural message ‘ALTITUDE ALTITUDE’ is triggered and a HTLM
message is displayed on the PFD on the top left of the attitude indica-
tor. When the collective is automatically driven up, it is normally limited
by the PI limiting function. Should the relevant MUH limits be
exceeded the PI limits will be moved up as follows:
— Maximum 121% AEO for airspeeds below 60 KIAS
— Maximum 176% OEI for airspeeds below 60 KIAS
— Maximum 110% AEO for airspeeds above 60 KIAS
— Maximum 160% OEI for airspeeds above 60 KIAS.
CAUTION
When voice message “Altitude Altitude” is triggered with
a HTLM message then the aircraft has descended
below the safety height. Ensure separation from terrain
visually or, if not possible, establish a positive rate of
climb to a safe height.
CAUTION
(Applicable only for Phase 5 or 6)
When descending over terrain, with a collective mode
engaged and after a continuous descent of at least
2500 ft, at approximately 2500 ft Rad Alt height, the Fly
Up safety function may erroneously intervene and
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
increase the PI to above the MCP level. This condition
should be controlled manually with the collective to
maintain the PI within the MCP limits until the HTLM
message on the PFD extinguishes.

MODE DESCRIPTIONS
The following descriptions assume the modes are coupled, unless
stated otherwise.
HDG Heading Hold Mode. This mode steers the aircraft to the
heading reference bug displayed on the PFD. The
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
heading bug can be adjusted using the HEADING knob
on the Remote Instrument Controller and can be
synchronized with the actual heading by pressing the
HEADING knob (PUSH SYNC). The heading reference
bug can be synchronized to the actual heading by
pressing the cyclic FTR button or modified using the
cyclic beep trim switch left or right. In HDG mode turns
are performed at standard rate 1 (3 deg/sec).
ALT Barometric Altitude Hold Mode. This mode maintains the
barometric altitude existing at the time of engagement.
The altitude reference is displayed as a set bug on the
PFD altitude tape. If the ALT SEL knob has not been
previously moved (i.e. no ALTA activation) the ALT
reference will also be displayed as a magenta digital
readout. The altitude reference can be adjusted using the
collective beep trim (aft to increase altitude) or by
pressing FTR button, flying to desired altitude, and
releasing. An audio tone is produced when the altitude
reference is changed. The collective PI limiting function is
enabled when ALT mode is coupled.
CAUTION
In ALT mode the voice message “Altitude Altitude” is
triggered when altitude exceeds the reference altitude by
±150 ft (46 m) .
IAS Airspeed Hold Mode. This mode maintains the airspeed
existing at the time of engagement. When engaged the
airspeed reference is displayed as a set bug and a digital
readout on the PFD. The airspeed reference bug is
adjusted by either using the cyclic beep fore/aft or
Page S70-18 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2697 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 70
Document N ° 4 Axis Basic Flight
139G0290X002 Director (Phase 5 and later)
repositioning the cyclic, with the FTR button depressed,
to the required airspeed and releasing FTR button. The
airspeed reference is adjustable via the cyclic beep
switch between 50 KIAS (60 KIAS for Phase 5 and 6)
and Vne less 5 KIAS. If airspeed, at time of engagement,
is higher than Vne less 5 KIAS then it is automatically
reduced to Vne less 5 KIAS.
ALTA Altitude Acquire Mode. This mode, when engaged with
a barometric altitude preselect reference set (through
ALT SEL knob), will automatically engage the IAS mode
and the aircraft is flown towards the preset altitude. The
final altitude reference is displayed as a cyan bug and
digital readout above the altitude scale. The vertical
speed reference is displayed as a bug and digital readout
on the PFD. The preset vertical speeds are +1000 fpm or
-750 fpm in the direction of the preset altitude. The
vertical speed reference can be changed by either using
the collective beep trim (aft to increase) or with collective
FTR button depressed, moving to the required vertical
speed and releasing. When the preset altitude is
achieved the mode will transition to ALT mode and the
IAS mode will remain engaged. The collective PI limiting
function is enabled when ALTA mode is coupled. When
collective PI limiting is active the airspeed is reduced to
maintain vertical speed reference.
Note
(Applicable only for Phase 5 or 6)
Engaging ALTA while climbing with a rate of climb greater
than 1500 fpm or descending with a rate of descent
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters greater than 1500 fpm, the system may erroneously
transition to ALT. The aircraft will, however, reach the
selected final altitude.

Final Level Segment (Phase 8 and later) is loaded into the
flight plan.
The mode produces a vertical guidance based upon the
vertical deviation between current aircraft barometric
altitude and FMS glidepath. The glide path is anchored at
the Bottom of Descent (BOD) with the glide path angle
stored in the data base at the corresponding waypoint or,

3) FMS approach for Custom Approach with Level Segment
(VRT).
This can be used when the FMS is the selected NAV
source on the selected PFD and a Custom Approach with
a Final Level Segment (Phase 8 only) is loaded into the
flight plan. The mode produces a vertical guidance based
upon the vertical deviation between current aircraft
barometric altitude and FMS glidepath. The glide path is
anchored at the Bottom of Descent (BOD) with 4 degree
slope. The VRT mode will automatically transition to RHT
mode at BOD sequencing or approaching the final height
reference selected by the pilot during approach settings,
whichever occurs first. The RHT reference can be
changed by using the collective beep trim switch (aft to
increase). Changing the RHT reference will not alter the
FMS glide path, but alter the height at which the aircraft
will level - off after VRT mode transitions to RHT
mode.The VRT mode is armed (white caption) by pushing
the APP or DCL button, while below 2400 ft AGL.
Intercepting the projected glidepath, the VRT mode is
automatically captured.Flying above 2500 ft AGL will
result in VRT mode disarming or disengagement.
In either case (ILS, VGP, VRT) within the vertical deviation
bug there will be a letter: I for ILS, P for VGP or VRT and
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
V for Vertical Path. See Figure 2-1. The P letter and bug,
when VGP or VRT is armed, appears on the left hand side
of vertical deviation scale in cyan. When captured the
symbol moves to the right hand side of the vertical
deviation scale in magenta.

PRV The PRV mode is a way to preselect ILS or VOR Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
approach functions while FD is still engaged in LNAV.
PRV is selected by pressing the PRV pushbutton on the
Display Controller. If the APP pushbutton is pressed the
FD will arm LOC and GS or VAPP functions depending
on the NAV receiver tuning (ILS or VOR) on the selected
PFD. At the capture of the LOC or VAPP functions the
FD disengages LNAV and engages LOC-GS or VAPP
functions. Selected PRV course will be displayed as thin
cyan, while armed, and as normal magenta when
captured.
DCL 1) ILS Deceleration Mode. The deceleration mode
decreases the aircraft speed from its present speed down
to approximately 80 KIAS as the aircraft reaches 200 ft
AGL. When the DCL pushbutton is pushed the LOC, GS
and DCL modes are armed and the IAS and HDG modes
are engaged. After GS capture and at a computed
condition for correct approach and deceleration the IAS
mode is disengaged and the DCL mode engaged. The
airspeed reference bug moves to 80 KIAS and the digital
reference is set to 80 KIAS. These values can be
adjusted using the cyclic beep trim at which time the IAS
mode automatically engages replacing the DCL mode.
2) VGP/VRT Deceleration Mode.
When the DCL pushbutton is pushed, during a VGP or
VRT approach, if the present speed is greater than the
FMS target speed (Ref MCDU PERF INIT page 2/3) the
DCL mode engages and the aircraft decelerates to the
FMS target speed. If, however, the speed is less or equal
to the FMS target speed, the DCL mode arms.
At the Initial Distance the DCL mode, if not already
engaged, engages and the aircraft starts to decelerate to

VS Vertical Speed Hold Mode. The vertical speed existing at
the time of engagement is held. Vertical speed reference
bug and digital readout are adjusted by either using the
collective beep or repositioning the collective, with the
FTR button depressed, to the required vertical speed and
releasing on the desired vertical speed. Collective PI
limiting function is enabled when VS mode is coupled. Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
GA Go Around Mode. The mode may be selected from either
collective GA pushbutton and will give, when the
conditions for a GA are met i.e. airspeed greater than
41 KIAS (60 KIAS for Phase 5 and 6), a 1000 ft/min climb
set bug reference on the Vertical Speed tape and an
airspeed bug at the airspeed existing when the mode is

OS Over Station Mode. When overflying a VOR station, with
VOR or VAPP FD functions engaged, the VOR equipment
detects the aircraft being within the zone of ambiguity.
The VOR deviation signal is removed from the command
until the VOR signal has stabilized after passing over
station. While over the station, course change may be
made by selecting a new course via the Course Selector
knob.
ALVL Autolevel Mode. If the APP (LOC/GS or VGP) mode is
continued, to below landing minimum, this safety feature
is automatically activated at 150 ft (46 m) and an
asymptotic flare to a radar height of 50 ft (15 m) will be
initiated. The green GS or VGP caption on the PFD will
be replaced by ALVL.

CAUTION
In VGP mode the ALVL will activate if the MAP (Missed

RHT Radar Height Hold Mode. This mode maintains the
aircraft at the radar height at the time of engagement
when the radar altimeter indications are within the
threshold limits. A reference bug on the radar altimeter
tape and a digital readout above the radar altimeter tape
are presented. The reference height can be changed by
depressing the collective FTR switch flying to the required
height and releasing the FTR switch or by using the
collective beep trim switch (aft to increase). An audio tone
is produced when the height reference is changed. The
collective PI limiting function is enabled when RHT mode
is coupled.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
CAUTION
In RHT mode the voice message “Altitude Altitude” is
triggered when height exceeds the reference by a value
proportional to the reference height.

FMS FUNCTIONAL INCONSISTENCIES ONLY FOR EPIC
SOFTWARE PHASE 5 OR PHASE 6 INSTALLED
1. When the destination runway/helipad is changed, without an
arrival or approach entered, and the runway/helipad is the TO
waypoint, the FMS incorrectly places the runway/helipad behind
the helicopter, shows it as the FROM waypoint, disengages LNAV Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
(if engaged) and the deviation bar is shown as INVALID.
Recommended corrective action if problem scenario encountered:
• Perform ‘Direct To’ to destination runway/helideck
• Select desired runway/helipad and activate
• Re-engage LNAV mode
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201002000030 for
further information.
Problem not present for software version EB7030191-00109
(Phase 6.5)
2. The ‘Direct-To Recovery’ procedure should not be used in any
phase of flight.
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201001000021 for
further information.
3. Approach and/or Star procedures which contain a certain
geometry of consecutive AT altitude constraints exhibit a TOD
misplacement and premature descent.
Refer to Honeywell Service Information Letter D201010000078 for
further information.
Problem not present for software version EB7030191-00109
(Phase 6.5)
4. Software version EB7030191-00109 (Phase 6.5) only, Activating
vectors during an FMS approach may result in below-glide path
VGP indications at the FAF. The crew should monitor VGP
indications during glide path capture and execute a missed
approach if VGP indications are not consistent with normal glide
path capture.”

CYCLIC FORCE TRIM RELEASE FAILURE
Cyclic FTR failure, due to a fault which removes electric power to the
clutches of the longitudinal and lateral trim, will result in cyclic
longitudinal and lateral clutches becoming permanently engaged. This
will require the pilot to fly the aircraft against the cyclic force spring feel
to manoeuvre the aircraft, or use the cyclic beep trim, as cyclic FTR
button does not function.
In this case it is suggested that a cyclic FD mode (i.e. IAS) is engaged
and the cyclic beep trim used to maintain the required flight condition.
COLLECTIVE FORCE TRIM OFF OR FAIL
When a FD mode is engaged, and coupled, and the collective trim is
switched OFF (Miscellaneous Control Panel) or fails, a chime sound is
generated, the collective may not maintain its selected position, the
CLTV annunciation will illuminate on the top left of the ADI display, and
the CLTV/YAW OFF green advisory will illuminate on the CAS window.
Collective modes are available uncoupled only.
COLLECTIVE FORCE TRIM RELEASE FAILURE
Collective force trim release failure, due to a fault which removes
electric power to the clutch of the collective trim will result in the
collective clutch becoming permanently engaged. This will require the
pilot to fly the aircraft against the collective force spring feel to
manoeuvre the aircraft, or use the collective beep trim, as the
collective FTR button does not function.
In this case when large collective movements are not required, it is
suggested that a collective FD mode (i.e. ALT) is engaged and the
collective beep trim used to maintain the required flight condition.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S70-33
Rev. 26

GUIDANCE CONTROL PANEL FAILURE
In case of Guidance Control Panel failure, recognised as non
functionality of panel pushbuttons (modes cannot be changed or
disengaged using panel), the FD may be disengaged using the cyclic
FD STBY button.
Continue flight, using the FD modes already engaged as required.
However, use the cyclic FD STBY button to disengage modes when
required. When disengaged FD is no longer available.

Flight in Icing 139G0290X002
GENERAL INFORMATION
The IPS is designed to allow full icing operations by automatically de-
icing MR blades and anti-icing TR blades. The functioning of the sys-
tem is controlled automatically (with two independent Channels A and
B) in relation to the severity of the icing conditions encountered at any
time. An additional cockpit indicating panel shows the status of the IPS
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
and additional IPS Master Warning and Caution lights (Figure 3) are
provided for both pilot and co-pilot positions.
Main Rotor Ice Protection is provided by electrical heating of the MR
blades (sequential heating of six leading edge zones along the blade
span). Tail Rotor Ice Protection is provided by continuous heating of
the leading edge of the four blades.
Electrical power is provided by two Main Gearbox mounted AC gener-
ators. Electrical power to the blades is controlled by a control box and
distributed through distribution boxes and slip rings. Atmospheric
information is provided to the control box by Outside Air Temperature
Sensors and Ice Detectors sensors (Liquid Water Content - LWC). The
Ice Detectors and windshield heating are active at all times with the
IPS ON.
The MR de-icing system works in AUTO by allowing a small amount of
ice to accrete on each leading edge zone and then sequential heating
of each zone causes the ice to be shed. It is normal, therefore, to see
an increase in torque required that will cycle up and down in accor-
dance with the heating cycles. Part of the torque increase (2 – 3%) is
due to the power required by the AC generators which also supply the
TR anti-ice function when the IPS is set to AUTO mode.
The torque variation, due to ice, can be expected to be around 5 ÷
15%, depending on OAT, LWC, and Water Droplet size (Mean Volu-
metric Diameter - MVD) when the system is working in icing condi-
tions. Higher torque increase may be experienced in more severe
icing conditions (higher LWC, larger MVD), but such conditions do not
occur frequently in the atmosphere.
No rotor unbalance is to be expected as a consequence of ice shed,
because of the symmetric 5 MR blades heating and the continuous TR
blades heating.
Page S71-2 E.A.S.A. Approved

=== DOC PAGE 2739 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 71
Document N ° IPS
139G0290X002 Flight in Icing
Ice shedding from the MR will be experienced during system function-
ing in ice and this can occasionally be seen and heard, with small
pieces of ice striking the windscreens.
With the IPS selected ON and in AUTO mode on the overhead panel
(See Figure 1), an encounter with ice is indicated by the ICING caution
illumination on the MFD CAS, when OAT is less than +4°C and LWC
values being shown on the IPS Panel ICE SEVERITY window (See
Figure 2). Icing is also indicated by a build up of ice on visible aircraft
structure, e.g. unheated area of windscreens, wiper arms, SLD
marker.
The SLD marker is a composite sphere, installed on the right side of
the fuselage, in view of the pilot through the lateral screen. It is
designed to help the pilot visually detect if SLD conditions are encoun-
tered. The sphere has a black central circle with yellow and red rings
around it. Ice accretion can be easily seen on the black marker.
A MANUAL mode is provided, selectable by the pilot, that overrides
the normal control system and applies the maximum possible heating
to the MR blades.
Different types of ice will form on the aircraft depending on the icing
conditions. The main types of ice are Glaze and Rime. Glaze ice is
clear and will tend to form at higher sub-zero temperatures (0°C to -
5°C) and is more likely with higher LWC and larger droplets. This type
of ice can generate high drag increase to occur due to the shape that
forms. Rime ice is white and opaque and tends to form at lower tem-
peratures with smaller droplets. Rime ice forms in a more streamlined
shape and causes a smaller increase in aircraft drag. It is possible to
have a mixture of both, which is know as Glime or Mixed Ice.
Flight in Freezing Rain or Freezing Drizzle is not permitted because it
is not covered by the current Airworthiness Rules for any type of air-
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
craft. Freezing Rain and Drizzle (also known as Supercooled Large
Droplets - SLD) consists of supercooled water droplets of sizes
greater than the EASA/FAA CS/Part 29 Appendix C, atmospheric defi-
nition used for Certification. These conditions, although rare, have a
serious effect on any aircraft’s performance. Pilots must use normal
operational planning and techniques to avoid flight in these conditions.
If encountered inadvertently, the conditions must be vacated immedi-
ately.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S71-3

SECTION 1 LIMITATIONS
GENERAL
All other Limitations as stated in RFM for VFR/IFR operations, Supple-
ment 22
Single Pilot IFR, Supplement 24 for VFR Night Single Pilot Opera-
tions, Supplement 12 for Category A Operations and Supplement 50
for Increased Gross Weight 6800 kg are applicable.
Operations in Icing Conditions are only permitted if the helicopter con-
figuration is in accordance with the document 139G3000A001 AW139
Icing Compatibility Reference Handbook. Any change to the air-
craft configuration which effect icing and not included in this
document, makes the aircraft NOT ICING COMPATIBLE and opera-
tions in Icing conditions are not permitted.

Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) Day/Night in known icing conditions

— Primus EPIC SW release 5.6 or higher versions.

the planned flight, periodically check OAT indications in the cockpit
(PFD & OAT back-up sensor).

 OAT is +4° C or less on one of the OAT indications in the cockpit.
Note
The following natural visual cues shall also be taken in
account:
 Ice accretion on SLD marker is detected
 Ice accretion on windshield and/or windshield
wipers is detected.
 Conditions of visible moisture are encountered.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY AND MALFUNCTION
PROCEDURES
GENERAL
The IPS is designed to maintain the maximum functionality in the
event of failures. In some cases, failures will simply be a loss of sys-
tem redundancy, in other cases some loss of rotor heating capability
will occur.
Failures are of four main groups:
• Main Rotor Critical Zone Heating Failures
• Main Rotor Non-Critical Zone Heating Failures
• Tail Rotor heating failures
• Sensor Failures.
The IPS Critical Zones are the three main rotor blade leading edge
zones, which are heated by dual power supplies and have duplicated
control systems. Failure of any of these zones causes the MR FAIL
warning to be displayed on the IPS panel and this indicates a com-
plete loss of main rotor heating (Critical and Non Critical Zones). In
case of MR FAIL (critical zone failure) also the TR heating is lost. In
these cases, depending on the severity of the icing conditions, torque
and vibration can increase quickly resulting in the need to vacate icing
conditions as soon as possible.
The IPS Non-Critical Zones are the three main rotor blade zones aft of
the leading edge critical zones. These zones are less likely to experi-
ence significant ice accretions and their failure results in the MR
DEGRADE caution to be displayed on the IPS panel. Depending on
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters the severity of the icing conditions, torque and vibration can increase.
The need to vacate icing conditions may be less urgent, but should be
considered as the consequence of subsequent failures is more severe
(loss of redundancy). The non-critical zones have single power supply
and single control systems.
The Tail Rotor heating is connected in pairs of opposing blades so it is
possible to have either pair of blades suffering a loss of heating, or all
four blades together. In the first case TR DEGRADE amber caution is
given, while in the second case the TR FAIL amber caution, both are
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S71-21

=== DOC PAGE 2758 ===
Supplement 71 AW139 - RFM - 4D
IPS Document N°
Flight in Icing 139G0290X002
displayed on the IPS panel. Loss of TR heating is not critical, but can
result in a noticeable increase in TR vibration due to asymmetric shed-
ding of ice accumulations (normally after prolonged flight in icing).
These vibrations are not damaging to the aircraft and continued flight
in icing is possible. After TR heating failure in icing, the vibration can
increase even after having left icing conditions, due to the natural
shedding that occurs resulting in TR imbalance. Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Loss of 1 ICE DET sensor and/or 1 OAT sensor is only a loss of sys-
tem redundancy with no effect on system functionality.
A double OAT sensor failure will also cause a loss of both ICE DET
sensors.
In the event of double sensor failures, the IPS uses default values (0.8
3
g/m LWC for double ice detector failure and/or -12° C for double OAT
sensor failure), in which case the IPS cycling may not match the actual
atmospheric conditions. This can result in a larger than normal MR
blade ice accretion if the LWC is higher or air temperature lower than
the default value, giving higher PI rise and possible larger PI cycles
due to less than normal heating for the actual conditions. Conversely,
if the air temperature is higher, or the LWC lower than the default val-
ues, greater than normal ice melting due to more than normal heating
for the actual conditions can cause water to re-freeze at the rear edge
of the heated area. This is ‘run-back’ ice and can cause a steady (non-
cycling) increase in PI values. Resetting of the IPS in case of a double
ICE DET and/or double OAT and/or double WSHLD sensor failure
can be beneficial to recover the system functionality.
If exceptionally severe icing conditions are encountered (including
SLD) with or without failures, speed can be reduced to 80 KIAS and
up to 110% PI used until the severity of the conditions reduces or icing
is vacated.
IPS Manual Mode is provided. Selecting MAN mode overrides the nor-
mal control system and applies maximum heating to the MR. MAN
mode is used during some failure drills and is available for use if the
icing conditions indicate the need for more MR heating than provided
by the system in AUTO mode. Care should be taken in using MAN
mode as excessive heating for long periods can result in runback ice.

139G0290X002 Flight in Icing
There are two phenomenons, related to the MR blades that can be, in
some cases, experienced when flying in ice: “high accretion of ice”
and “runback ice”.
The first may occur when the IPS is functioning in “default” mode,
using OAT and/or LWC default values and these give a heating sched-
ule, compared with the outside ice conditions, that is not completely
deicing the MR blades (less heating) and ice could accrete on the MR
blades
The second one could be related to the failure of the “non critical”
zones or to the selection of the MAN mode or when the default values
give heating schedule higher than the ambient conditions require.
In this case the system is heating not the entire blade zones, but only
the “nose” ones or it is heating too much.
This situation leads to a overheating of the blades so ice is not broken
and shed but melted, and water travels back on the blade until it
freezes again on the cold zones of the blade downstream, giving a
steadily PI rise.
Both cases will give a steady increase in PI, sometime associated with
asymmetrical shedding and increase in vibrations (i.e. instruments dif-
ficult to read).
The pilot should be aware that, in case of default mode functioning of
IPS, he has to closely monitor PI, OAT, A/C vibrations and SLD
marker, which is to be monitored to understand the type of ice encoun-
tered.
Switching OFF then ON the IPS the electrical power is removed for
about 15 seconds. During this period all the de-icing functions are not
available. If flying in ice the parts of the helicopter not heated will con-
tinue to accumulate ice.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters All failures that can affect the IPS trigger either the IPS red Master
Warning Light (IPS MWL) or the IPS amber Master Caution lights (IPS
MCL) See Figure 3-1. These 2 additional attention getters are posi-
tioned on the instrument panel beside the main MWL, MCL in front of
the pilot and copilot positions.

PILOT ACTIONS IN CASE OF SEVERE ICE ENCOUNTERS
Severe icing conditions are indicated by some or all of the following:
 High PI rise (>30% above normal for flight condition)
 Steady increase in base PI with heating cycles
3
 High LWC (>1.5 g/m )
 Heavy amounts of water streaming across windscreens
 Evidence of SLD (ice forming on sides of aircraft, SLD
Marker)
 Increase in vibration
 Tendency for significant speed loss.
Actions:
 Reduce speed to 80 KIAS
 Select 102% NR
 Use up to 110% PI
 Check for system failures
 Select MAN
— if PI reduces Select AUTO, and use MANUAL to
reduce subsequent PI rise.
— if PI does not reduce, or rises steadily, select AUTO
and do not select MAN again (possible runback ice)
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
 Change altitude – severe ice conditions are usually near the
top of the clouds
 Consider vacating icing conditions if severity does not reduce
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S71-25

PART II - MANUFACTURER’S DATA
SECTION 6 - WEIGHT AND BALANCE
No Change.
SECTION 7 - SYSTEM DESCRIPTION
The Ice Protection System (IPS) is composed of:
- Main Rotor blade de-ice protection, cyclical heating the lead-
ing edge zone of each blade to remove the ice that accretes
- Tail Rotor blades anti-ice protection, continuous heating the
leading edge of each blade, not allowing ice accretion
- Windshield anti-ice protection, continuous heating the frontal
part of the pilot and copilot screens, not allowing ice accretion
- Engine intakes passive protection, allowing proper airflow to
engines even in case of ice accretion
- Heating power management and distribution by dual channel
boxes
- Ice detectors for ice severity evaluation
- Two AC generators
- Additional Intake passive protections: ECS, cabin ventilation
and AC GEN generators
- The system has some control boxes, ICB, MRUD, MRLD and
TRD, with two control channels (ch.A & ch.B).
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Figure 7-1 is a schematic drawing of the components of the entire sys-
tem.
The 270VDC power for the blades heating and the 115V/400Hz AC
power for the windshield heating is generated by two alternators (one
45 KVA and one 25 KVA) fitted on the MGB.
The AC power is transmitted directly to the windshields, while for the
blades it is converted to DC by two Auto Transformer Rectifier Unit
(ATRU) fitted in the RH rear avionic bay.

MAIN ROTOR BLADES HEATING
The DC power for MR blades from ATRUs passes through
- the MR Lower Distributor (MRLD) fitted in the rear baggage
compartment and controlling the power ON/OFF
- the MR slip ring fitted in the MR mast passing power from
fixed to rotating parts
- the MR Upper Distributor (MRUD) fitted in the beanie, where
the power is switched sequentially to each of the six zones of
each blade leading edge.
The blades are heated by metallic nets embedded inside the blade
structure below the anti-erosion shields.
In each blade there are 6 spanwise zones activated in sequence to
allow proper ice shedding (see Figure 7-2).
When a blade zone is heated, the same zone of the other blades are
heated in the same way, to avoid asymmetric shedding on blades
leading to vibration and unbalance.

TR BLADES HEATING

Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

avoid overheating.

SYSTEM MANAGEMENT
The system is managed by an IPS Control Box (ICB) fitted in the rear
of the baggage compartment, controlling the power distribution and
cycling based on the data received from:
- the two ice detectors
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
- the two OAT sensors
- the two pitot probes
- the temperature sensors fitted in the windshields and in each
TR blade.
The system status signals are displayed on a dedicated panel, fitted in
the central zone of the cockpit (See Figure 7-5), with dedicated Master
Warning and Caution lights in front of both pilot and copilot.
The system functioning is selected by the four switches on the over-
head panel, pilot side (See Figure 7-6).

ICE DETECTORS
The two ice detector measuring heads are fitted on the fuselage

3

SLD MARKER
This feature is installed on the pilot side and it is designed to help the
pilot to detect if SLD conditions are encountered, when the red marker
is completely covered with ice.
The SLD marker is a composite sphere (See Figure 7-8), installed with
a support on the right side of the fuselage, positioned where the pilot
can promptly determine ice accretion on it by simply looking outside
the lateral screen. The sphere is provided with a black circle, a yellow
and a red ring. The ice accretes on the different zones, depending on
the MVD. The black circle (near the stagnation point) and yellow ring
are relevant to the conditions of the icing envelopes. When ice starts
to accrete on the yellow ring (far from the stagnation point, therefore
indicating ice accretion with increasing droplet size) a significant (but
still not critical) PI increase is expected.
Ice accretion on the red zone is an indication of icing conditions out-
side the certification envelopes for which the IPS is designed to oper-
ate. The SLD marker is presently not de-iced, therefore its suitability to
detect SLD conditions could be impaired by an excessive accretion of
ice on the sphere.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

IPS FUNCTIONING MODES
IPS TST/RST function is inhibited in icing conditions. The test duration
is approximately 30 seconds, following an ON/OFF switching the time
for system activation is approximately 15 seconds.
AUTO:
This is the normal mode of IPS (IPS switched ON and in AUTO
mode).The system is heating TR blades, windshields and ice detec-
tors to anti-ice them.
It processes also LWC and OAT data to compute the ON/OFF time to
heat and deice the six MR blades zones in turn. In this mode MR and
TR blades are heated when the LWC value is detected.
MANUAL:
When the IPS is set to MAN mode, the IPS is always heating the TR
blades, windshields and ice detectors but is heating the six MR blades
zones in turn without any rest time at the end of the MR blade heating
cycle.
Page S71-68

=== DOC PAGE 2809 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 71
Document N ° IPS
139G0290X002 Flight in Icing
In this case the IPS is working by automatically setting OAT = -23° C
and
LWC = 1.5 g/m³.
DEFAULT OAT AND LWC VALUES
In case of both OAT and/or LWC sensors failure, the IPS is functioning
by automatically setting these data to default values of -12° C and 0.8
g/m³, respectively.
SYSTEM CONTROL AND CAUTION/WARNING/ADVISORY LOGIC
The ICB controls the system through 4 different “chains”:
1. ICB-MRLD-MRUD chain (MR heating control)
If Ch A of one of the 3 boxes (whichever) fails, all the 3 boxes’ Ch
A are lost.
If Ch B of one of the 3 boxes (whichever) fails, all the 3 boxes’ Ch
B are lost.
2. ICB-TRD chain (TR heating control)
If ICB Ch A fails, also TRD Ch A fails.
If TRD Ch A fails, ICB Ch A does not fail (therefore a TR failure
does not cause the loss of also the MR).
3. ICB-W/S chain (W/S heating control)
If ICB Ch A fails, W/S2 (pilot) is lost.
If ICB Ch B fails, W/S1 (copilot) is lost
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters The windshields anti-icing is started as soon as the IPS is
switched ON, not when LWC is detected. This is to give the crew
the additional possibility to de-mist the screens when the helicop-
ter is out of the clouds.
4. ICB-cockpit panel (System status to flight crew)
The ICB Ch A and Ch B are independent from the cockpit panel Ch A
and Ch B.
Page S71-69

=== DOC PAGE 2810 ===
Supplement 71 AW139 - RFM - 4D
IPS Document N°
Flight in Icing 139G0290X002
Failure of the panel’s Ch A/B are managed with advisory “CH A” and
“CH B” in the ICE SEVERITY window, while loss of ICB Ch A + Ch B
communication to display, are managed with the advisory “DATA”.
The “CHK” indication is displayed for failure of 1 or 2 temperature sen-
rd
sors inside one of the windshields (the 3 sensor is available for the
system, so there is no impact on the windshields heating) or in case of Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
loss of the temperature sensor inside one of the two opposite TR
blades (the opposite blade’s sensor is used instead, so there is no
impact on the TR heating).
The “BOUT” indication is raised in case of loss of the control boxes’
Ch B while the Ch A is controlling the system (there is no impact on
the IPS operation, only loss of redundancy in case of subsequent fail-
ure of Ch A).
“CHK” and “BOUT” indications may be displayed continously, if one of
the relevant conditions is met, only with the helicopter on ground. In
flight they are displayed only in non-icing conditions for a limited time
(20’’) after the ICB IBIT function, if initiated by the crew. The indica-
tions of the loss of the status panel channels can be displayed only on
ground.
When both ice detectors’ LWC values are correctly read by the ICB,
the current ice severity displayed by the panel is the maximum of the
two. If one of the two is not valid, only the remaining value is dis-
played. If both the two LWC values are not received, the message “ —
.— — ” is displayed.
OAT values from the two helicopter sensors are received by ICB and
for system management the lower of the two is always considered. In
case of failure of one of the sensors, the value from the other is used.
For failures of both the OAT sensors and/or both the ice detectors, or if
the ICB doesn’t receive the OAT and/or the LWC data, with the mode
switch to AUTO the ICB automatically passes to the “default mode” of
operation, where intermediate fixed values of OAT and/or LWC are
3
used (OAT = -12° C and LWC = 0.8 g/m ).
For failure of both the OAT sensors, the ice detectors will fail as they
use OAT value for LWC calculation.

AC POWER DISTRIBUTION
The 45 KVA generator is the primary source for the rotors heating. In
normal operation it supplies the entire power required by the MR and
TR blades. The power required by the ice detectors and the wind-
shields is shared between the generators: the 45 KVA AC Generator
supplies the co-pilot side, while the 25 KVA Generator supplies the
pilot side.
If, during the normal operation of the system, a failure on the 25 KVA
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
AC generator occurs, the entire power required by the IPS is supplied
by the 45 KVA AC gen.
For a failure of the 45 KVA generator the system automatically starts
to operate in low power mode, with the secondary AC gen supplying
only the MR critical zones, the TR blades, the pilot W/S and the pilot
ice detector.

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 72
Document N ° Ultraforce Series
139G0290X002 FLIR
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Ultraforce 350, 350 EP (Enhanced Performance) and 350HD
(High Definition) FLIR system is a remote controlled day/night high
resolution, infrared (IR) imaging system and a TV (CCD) camera with
colour video.
The system consists of a stabilized Turret-FLIR Unit (TCU), mounted
under the nose of the helicopter (Figure 1 & Figure 3), and a Hand
Control Unit (HCU) that contains all the controls necessary to operate
the FLIR turret and systems. (See Figure 4 & Figure 5). The HCU
handgrip has a stowage at the rear of the interseat console.
The TCU is gyro stabilized. Its azimuth and elevation, therefore the
FLIR Line Of Sight (LOS) corresponding to the center of the image,
can be directed to any position within the Field Of Regard (FOR)
which is +20° to -120° in elevation and 360° in azimuth from the for-
ward position.
The FLIR Imager incorporates all the necessary optics, detectors and
required electronics to convert the infrared radiation from the medium
wave infrared thermal imaging sensor into standard video signals
which are processed within the TCU for display.
The IR and TV (CCD) and optional Spotter Scope camera provide
video outputs that can be monitored on either pilot or copilot MFD.
Either IR or CCD images can be selected independently on pilot and
copilot MFD or both images in miniature. If a digital map is installed
the copilot and pilot MFD will only display the same source data, either
FLIR or digital map.
The optional central 5th display or a cabin display can also be used to
display either image.
Additional optional equipment available on certain models of the Ultra-
fore 350 are the laser range finder (Class 1 eye safe) ESLRF, the laser
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
pointer and laser illuminator both Class IIIb and not eye safe.
The Ultrafore 350 laser Class IIIb devices, if fitted, are electrically dis-
abled. When laser operations are authorised, a Laser Interlock Unit
(LIU), Figure 6, is fitted in the interseat console incorporating an ARM
switch requiring a key to ARM the laser before firing. A WOW interlock
ensures the laser is not used when the aircraft is on the ground.
For full information on the use of the Ultraforce 350 FLIR refer to the
Ultraforce 350, 350EP or 350HD FLIR Owners Manual, latest revision.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S72-1
Rev. 11

GENERAL INFORMATION
This Supplement gives details of the radar Selex-Galileo Gabbiano
T20N (P/N 4G3441F00211) and TS20N (P/N 4G3441F00611)
Surveillance and Weather Radar.
The Gabbiano T20N and TS20N Surveillance and Weather radar
provides a multi-mode radar capability for maritime missions. The
following air to surface modes of operation are available:
• Sea surface search for maritime surveillance
• ISAR (Inverse Search and Rescue)
• Track While Scan
• Strip SAR (Search and Rescue)
• Spot SAR (Search and Rescue)
• Weather
• Ground mapping
• Beacon.
The radar system comprises of a flat plate antenna and drive unit, a
receiver exciter processor, a transmitter front end unit, and a radar
control panel mounted in the interseat console (See Figure 1).
The radar control panel (See Figure 2) allows the selection of all radar
modes, radar controls and non-radar modes such as navigation
overlays modes and target marker mode. The control panel also
contains a joystick for controlling the cursor for target marker and
tracker functions.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters The information may be displayed on the MFD’s or (central) 5th
display (if fitted) by pressing the appropriate button on the 5th display.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S73-1
Rev. 22

GABBIANO RADAR DISCREPANCIES
(T20N P/N 4G3441F00211 ONLY)
The following radar functional discrepancies have been noted:
• To ensure the radar control panel button operations are regis-
tered by the radar system, the pushbuttons must be held
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
depressed for at least half a second
• Beacon mode detection ranges. The maximum range demonst-
trated are as follows:
a) SART. Less than 5 NM
b) SST-181E (two pulse). Less than 10 NM.
The DO-172 six pulse beacon has not been tested.
To improve beacon detection stability it is recommended to
reduce antenna scan to ±30°.
• During operation of Radar in weather mode the STS caption on
the control panel may illuminate sporadically. This is not an indi-
cation of a system malfunction
• In HSS mode the TWS function is inoperative
• In SRV Mode if a TWS track is lost temporarily it may not be
automatically recovered by the radar
• Care should be taken when entering a SEGMENTED STRIP
SAR to ensure a segment greater than 0 is entered or the radar
may fail requiring the radar system to be re-started.

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 74

139G0290X002 Light Configuration
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Enhanced Landing Light Configuration, installed as standard on
aircraft from S/N 31400 onwards and S/N 41300 onwards with kit
P/N 4G3340F00211 (Non NVG Compatible) and variant
P/N 4G3360F04411/4G3340F02611(NVG Compatible), introduces 2
steerable landing lights mounted under the aircraft on the right and left
hand side of the aircraft nose (See Figure 1). These replace the origi-
nal Taxi/Landing lights mounted on the LH and RH sponsons.
The normal control of the two landing lights is via the LT control panel
installed in the interseat console (See Figure 2 or Figure 3) and the
standard five way switch mounted on each collective grip.
(See Figure 4).
When the LDG LTS SELECT rotary switch on the LT panel is set to
NORM the right hand and left hand landing lights are controlled inde-
pendently by their respective side collective 5 way switch, i.e RH col-
lective switch controls only the RH light and LH collective switch
controls only the LH light.
Selecting the RH UNSTOW STOW/OFF switch to UNSTOW the RH
landing light remains stowed but is powered. By pressing the five way
switch on the RH collective in the central position, the light is turned
on, the green advisory message LANDING LT ON (for RH landing
light) illuminates on the CAS and the RH ON green indicator light on
the LT panel illuminates. The light remains stowed until the collective
five way switch is moved to EXT which extends the light. The light may
then be directed left (L) or right (R) and down (RETR) or up (EXT) by

GENERAL INFORMATION
LIMITED ICING CLEARANCE AND ICING GENERAL
The Limited Ice Protection System (LIPS) permits flight into icing
within a limited envelope of icing conditions without blade de-icing pro-
vided that the operational capability to descend into non-icing condi-
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
tions is available throughout the intended route. The ability to escape
from icing conditions is required because of the possibility of encoun-
tering ambient conditions more severe than those permitted for contin-
uos operation. For this purpose, the LIPS Limitations include a
requirement for a 500 ft band of positive temperature air always to be
available above the Minimum Safe Altitude (MSA) for the route being
flown.
Continuous operation is possible within a defined severity of ambient
icing conditions and time limited operation is permitted in defined con-
ditions of greater severity. The purpose of the time limited area is to
allow the crew to take action to reduce the severity of the conditions
being encountered, usually by descending to allow natural de-icing of
the aircraft. The crew are provided with methods to monitor the icing
severity and the effect on the aircraft.
The severity of the ice in icing conditions depends on the temperature
and liquid water content (LWC). Different types of ice will form on the
aircraft depending on the icing conditions. The main types of ice are
Glaze and Rime. Glaze ice is clear and will tend to form at higher sub-
zero temperatures (0°C to -5°C) and is more likely with higher LWC
and larger droplets. This type of ice can generate high drag increase
to occur due to the shape that forms. Rime ice is white and opaque
and tends to form at lower temperatures with smaller droplets. Rime
ice forms in a more streamlined shape and causes a smaller increase
in aircraft drag. It is possible to have a mixture of both, which is known
as Glime or Mixed Ice.
The PI variation, due to ice, can be expected to be around 5 ÷ 20%,
depending on OAT, LWC, and Water Droplet size (Mean Volumetric
Diameter - MVD). Higher torque increase may be experienced in more
severe icing conditions (higher LWC, larger MVD), but such conditions
do not occur frequently in the atmosphere. Cloud formations that are
know to contain high levels of icing, such as large vertical clouds,
should be avoided.
Page S76-2 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 6

=== DOC PAGE 2869 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 76
Document N ° LIPS
139G0290X002 Flight in Limited Icing
Ice shedding from the MR will be experienced and this can be associ-
ated with vibrations or seen and heard, with small pieces of ice striking
the windscreens.
Flight in Freezing Rain or Freezing Drizzle is not permitted as it is not
covered by the current Airworthiness Rules for any type of aircraft.
Freezing Rain and Drizzle (also known as Supercooled Large Droplets
- SLD) consists of supercooled water droplets of sizes greater than the
EASA/FAA Part 29 Appendix C, atmospheric definition used for Certi-
fication. These conditions, although rare, have a serious effect on any
aircraft’s performance.
Pilots must use normal operational planning and techniques to avoid
flight in these conditions. If encountered inadvertently, the conditions
must be vacated immediately.
LIPS FUNCTIONALITY
The LIPS system comprises of the following equipments:
— Cockpit indicating ICE CONDITION panel indicating the LWC
value and the TIME IN ICE (Figure 2 and Figure 3)
— Limited Ice Protection System (LIPS) control box
— 2 Ice detectors and their associated processing units
— Heated Windscreens
— Main Gearbox mounted AC generator to supply electric power via
a control box and distribution box to the heated windscreens
— LIPS System control panel on overhead panel (See Figure 1)
— SLD Marker installed on the right side of the fuselage, in view of
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
the pilot through the lateral screen.
The LIPS control box has two independent channels (A and B) which
receive the signals of OAT (from aircraft basic sensors via MAU) and
the two ice detectors and determines the severity of the icing condi-
tion. The value of the LWC, temperature and time have specific maxi-
mum limits which have been determined for the ‘Limited Icing’
envelope. The exposure and severity of the icing is indicated to the
pilot by CAS cautions, advisory messages and on the indicating panel
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S76-3
Rev. 6

the LWC and “Time-In Ice” values. Icing is also indicated by a build up
of ice on aircraft structure visible to the pilot, e.g. unheated area of
windscreens, wiper arms, SLD marker.
For any exceedance indicated by the system the action is to vacate
the icing conditions as soon as possible.
The “Limited Icing” conditions approved and incorporated in the LIPS

logic on the AW139 are presented in Figure 4. Ambient OAT and LWC

No-Ice Zone (Blue) - For any OAT above +0°C and any LWC

craft.

VACATING THE ICING ENVIRONMENT
Vacating the icing environment, due to expire of the maximum “TIME
LIMITED ZONE” of 5 minutes or entry into the “VACATE ZONE”
requires the aircraft to manoeuvre into a less severe ambient OAT and
LWC icing zone.
When vacating into the “NO-ICE ZONE” ice shedding will take place
and after a period of 30 seconds in this zone the aircraft should be
clear of ice and it is possible to re-enter the “TIME LIMITED ZONE”, if
required.
When vacating into the “NO-LIMIT ZONE” there is no ice shedding but
no increase in ice accumulation so these ambient conditions can be
maintained with no time limit, however, re-entry into the “TIME
LIMITED ZONE” is only permitted if a total time of 5 minutes in the
“TIME LIMITED ZONE” has not occurred.
LIPS OPERATION
With the LIPS selected OFF and a temperature below +4°C the CAS
1-2 ICE DET OFF caution will illuminate, to indicate the system is off
and icing conditions are being approached. Selecting the ICE DET
switch ON, on the overhead panel activates the system, the AC GEN
and WSHLD switches must also be selected ON (if not already
selected ON) which will illuminate the green 1-2 WSHLD HTR ON
advisory.
An ice encounter is indicated by the amber CAS ICE CONDITION
caution and green ICE advisory illumination depending on the severity
of the icing condition encountered.
Entry into the NO-LIMIT ZONE (Figure 2) causes the ICE CONDITION
caution to illuminate for 5 seconds and the green ICE advisory
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters illuminates. The LWC value is displayed on the panel but the time in
ice condition does not increment as there is no time limit in this zone.
Entry into the “TIME-LIMITED ZONE” causes the ICE CONDITION
caution to illuminate continuously (the ICE advisory extinguishes, if
illuminated). The LWC value is displayed on the panel and the time in
ice condition display increments as the maximum permitted time in
this zone is 5 minutes. On expiry of the 5 minutes continuous time or
total cumulative time in this zone the ICE LIMIT caution illuminates
indicating to the pilot the icing conditions must be vacated.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S76-5
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 2872 ===
Supplement 76 AW139 - RFM - 4D
LIPS Document N°
Flight in Limited Icing 139G0290X002
To clear the ICE LIMIT caution the aircraft must enter the “NO-ICE
ZONE. To reset the “TIME IN ICE counter to 0:0 a period of
30 seconds or more in the “NO ICE ZONE” (above 0 °C) is necessary.
Entry into the “VACATE ZONE” causes the ICE CONDITION and ICE
LIMIT cautions to illuminate immediately indicating to the pilot the icing
conditions must be vacated. When the aircraft is back in one of the
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
reduced icing zones the caution extinguishes.
When vacating the icing zone if the aircraft enters the “NO LIMIT
ZONE” the “TIME IN ICING” count stops and remains at the value
when the zone was entered whether the entry into the NO-LIMIT
ZONE was due to expiry of the time limit or not. If the time limit has not
expired further excursions into the TIME LIMITED ZONE are
permitted up to the maximum time allowed (5 minutes).
If the “NO-ICE ZONE” conditions are entered the time remains at the
value when the zone was entered until a continuous time of
30 seconds has expired (allowing the ice to shed) then the “TIME IN
ICE” is reset to zero.
Due to the tolerances of the OAT and ICE sensors and the LIPS
algorithms used the cautions may illuminate when the values of OAT
and LWC observed are in a different zone to that being indicated by
the caution system. The LIPS operation is conservative, however, the
caution procedures should be followed regardless of the indication of
OAT and LWC and taking into consideration the other associated
indication of icing.
As part of the LIPS system an SLD marker is installed on the right side
of the fuselage, in view of the pilot through the lateral screen. The SLD
marker is a composite sphere designed to help the pilot visually detect
if SLD conditions are encountered. The sphere has a black central
circle with yellow and red rings around it. Ice accretion can be easily
seen on the black marker.
See Section 7 of this Supplement for detailed system information.
Page S76-6 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 25

SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
GENERAL
All other Limitations as stated in RFM for VFR/IFR operations,
Supplement 22 Single Pilot IFR, Supplement 24 for VFR Night Single
Pilot Operations, Supplement 12 for Category A Operations and Sup-
plement 50 for Increased Gross Weight 6800 kg are applicable.
Operations in Limited Icing Conditions are only permitted if the
helicopter configuration is in accordance with the document
139G3000A001 AW139 Icing Compatibility Reference Handbook. Any
change to the aircraft configuration which effect icing and not included
in this document, makes the aircraft NOT LIMITED ICING COMPATI-
BLE and operations in Limited Icing conditions are not permitted.
The LIPS equipment certification approval does NOT constitute opera-
tional approval. Operational approval for Limited Icing conditions must
be granted by the Local Aviation Authority.
Any flight where Limited Icing conditions are encountered must be
recorded in the helicopter log-book.
TYPE OF OPERATIONS
Limited icing assumes that the aircraft has the ability to vacate
the icing conditions, at any time, with the availability of a band of posi-
tive air temperature of at least 500 ft height into which the aircraft
can descend to de-ice naturally.
MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW
Limited Ice conditions - Two pilots
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
REQUIRED EQUIPMENT
— For Operations in Limited Icing conditions LIPS is to be installed
(P/N: 4G3000F00111 “Kit Limited Ice Protection System”).
— Primus Epic system SW release 5.6 or higher versions.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S76-9

IN FLIGHT PROCEDURES
When OAT is 4 °C or below and/or icing conditions are expected along
the flight route and/or when visible moisture condition are encountered
and/or ice accretion is detected during flight:
1. AC GEN switch — ON Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
2. ICE DET switch — ON
3. WSHLD switch — ON
With the LIPS system selected ON, entering icing conditions will
cause illumination of the ICE CONDITION caution on the CAS and
indication of “TIME IN ICE” and “ICE SEVERITY”. If the ambient con-
ditions are within the NO-LIMIT ZONE the caution illuminates for 5
seconds only and the green ICE advisory illuminates.
When entering icing conditions a maximum airspeed of 120 KIAS is
recommended until the severity of the icing conditions is established.
In cruise when ALT and IAS modes are engaged, if PI limiting is active
the airspeed will automatically reduce to maintain altitude.
CAUTION
A power increase can be expected in icing conditions and
should be carefully monitored by the pilot. The icing con-
ditions should be vacated as soon as possible if exces-
sive power increase or unacceptable or vibration are
noted.
Note
Monitoring PI variation, IAS, OAT, LWC, ice accretion
type (on visible structure and SLD Marker), amount of
water streaming on the heated windscreen will all give
good cues to the severity of the icing conditions.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY AND MALFUNCTION
PROCEDURES
GENERAL
The LIPS is designed to maintain the maximum functionality in the
event of failures. In some cases, failures will simply be a loss of sen-
sor redundancy, in other cases some loss of sensor readings.
Loss of one ICE DET sensor and/or one OAT sensor is only a loss of
system redundancy with no effect on system functionality.
A double OAT sensor failure will also cause a loss of both ICE DET
sensors.
Cautions AC GEN FAIL and/or AC BUS FAIL will suppress 1-2 ICE
DET FAIL and/or 1-2 WSHLD FAIL.
Selecting the LIPS ICE DET switch OFF then ON in case of a double
ICE DET and/or double OAT and/or double WSHLD sensor failure can
be beneficial to recover the system functionality.
If exceptionally severe icing conditions are encountered (including
SLD) with or without failures, speed should be reduced to 80 KIAS and
up to 110% PI used and the icing conditions vacated.
The pilot should be aware that, in case of general default mode func-
tioning of LIPS, the PI, OAT, A/C vibrations and SLD marker should be
closely monitor to understand the type of ice encountered.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S76-25
Rev. 6

=== DOC PAGE 2892 ===
Supplement 76 AW139 - RFM - 4D
LIPS Document N°
Flight in Limited Icing 139G0290X002
PILOT ACTIONS IN CASE OF SEVERE ICE ENCOUNTERS
Severe icing conditions are indicated by some or all of the following:
 High PI rise (>30% above normal for flight condition)
3 Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
 High LWC (>1.5 g/m )
 Heavy amounts of water streaming across windscreens
 Evidence of SLD (ice forming on sides of aircraft, SLD
Marker)
 Increase in vibration
 Tendency for significant speed loss
Actions:
 Reduce speed to 80 KIAS
 Select 102% NR
 Use up to 110% PI
 Check for system failures
 Vacating icing conditions immediately
Page S76-26 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 6

SECTION 7 - SYSTEM DESCRIPTION
The Limited Ice Protection System (LIPS) is composed of:
- Windshield anti-ice protection, continuous heating the frontal
part of the pilot and copilot screens, not allowing ice accretion.
- Engine intakes passive protection, allowing proper airflow to
engines even in case of ice accretion
- Heating power management and distribution by dual channel
boxes
- Ice detectors for ice severity evaluation.
- One AC generator
- Additional Intake passive protections: ECS, cabin ventilation
and AC GEN generator.
- The system has one control box: ICB, with two control chan-
nels (ch.A & ch.B).
Figure 7-1 is a schematic drawing of the components of the entire sys-
tem and Figure 7-2 is the LIPS block diagram.
The 115V/400Hz AC power for the windshield heating is generated by
one alternator (25KVA) fitted on the MGB.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S76-39

ENGINE INTAKE PROTECTION
Each main engine intake and each auxiliary engine intake is protected

passes (See Figure 7-4).

SYSTEM MANAGEMENT
The system is managed by an LIPS Control Box (ICB) fitted in the rear
of the baggage compartment, controlling the power distribution based
on the data received from:
- the two ice detectors
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
- the two OAT sensors
- the temperature sensors fitted in the windshields.
On LIPS panel the LWC value along with TIME IN ICE are displayed
on a dedicated panel, fitted in the central zone of the cockpit
(See Figure 7-5).
The system functioning is selected by the three switches on the over-
head panel, pilot side (See Figure 7-6).
TIME IN ICE is computed by the system with the higher LWC value
given by the two ID and the lower OAT value measured by the two air-
craft sensors.
Due to this configuration it may occur that the PFD OAT indication is in
the “Continuous” LIPS area and the LIPS logic is displaying the “Inter-
mittent area on the CAS list.

139G0290X002 Flight in Limited Icing
SLD MARKER
This feature is installed on the pilot side and it is designed to help the
pilot to detect if SLD conditions are encountered, when the red marker
is completely covered with ice.
The SLD marker is a composite sphere (See Figure 7-8), installed with
a support on the right side of the fuselage, positioned where the pilot
can promptly determine ice accretion on it by simply looking outside
the lateral screen. The sphere is provided with circular bands having
three different colours: the ice accretes on the different zones,
depending on the MVD. The black and yellow zone (near the stagna-
tion point) are relevant to the conditions of the icing envelopes. When
ice starts to accrete on the yellow zone (away from the stagnation
point, therefore registering ice accretion only when MVD is high) a sig-
nificant (but still not critical) PI increase is expected.
Ice accretion on the red zone is an indication of icing conditions out-
side the certification envelopes for which the LIPS is designed to oper-
ate. The SLD marker is presently not de-iced, therefore its suitability to
detect SLD conditions and is limited by excessive accretion of ice on
the sphere.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Figure 7-8 SLD Marker

SYSTEM CONTROL AND CAUTION/ADVISORY LOGIC
The ICB controls the system through 2 different “chains”:
1. ICB-W/S chain (W/S heating control)
If ICB Ch A fails, W/S2 (pilot) is lost;
If ICB Ch B fails, W/S1 (copilot) is lost.
The windshields anti-icing is started as soon as the LIPS is
switched ON, not when LWC is detected. This is to give the crew
the additional option to de-mist the screens when the helicopter is
out of the clouds.
2. ICB-cockpit panel (System status to flight crew)
The LIPS ICB has two independent, redundant channels (CH A &
CH B) that work in parallel. The ICB manages power to the two heated
windshields, CH A controls the pilot windshield (WSHLD 2) and CH B
the copilot windshield (WSHLD 1).
The ICB CH A and CH B are independent from the cockpit panel
channel.
The operation of the windshield heating is via the WSHLD ON/OFF
switch mounted in the overhead panel. AC power to the windshield
heating elements is regulated by values from the temperature sen-
sors, fitted within the windshields, which are used to turn the power on
and off to maintain the temperature of the windshield between 35°C
and 52°C. An overheat threshold of 82°C is used by the ICB to shut
down the relevant windshield heating if the value is reached or super-
seded. If one of the three temperature sensors fails the ICB uses the
remaining sensors to control the power. If a second sensor fails the
ICB indicates a DEGRADED status and uses the remaining sensor to
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters control the temperature. In the event of failure of all the three sensors
the ICB indicates a FAIL status and shuts down the relevant wind-
screen.
The ICB has two ARINC429 input lines (high speed) for the two ICE
DETECTOR signals. The ICB compares the LWC worst value (MAX)
to the predefined limits and signals and alarm if the limit has been
exceeded. A failure of one ice detector causes the ICB to use just the
values from the other ice detector.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S76-49
Rev. 6

A further two ARINC429 lines (low speed) are used to receive the
OAT values from each MAU (ADC 1 and 2), the system uses the lower
of the two.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The Goodrich Landing Gear is available as an option to substitute the
standard Liebherr Landing Gear.
The Goodrich Landing Gear provides the aircraft with more ground
clearance and improves taxiing characteristics on rough ground at
weights up to 6800kg.
The installation of this landing gear includes a different sponson
design, due to the different mounting, geometry and retraction mecha-
nism of the landing gear. The landing gear control panel, in the cock-
pit, is supplied by a different manufacturer, however, it is identical,
externally and functionally, to the standad landing gear control panel.
Due to the different sponson design the Life Raft installation (Ditching
Configurations Supplement 9) has also been modified to be compati-
ble with the new sponson (P/N 4G2560F00711). The life rafts are
mounted vertically, however, functionality has not changed.
The Emergency Flotation System P/N 3G9560F00113 may be
installed with the Goodrich Landing Gear. (Ditching Configurations
Supplement 9).
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S77-1
Rev. 3

139G0290X002 ADS-B Transmitter
GENERAL INFORMATION
The FreeFlight Systems FDL-978-TX Universal Access Transceiver
(UAT) Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B) Out
Transmitter is a 978 Mhz class B1 transmitter which broadcasts peri-
odically (once per second) the aircraft position, speed and other flight
information. This information may can be displayed to an ATC and
other aircraft which have suitable equipment. The equipment satisfies
the DO-282B MOPS and the TSO-C154c requirements for UAT ADS-
B class B1 and B1S equipment and has been shown to meet the
equipment requirements of 14CFR §91.227.
The system comprises of a Front Panel Controller TC-978 mounted in
the cockpit interseat console (See Figure 1), the FDL-978-TX Trans-
mitter mounted in the baggage compartment, two antennae installed
on the top and bottom of the tail and all associated wiring.
The system is connected to the aircraft systems for GPS position, alti-
tude, airspeed and other aircraft parameters which are configured in
the installation.

Mode Selection Knob Functions
OFF Power is removed from the FDL-978-TX.
SBY The FDL-978-TX is on but will not transmit any ADS-B
messages.
GND The FDL-978-TX is placed in Airborne Transmission Mode Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
or automatically switches between Airborne and Ground
Mode with WOW switch and the aircraft velocity meets the
criteria described in DO-282B for the specific aircraft con-
figuration. Pressure altitude is displayed.
ON The FDL-978-TX is placed in Airborne Transmission Mode
or automatically switches between Airborne and Ground
Mode with WOW switch and the aircraft velocity meets the
criteria described in DO-282B for the specific aircraft con-
figuration. Pressure altitude reporting is suppressed.
ALT The FDL-978-TX is placed in Airborne Transmission Mode
or automatically switches between Airborne and Ground
Mode with WOW switch and the aircraft velocity meets the
criteria described in DO-282B for the specific aircraft con-
figuration. Pressure altitude is reported.
Push Buttons
IDT Press the IDT button when ATC instructs you to “Ident” or
“Squawk Ident”.
FN Pressing the FN button provides access to changing the
Call Sign/ Flight ID. You may either directly rotate the
code knob or press the key and the first character of the
flight ID will be highlighted. Use the rotary code knob to
select your choice of alpha-numeric characters. Press
again and the cursor moves to the next character. You
must present each time all the way through the 8 charac-
ters to save your Call Sign/ Flight ID change. Pressing
the button again allows the pilot to view the present posi-
tion being transmitted. Pressing the button a third time
allows the pilot to view the FDL-978-TX WARNINGS.

139G0290X002 ADS-B Transmitter
VFR Pressing the VFR button sets the ADS-B to the pre-pro-
grammed conspicuity code and VFR Flight ID. Pressing
the button again restores the previous squawk code and
Flight ID.
ENT The ENT button enters a digit in the code selector.
Code Selector Knob
The right hand knob is used to set squawk codes and the Flight ID.
The FN button selects which will be updated. Turning the knob will
highlight the first digit on the display, and the digit can be changed as
required. Press the ENT button to advance to the next digit. When
ENT is pressed on the last digit, the new squawk code or Flight ID will
replace the previous value. If the code entry is not completed within 7
seconds the changes are ignored and the previous code restored.

NEW PHASE 7 FUNCTIONS
RNP Navigation Specification Compliance
The Phase 7 and later Primus EPIC software is certified for operations
in accordance with RNP Navigation Specifications per PBN Manual
ICAO doc. 9613 as described in Supplement 80.
RNP Approach Indications
As an aid for RNP AR APCH approaches, an expanded lateral
deviation scale is added on the PFD below the ADI, refer Supplement
80 for further details.
Automatic LNAV engagement at Go-Around
The Phase 7 and later software has implemented a change to the Go
Around mode. The GA mode engagement has been modified to
include an automatic engagement of LNAV mode.
To allow steeper and safer steep approach, when activated from
speed below 70 KIAS, the GA will automatically acquire an IAS
reference airspeed of 70 KIAS, instead of the previously implemented
80 KIAS. Furthermore the minimum engagement speed is reduced to
41 KIAS (See Supplements 67, 69, 70 as appropriate for full details).

TCAS II Capability
The EPIC Phase 7 and later software supports the TCAS II
requirements for the display parameters.
For full details of the TCAS II see Supplement 82, if applicable.
EGPWS -30 and later capability
The EPIC Phase 7 and later software supports the improvements in
the EGPWS-30 installation with the inclusion of the OFFSHORE and

Glideslope” alerts, new “TAIL TOO LOW” curves to reduce nuisance

applicable.

in NM from the associated NavAid, continuously on the bottom left
corner of each PFD. This display appears as long as a valid DME
frequency has been tuned, regardless of the selected NAV source.
