NEW EPIC FUNCTIONS
ADS-B Out
The EPIC Phase 7 and later system incorporates the new optional XS-
858B XPDR, which supports the ADS-B Out (Automatic Dependant
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Surveillance - Broadcast Out) function. The ADS-B Out transponder
operates at 1090 Mhz and broadcasts periodically (once per second)
the aircraft position, speed and other flight information. This
information can be displayed to an ATC and other aircraft which have
suitable equipment. The equipment satisfies the AMC 20-24, TSO
C166b, RTCA/DO-260B, FAA AC 20-165.
The ADS-B Out transponder (if fitted) transmits the following data sup-
plied by the on board systems and GNSS:
— ADS Pressure Altitude,
— ADS Altitude Rate,
— AHRS Vertical Speed,
— ADS Airspeed,
— AHRS Magnetic Heading,
— AHRS True Heading,
— GPS Sensor Status,
— GPS Latitude - Longitude,
— Aut.Horiz/Vert. Integ Level,
— Horizontal and Vertical Pos FOM,
— N/S and E/W velocity,
— Vertical velocity,
— Horizontal and Vertical Vel. FOM,
— GPS Height.
The control of the ADS-B transponder and IDENT operation is via the
MCDU Radio pages.
Operation and procedures for the ADS-B Transponder can be found in
the Honeywell EPIC Pilot’s Manual latest issue.
Page S79-4 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2957 ===

139G0290X002 later Specific Functions
Optional Additional Landing Gear Alert Message
Specifically for offshore customers an additional logic to trigger the
‘Landing Gear’ caution and aural message, when approaching an oil
rig, for example, is available to be selected in the configuration at the
customers request.
The reason for this additional logic is to prevent late alerting when the
helicopter is already above the oil rig with the landing gear still
retracted. The logic activates the “LANDING GEAR” caution in the
CAS list and the LANDING GEAR aural when the aircraft is
decelerating below 30 kts GS and the landing gear is retracted,
independently from height. When selected this logic activates
additionally and independently to the 150 ft AGL threshold which
remains unchanged.
New CAS Advisory Messages
The Phase 7 and later software includes two new CAS green advisory
messages that are for use with the Enhanced Landing Light
Configuration (Supplement 74). This landing light configuration is
installed, as standard, on aircraft from S/N 31400 onwards and S/N
41300 onwards. The new advisory messages are LANDING LT RH
ON and LANDING LT LH ON that correspond to the LDG LTS panel
and collective switch labels.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

Note
The airspeed at the FAF and MAP, as indicated on the
the Approach Plate being used, must not be exceeded.
Note
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Use of IAS mode is recommended with RNP APCH and
RNP AR APCH approaches below 60 KIAS.
AUTOMATIC FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM LIMITATIONS
RNP operations must be flown using the default Flight Director
coupled mode or by following raw data. Use of Flight Director in
uncoupled mode for RNP operations is not approved.
For RNP APCH approaches with a glide slope angle greater than 7.5
degrees the final approach segment (from FAF to MAP) must be flown
with AFCS approach modes coupled. In case a failure occurs after the
FAF, causing the FD to decouple, the pilot must discontinue the
current approach.
RNP procedures including RF legs must be flown with LNAV Flight
Director mode coupled. In case a failure occurs, causing the FD to
decouple, the pilot must discontinue the current procedure.
FLIGHT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM LIMITATIONS
Use of FMS offset function during RNP 0.3 operations is forbidden.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY AND MALFUNCTION
PROCEDURES
GENERAL
The following malfunction procedures are intended to integrate those
of the basic RFM and, if a Flight Director is used, those of the Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
applicable Supplement installed 67, 69 or 70.
The following malfunction procedures are to be used only during RNP
Operations.
In the specific case of loss of GNSS Navigation information the FMS
system reverts to the remaining navigation sensors, which are not
allowed for use during RNP Operations.
Even when using non-GNSS sensors or in degraded mode (EPU
higher than RNP), the FMS continues to provide navigational position,
groundspeed, and ground track information. The procedure waypoints
still remain displayed in the PFD.

GENERAL INFORMATION
RNP AR APCH Operational approval must be requested by Aircraft
Operator (AO) and granted by the local Competent Authority. A Flight
Operational Safety Assessment (FOSA) methodology is used.
The FOSA must account for the fact that a loss of GNSS reception (in
case of loss of GNSS satellites view or dual GNSS receiver failure)
has, as a consequence, the loss of RNAV and RNP capabilities.
In case of loss of RNP capability during RNP AR operations, the flight
crew must discontinue the approach, unless the pilot has runway
visual references in sight.
In this case, the relevant and specific contingency procedures
(assessed in the FOSA) must be applied to terminate the RNP
navigation and revert to conventional navigation or apply specific ATC
instructions.
For all navigation specification listed in Table 1, except for LPV
approaches, the FMS (selected as Navigation Source) computes
lateral path deviation/guidance by using available sensors for position
computation. The lateral deviation computed by FMS is used as input
for LNAV Flight Director Mode.
Page S80-20
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 2991 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 80
Document N° RNP Operations
139G0290X002 (EPIC Phase 7 and later)
For approaches with LNAV, LNAV/VNAV and RNP 0.3 minima/MA 1.0,
FMS uses baro VNAV to compute vertical path deviation/guidance.
The vertical deviation computed by FMS is used as input for VGP
flight director mode.
For the specific case of LPV approaches, lateral and vertical deviation/
guidance are directly computed by GPS, based upon the FAS data
block defining the approach path. These deviations are used as input
of NLOC / NGS flight director modes, respectively.
Intercept of the final approach segment may be performed either flying
an approach transition or through vectoring.

As an aid to the pilot for RNP AR APCH approaches, an expanded
lateral deviation scale is added on PFD below the ADI.
The scale is displayed in the approach and missed approach (except
for holdings) phases of RNP AR APCH approaches. The lateral
deviation pointer is scaled as a function of FMS RNP, such that the
full scale deflection is equal to the active RNP value. The winglets
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
starting at the center of the triangle pointer are sized according to the
current EPU.
When within RNP limit, the lateral deviation pointer with winglet is
displayed in cyan for non-coupled side and in magenta for coupled
side.
When the lateral deviation pointer with winglet exceeds the RNP
value, it will be displayed in amber and flash initially. Correspondingly
a “RNP RNP” aural alert will be played.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The Honeywell MK XXII EGPWS is an optional system providing
Ground Proximity Warning and Terrain Awareness functions. Five soft-
ware version of the EGPWS are available -024, -026, -030, -034 and -
036.
The basic functionalities are identical for all version of the Primus
EPIC, however, additional functionalities are available depending of
the EGPWS version and EPIC Phase software installed.
Refer to Table 1 for details of software differences.
The EGPWS provides the pilot with the following Basic functionalities:
— Terrain and obstacle awareness display
— Voice alerts/warnings/call outs
— Visual Caution and Warning messages.
This information is provided through two independent functions:
1. Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS)
This function is based primarily on the vertical separation of the
helicopter with terrain. It uses altitude and altitude rates/terrain
closure rates to alert to insufficient terrain clearance. There are
six operating modes:
Mode 1: Excessive Descent Rate
Mode 2. Excessive Terrain Closure Rate
Mode 3: Descent after Take-Off
Additional for -036 only:
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters Mode 3B, Loss of Airspeed after Take-Off
Mode 4: Unsafe terrain clearance
Mode 4A: Cruise and approach with landing gear up
Mode 4B: Cruise and approach with landing gear down
Mode 4C: Take-Off with landing gear up.
Mode 5: Descent Below Glideslope
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S81-1
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 3004 ===
Supplement 81 AW139 - RFM - 4D
EGPWS Document N°
MK XXII 139G0290X002
Mode 6: Advisory alerts for Excessive Bank Angle, Tail Too Low,
and Altitude call outs in Autorotation.
2. Terrain Awareness Display and “Look Ahead” alerting and
warning.
This function uses information from the GPS and other sources
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
on the aircraft to calculate horizontal position and vertical altitude.
This data provides a three dimensional position for the aircraft.
This position is then compared to the terrain database and if a
conflict with terrain or a known obstacle is imminent the system
provides an alert.
The MK XXII-030,-034,-036 versions when installed with EPIC Phase
7 also includes dedicated options (selectable on system installation),
Offshore mode and SAR mode.
The EGPWS is compliant with TSO C194.
EGPWS FUNCTIONALITY
The following table summarises the functional differences between the
PRIMUS EPIC software version and the EGPWS software version
combinations.

SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
WEIGHT AND CG LIMITATIONS
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
After EGPWS system installation, the new empty weight and CG
location must be determined.
BUILD STANDARD
For EGPWS functionalities and compatibilities with PRIMUS EPIC
software release, refer to Table 1.
EGPWS LIMITATIONS
— EGPWS must not be used for navigation.
CAUTION
The Terrain and Obstacle display is intended to serve as
a terrain and obstacle awareness tool only. The display
and database may not provide the accuracy and fidelity
on which to base routine navigation decisions and plan
routes to avoid terrain or obstacles.
— Customised EGPWS modes (LOW ALT, SAR, OFFSHORE) shall
not be selected when carrying out conventional, approved IFR
procedures.
Note
LOW ALT, SAR and OFFSHORE EGPWS Modes are
intended to be used during these specialised operations.
They de-sensitise the basic EGPWS envelope so are not
appropriate for use in the conventional IFR infrastructure.
They should only be selected as required during the
appropriate specialised operation, to avoid nuisance
warnings.

— Obstacle : A human made structure, higher than 100 ft AGL
— Offshore : Operations Offshore
— SA : Situational Awareness
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
— SAR : Operations SAR

outputs:
Terrain/Obstacle Awareness Display (TAD)

This information is provided through two independent functions:
1. Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS)
(Voice/Visual alert and callouts only)
2. Terrain Awareness Display with “Look-Ahead” Alerting
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
and Warning.
The EGPWS (GPWS and TAWS) uses information from the GPS and
other sources on the aircraft to calculate horizontal position and
vertical altitude. In particular the system merges barometric pressure,
Radio Altitude and a GPS derived altitude into a so-called “Geometric
Altitude” to provide more accurate altitude information less susceptible
to errors induced by pilot (altimeter settings), cold temperature or
malfunctions in altimeters systems.

GROUND PROXIMITY WARNING SYSTEM
The ground proximity system is based primarily on the vertical
separation of the helicopter with the terrain. It uses radio and
barometric altitude to determine altitude rates/terrain closure rates to
alert for insufficient terrain clearance. There are 6 modes:
Mode 1: Excessive Descent Rate
Mode 2: Excessive Terrain Closure Rate
Mode 3: Descent after take-off / Loss of Airspeed after Take-Off
Mode 4: Unsafe terrain clearance
Mode 5: Descent below Glideslope
Mode 6: Advisory Alerts for the following functions
• Excessive bank angle
• Tail too low
• Altitude call-outs in autorotation
MODE 1: Excessive Rate of Descent
For excessive rate of descent a voice alert “SINK RATE” will be heard
and the amber caution caption ‘GND PROX’ will appear on the ADI. If
the helicopter continues the high rate of descent the same voice alert
will be repeated at an increasing frequency. Should the helicopter
penetrate the defined warning boundary, the voice alert “PULL UP” will
be heard continuously and the red warning message “PULL UP” will
appear on the ADI.
When -036 installed and OFFSHORE selected the Mode 1 boundaries
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
are modified.
When -036 installed Mode 1 alerts are disabled during Take-Off, in
Autorotation and for the LOW ALT and SAR mode.
When -036 installed the Mode 1 alerts are disabled when in OEI
conditions.
Page S81-19
Rev. 26

=== DOC PAGE 3022 ===
Supplement 81 AW139 - RFM - 4D
EGPWS Document N°
MK XXII 139G0290X002
MODE 2: Excessive terrain closure rate
When the helicopter is closing with the terrain at an excessive rate
(descending, level flight or even climb) the aural message “TERRAIN
TERRAIN” is generated and the amber caution “GND PROX” is shown
on the ADI. If the helicopter continues to penetrate the defined
envelope the aural message “PULL UP” is repeated continuously and
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
the red warning “PULL UP” is shown on the ADI.
The envelope is de-sensitized for three situations (called Mode 2B):
1 Landing gear is down
2 Aircraft is performing ILS approach
3 within 60 seconds after take-off.
The aural warning “TERRAIN” and a visual alert amber message
“GND PROX” is displayed on the ADI, and remains until the defined
envelope is exited. During autorotation, for the LOW ALT, SAR and
OFFSHORE Modes the Mode 2 alerts are disabled.
MODE 3: Loss of Altitude After Take-Off
This function provides alerts when the aircraft loses significant altitude
during Take-Off or Go-Around and the landing gear has been selected
up, or when the airspeed exceeds 50 KIAS. The alert boundary
depends on the elapsed time since Take-Off and the amount of
altitude loss. If the boundary is violated an aural warning ‘DON’T
SINK’ is generated with the visual message “GND PROX” on the ADI,
which remains until a positive rate of climb is established.
This function is inhibited in LOW ALT mode when above 100 ft AGL.
For version -036 this mode is modified and subdivided into two forms:
Mode 3A: Loss of altitude after take-off (inhibited in OEI).
If OFFSHORE mode selected then Mode 3A only
active for 60 seconds after Take-Off
Mode 3B: Excessive loss of airspeed after Take-off (inhibited in
LOW ALT mode).
If OFFSHORE mode selected then Mode 3B only
active for 60 seconds after Take-Off.
Page S81-20
Rev. 26

Document N ° EGPWS
139G0290X002 MK XXII
Mode 3B has an aural ‘CHECK AIRSPEED’ caution when the
aircraft airspeed reduced below 55 kt after Take-Off
and having attained 60 kt. The caution remains
active until the airspeed exceeds 60 kt or
60 seconds has expired.
MODE 4: Unsafe Terrain Clearance.
This function provides alerts for insufficient terrain clearance with
respect to phase of flight and speed. This mode is subdivided in three
forms:
Mode 4A: Cruise and approach with landing gear up
Mode 4B: Cruise and approach with landing gear down
Mode 4C: Take-Off with landing gear up.
Mode 4A • For -024 and -026, below 150 ft radio altitude aural "TOO
LOW GEAR", below 100 KIAS and “TOO LOW TERRAIN”
above 100 KIAS. (in Low Alt mode only “TOO LOW
GEAR” below 100 ft and 60 KIAS)
• For -030 and -034, below 150 ft radio altitude “TOO LOW
TERRAIN” above 60 KIAS (in Low Alt Inhibit)
• For -036, below 150 ft radio altitude only “TOO LOW
TERRAIN” above 60 KIAS (in Low Alt Inhibit)
(in OFSH when below 350 ft, “TOO LOW GEAR” below
100 KIAS and “TOO LOW TERRAIN” above 100 KIAS).
Mode 4B has an aural ‘TOO LOW TERRAIN’ caution for speeds
above 120 KIAS and altitudes below 100 ft AGL. For
speeds between 120 KIAS and 80 KIAS this boundary
reduces from 100 to 10 ft AGL.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
When -036 installed and OFFSHORE mode selected the
Mode 4B boundaries are modified.
Mode 4C provides an aural ‘TOO LOW TERRAIN’ when the radio
altitude enters the minimum terrain clearance value,
landing gear up or airspeed greater than 50 KIAS.
For the SAR mode the Mode 4 alerts are disabled.

MODE 5: Excessive glideslope deviation
This function provides two levels of audio alerting when the aircraft
flight path descends below the Glideslope beam on front course ILS
approaches or LPV approaches (for -030 and later). The first alert is
generated when the aircraft descends more than 1.3 dots below the
beam. An audio ‘GLIDESLOPE’ caution is generated with
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
approximately half volume compared to the other alerts. When the
aircraft descends below 300 ft (radio altimeter) and with greater than 2
dots deviation the audio ‘GLIDESLOPE’ caution is generated with
standard volume level.
MODE 6: Advisory Alerts
The following Advisory Alerts are configured:
1 Excessive Bank Angle. An audio alert ‘BANK ANGLE’ is
generated for exceedances of the the bank angle boundary.
The boundary between 10 ft and 50 ft AGL is 30° of bank
which then slopes up to 45° of bank at 500 feet AGL. The
slope steepens to 55° at 1000 feet AGL, then remains
constant at 55°.
2 Excessive Pitch angle (Tail Strike). An audio alert ‘TAIL TOO
LOW’ is generated for exceedences of the boundary that
starts at 15° of aircraft pitch-up at 3 feet AGL and slopes up to
48.5° pitch-up at 50 feet AGL.
3 Autorotation call-outs and generated when the aircraft is in
autorotation at the following radio altimeter heights: ‘200’,
‘100’, ‘80’, ‘60’, ‘40’, ‘20’, ‘10’.

TERRAIN AWARENESS FUNCTIONS
The Mk XXII computer uses following aircraft inputs:
Radio Altitude
Roll and Pitch Attitude
Baro Altitude and Vertical Speed
Ground Speed and track
Localizer and Glide Slope
Engine torque
Airspeed and OAT
GPS signal quality
Gear position and Weight on Wheels
Magnetic Heading
Display range
to determine the aircraft’s 3-D position and create a safe envelope
forward of its flight path. The envelope is then compared with a terrain
and obstacle database to generate warnings and cautions when these
boundaries are violated.
For all EPIC Phases up to and including Phase 7:
The Terrain Awareness Display depicts the terrain in front of the
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
aircraft as variable density dot patterns in green, yellow and red.
When terrain awareness alerts are generated, the threatening terrain
is painted solid yellow or red. The display includes numerical values of
minimum and maximum elevation of the displayed terrain.
Page S81-23
Rev. 26

TERRAIN DISPLAY
For all EPIC Phases up to and including Phase 7:
The Terrain Display presented on the PFD and MFD uses the colours,
green, yellow and red, to indicate the following:
Green: terrain/obstacles are at least 250 ft below the aircraft
altitude and there is a safe terrain/obstacle clearance.
Yellow: terrain is from 250 ft below to 500 ft above the aircraft
altitude. The helicopter may not have a safe terrain clearance.
Red: terrain is at least 500 ft above the helicopter altitude. The
helicopter does not have safe terrain clearance and may not
be able to escape this terrain.

SYSTEM OPERATIONS
The system is powered continously and during normal flight
operations it remains essentially silent and, if selected on the PFD HSI
or/and MFD MAP page, the terrain colour display will be present.
EGPWS SELF TEST FUNCTION
The following procedure can be used to initiate the self test function
for determining a serviceable system:
— Select TAWS display on MFD MAP page and PFD HSI.
— Select TAWS self test ON and confirm the following:
• TAWS TEST message displayed on PFD and MFD.
• TERR N/A (or TAWS N/A) message displayed momentarily on
PFD.
• TAWS LOW ALT advisory displayed momentarily on CAS.
• TAWS AUDIO MUTE and TAWS GS CANCEL advisories
display momentarily on CAS.
• GLIDESLOPE and PULL UP audio messages heard by pilot and
copilot.
• Terrain Display Self Test pattern displayed on MFD and PFD
or for EPIC Phase 8 with -034 or -036 SA Terrain on PFD and
MFD terrain colour brightness changes from low to high.
• WARNING! TERRAIN audio message is heard by pilot and
copilot.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
— On conclusion of the test confirm Terrain Self Test pattern is turned
off and no TAWS messages remain.

Terrain Awareness and ‘Look-Ahead’ Alerting
When the “Look-Ahead” function detects a terrain or obstacle threat
approximately 30 seconds ahead of the helicopter, the voice alert
“Caution Terrain, Caution Terrain” (or “Caution Obstacle, Caution
Obstacle”) is given and the threat area is painted solid yellow on the
terrain display. Should the helicopter flight path continue toward the
threat area, the alert message will be repeated approximately every
7 seconds. If the helicopter path approaches to within approximately
20 seconds of the threat area, the voice message turns to “Warning
Terrain, Warning Terrain” (or “Warning Obstacle, Warning Obstacle”)
and will be given continuously while the threat area will be shown in a
bright, solid red colour.
The system uses the turn rate and direction to predict the aircraft flight
path. Forward speed is also used to modify the look-ahead envelope.
Below 100 knots the envelope is reduced until it is completely inhibited
below 70 knots.
The control of the various functions of the EGPWS is via a dedicated
page (TAWS) under the MENU button on the MCDU.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

139G0290X002 System II (TCAS II)
GENERAL INFORMATION
The TPA 100B is an onboard Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance
System (TCAS II) which monitors a radius of nominal 14 NM around
the helicopter by interrogating any intruding aircraft transponder and
determining if a potential conflict with other aircraft exists.
The system comprises of a TCAS II processor installed in the aft
avionic bay and two directional antennas one mounted on the top
surface within the nose radome and the second rear antenna is
mounted under the rear part of the aircraft belly. The system is
interfaced and controlled by the PRIMUS EPIC software version 7 or
later.
The TCAS II system interrogates ICAO compliant transponders of
aircraft in the vicinity and based on replies received computes the
relative range, altitude (if included in the reply message), bearing and
closure rate of other transponder equipped aircraft with respect to the
helicopter. The TCAS II calculates the time to reach the Closest Point
of Approach (CPA) with the intruder, this time value is the main
parameter for issuing alerts. If the transponder replies from nearby
aircraft includes their altitude, the TCAS II computes the time to reach
co-altitude.
TCAS II issues two types of alerts:
— TAs (Traffic Advisory) to assist the visual search for the intruder
aircraft and prepare the pilot for a potential RA,
— RAs (Resolution Advisory) to define manoeuvres that will either
increase or maintain the existing vertical separation from the
intruder aircraft. When the intruder aircraft is also fitted with
TCAS II, both TCAS II systems coordinate their RAs through the
Mode S data link to ensure that complementary resolution senses
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
are selected.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S82-1
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 3046 ===
Supplement 82 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Traffic Advisory Document N°
System II (TCAS II) 139G0290X002
RESOLUTION ADVISORY MANOUVRES
The pilot action on activation of a Resolution Advisory is to initiate
immediately a climb or descent as dictated by the TCAS II Resolution
Advisory. The technique to achieve the requested climb or descend
rate will be dependant on the initial flight conditions such as airspeed,
altitude, weight, AFCS modes engaged etc.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
On activation of a RA the pilot should not initiate banking manoeuvres
but attempt to fly the aircraft in accordance with the indication
displayed on the VSI.
Note
To manoeuvre the aircraft for compliance with a RA the
cyclic and collective FTR buttons should be pressed and,
if FD modes are engaged, held pressed throughout the
entire manoeuvring phase to maintain the IAS and
Vertical mode bugs synchronized with the actual
airspeed and altitude.
When a ‘CLIMB’ Resolution Advisory is generated initiate immediately
a climb to achieve the rate of climb as dictated by the TCAS II.
The following airspeed and power considerations should be taken into
account:
— If airspeed is above 80 KIAS initiate climb using cyclic to reduce
airspeed towards but not below 80 KIAS, whilst simultaneously
applying MCP 100% PI, or TOP 110% PI when below 90 KIAS,
using collective.
— If airspeed is 80 KIAS or below initiate climb using collective to
apply TOP 110% PI whilst allowing IAS to increase towards but
not above 80 KIAS.
— If the required climb rate cannot be achieved, maintain the
maximum achievable within the aircraft limits.
— Following the ‘CLEAR OF CONFLICT’ advisory, the aircraft should
be returned promptly to the applicable clearance unless otherwise
directed by ATC.
Page S82-2 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 3047 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 82
Document N ° Traffic Advisory
139G0290X002 System II (TCAS II)
When a ‘DESCENT’ Resolution Advisory is generated then:
— initiate immediately a descent to achieve the rate of descent as
dictated by the TCAS II using collective to decrease the torque
setting as required, but not entering into autorotation (minimum
10% PI).
— If the required descent rate cannot be achieved, maintain the max-
imum descent rate respecting the aircraft limits.
— Following the ‘CLEAR OF CONFLICT’ advisory, the aircraft should
be returned promptly to the applicable clearance unless otherwise
directed by ATC.
The TCAS II continues to monitor the flight paths of conflicting aircraft
following an RA. If the aircraft flight paths are different from those
required, the TCAS II can issue a new RA to maximize separation. If
this occurs follow the revised RA.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
TYPE OF OPERATION
The TPA 100B is approved for VFR and IFR operation as an aid to vis-
ually acquiring traffic and indicates the vertical manoeuvre necessary
to avoid conflicting traffic.
WEIGHT AND CG LIMITATIONS
After TCAS II system installation, the new empty weight and CG loca-
tion must be determined.
TCAS II SYSTEM LIMITATIONS
— The pilot must not manoeuvre the helicopter based only on Traffic
Advisory (TA) or on information displayed on the traffic display.
— The pilot is authorized to deviate from the current ATC clearance
to comply with a TCAS II Resolution Advisory (RA).
— The pilot is not authorized to exceed aircraft flight envelope limits
based on Resolution Advisory (RA) alarms.
— When the undercarriage is extended the TCAS II lower antenna
operates in omnidirectional mode. Therefore, when the intruder
aircraft is below the helicopter, bearing information is not available.
— TCAS II must be selected to TA ONLY mode during underslung
load operations.
— The following inhibits are active:
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

inhibited below 1000 ft AGL while descending

nominally between 1500 and 2000 fpm )

completed)

(Climb at the rate depicted by the green (fly to) arc on VSI
nominally between 1500 and 2000 fpm. Safe separation will be
best achieved by climbing through the threats flight path)

(Descend at the rate depicted by the green (fly to) arc on the VSI
nominally between 1500 and 2000 fpm. Safe separation will be
best achieved by descending through the threats flight path)

(Continue the existing climb or descent rate, or other vertical
speed, as depicted by the green (fly to) arc on VSI. Safe
separation will be best achieved by not altering the existing
vertical speed and climbing or descending through the threats
flight path)

SECTION 7 - SYSTEM DESCRIPTION
INTRODUCTION
TCAS II (Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System) is an airborne
system used for detecting and tracking traffic near the helicopter.
TCAS II includes a TCAS II processor, antennas, a traffic display
(MFD) and a means to control the system (CCD-MCDU).
The TCAS II system interrogates ICAO compliant transponders of
aircraft in the vicinity and based on replies received computes the
relative range, altitude (if included in the reply message), bearing and
closure rate of other transponder equipped aircraft with respect to the
helicopter. The TCAS II calculates the time to reach the Closest Point
of Approach (CPA) with the intruder, this time value is the main
parameter for issuing alerts. If the transponder replies from nearby
aircraft includes their altitude, the TCAS II computes the time to reach
co-altitude.
TCAS II issues two types of alerts:
— TAs (Traffic Advisory) to assist the visual search for the intruder
aircraft and prepare the pilot for a potential RA,
— RAs (Resolution Advisory) to define manoeuvres that will either
increase or maintain the existing vertical separation from the
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
intruder aircraft. When the intruder aircraft is also fitted with
TCAS II, both TCAS II systems coordinate their RAs through the
Mode S data link to ensure that complementary resolution senses
are selected
The vertical RAs given are calculated and given against intruder
aircraft that report altitude data in their transponder messages while,
for non altitude reporting (NAR) aircraft only TAs are given.
Page S82-17
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 3064 ===
Supplement 82 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Traffic Advisory Document N°
System II (TCAS II) 139G0290X002
When TA-RA mode selected, the operating Sensitivity Level (SL) is
automatically selected via inputs from the aircraft’s radar or pressure
altimeter. SL2 will be selected when the TCAS aircraft is below 1,000
feet above ground level (AGL) (±100 feet) as determined by the RAD
ALT input, in SL2, RAs are inhibited and only TAs will be issued. See
Figure 7-1.

2. TA: Traffic Alert with Transponder Mode C operation.

TRAFFIC ADVISORY DISPLAY
The TCAS II displays an intruder aircraft symbol on the traffic advisory
display. The symbol position on the display shows relative range and
bearing of the intruder. The symbols shape and colours, provided by
TCAS II system, identifies the category of the intruder as nonthreat
(OT), Proximity (PT), Traffic Advisory (TA) or Resolution Advisory
(RA), as shown in Figure 7-5. If the intruder is reporting altitude,
intruder relative altitude is shown on the display near the threat traffic
symbol. The relative altitude data tag consist of two digits indicating
hundreds of feet with the same color as the corresponding traffic sym-
bol.
The symbols change shape and colour as separation decreases
between the helicopter’s and Intruder’s to represent increasing levels
of urgency.
The traffic symbols may also have an associated altitude tag that
shows relative altitude in hundreds of feet.
A + sign and number above the symbol means the Intruder is above
the helicopter altitude.

The TCAS II system is able to display also the Flight Level (absolute
altitude), of the intruder aircraft, in place of the relative altitude, when
selected from the MAP drop down menu. The absolute altitude is cal-
culate by adding the relative altitude provided by the intruder TCAS II
to own aircraft's barometric altitude. Absolute altitude consists of three
digits indicating hundreds of feet. Absolute altitude is replaced with rel-
ative altitude after 15 seconds or whenever a TA or RA condition is
encountered. When absolute altitude is selected, a green annuncia-
tion "FLT LEVEL" is located in the MFDs TCAS status window. In the
event that a TA or RA target is encountered, that does not have a
bearing available for display, the information for that target is dis-
played in two text lines above the TCAS status window. The first line
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters will contain data for the highest priority no bearing target and the sec-
ond line will contain data for the second highest priority no bearing tar-
get.

will be automatically enabled for display on the MFD map and pilot or
copilot can display TCAS II information by simply pressing enter on

RESOLUTION ADVISORY DISPLAY
The RAs are shown superimposed on the vertical Speed indication on
the PFDs, see Figure 7-6. The RA visual advisory provides the pilot
with information on the vertical speed to fly, or avoid, in order to
resolve a potential conflict. The RA advisory on the vertical speed tape
is depicted with red and green bands to indicate the vertical speeds to
be avoided (red) and the desired vertical speed to be flown (green)
and the Vertical speed digital readout is deleted. In addition, a TRAF-
FIC text is shown in the upper left corner of the attitude sphere during
TA and RA condition, in amber (TA) or red (RA) colours dependent on
the advisory type. RED and AMBER TRAFFIC annunciation share the
same location on PFD. In the event that both an amber and a red
"TRAFFIC" annunciation are present, the red "TRAFFIC” is displayed.
This position is also used to display the “TA ONLY” annunciation when
the altitude is below 1000 ft an RA is not allowed or when the Pilots
has selected TA only mode.

SELF TEST
The self-test function of TCAS II subsystem can be activated by
selecting the XPDR/TCAS page on the MCDU then selecting the
TEST line select key. A ‘TEST’ caption illuminates in the ACTIVE field
of the MCDU page.
The self test determines the operational status of the entire TCAS II Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
system. Once begun, self test continues automatically for approxi-
mately eight seconds.
During self test, normal TCAS II operation is inhibited.
For the test a range of 2.5 nm (half range 1.25) should be selected
and the test generates the symbols arranged as shown.
The traffic display annunciates the phrase “TCAS TEST”.
ICN-39-A-155025-A-00003-00860-A-01-1
A Resolution Advisory (filled red square) wil appear at 3 o’clock, range
2 miles 1000 feet below flying level.
A Traffic Advisory (filled yellow circle) will appear at 9 o’clock, range of
2 miles, 200 feet below and climbing.
Selecting the 5 nm range (half range 2.5) during the test allows the
proximity traffic (filled cyan diamond) to be seen at 1 o’clock, range 3.6
miles, 200 feet above, descending and Non-Threat traffic (open cyan
diamond) to be seen at 11 o’clock, range of 3.6 miles, flying level
1000 feet above.

139G0290X002 Searchlight
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Trakkabeam series of searchlight are high intensity external light
source installed on a gimbal support on the left hand side of the
helicopter. It is used to provide high intensity external lighting for
reconnaissance operations during night time operations.
This Supplement gives instruction on the Trakkabeam series including
the A800 searchlight installation P/N 4G3340F02411 and
4G3340F02413 (non NVG) and P/N 4G3340F02412 and
4G3340F02414 (NVG), and the TLX version P/N 4G3340F03011,
both of which include the capability to slave the searchlight operation
to a FLIR.
The searchlight ranges of movements are shown below:
P/N 4G3340F02411 and P/N 4G3340F02412:
Elevation ................................................................-26 deg to -120 deg
Azimuth ............................................... 180 deg to right, 180 deg to left
P/N 4G3340F02413, P/N 4G3340F02414 and P/N 4G3340F03011:
Elevation ................................................................... -142 deg to 0 deg
Azimuth ................................................... 1 deg to right, 151 deg to left
The installation consists of the searchlight with a 800W lamp, gimbal
support (Figure 1), a Power Conditioning Interface Unit (PCIU), a
Cockpit Controller (Figure 2 to Figure 4), Pendant Grip Controller
(Figure 5) and all necessary hardware and cabling.
The searchlight unit has an integrated optical filter system which
provides the option for different light beam filter colours including infra-
red depending on customer requirements. The filters are easily
selectable during flight via the cockpit and pendant controllers.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The PCIU is the central power and control hub for the entire system,
aircraft power supply (28VDC) is converted and distributed to each
item in the system. The PCIU performs all gimbal position control, filter
selection, light zoom and lamp on/off control and provides an interface
to the cockpit control unit, hand controller and interfacing for FLIR
slaving capability.
The Cockpit Controller unit includes all switches for searchlight power
ON/OFF, function selection and provides displays to indicate filter
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S83-1
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 3082 ===
Supplement 83 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Trakkabeam Series Document N°
Searchlight 139G0290X002
number and current system status. The controller does not have a
joystick for light direction (except the TLX version), however, inputs
are available for light azimuth and elevation control by collective
landing light 5 way switch inputs.
The Pendant Grip Controller also provides switches for searchlight
power ON/OFF, function selection and provides displays to indicate
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
filter number and current system status. The Pendant Controller also
includes a joystick to control the light azimuth and elevation. Selection
of the Pendant Grip Controller to operate the system is via the Cockpit
controller.
TRAKKABEAM OPERATION
On the cockpit controller selecting the SYS (PWR) switch to ON the
system performs Power-On-Self-Test (POST). This should take
around 12 seconds, however, if the gimbal has not been stowed
previously before power down or the searchlight hit the mechanical
stops during the previous flight, it will take 60 seconds. Upon
completion of the POST, the searchlight will travel to the STOW
position and the STOW light will flash while the searchlight is moving
then steady when it is in the STOW position. The searchlight will only
respond to the DEPLOY command when in the STOW position, no
other buttons will function. Depressing the DEPLOY switch will move
and point the searchlight in a preset direction ready for turning the
lamp ON. When in DEPLOY, all of the control functions become
active. To start the lamp the ARM switch, on the cockpit controller,
must be selected ON then by depressing the Lamp ON/OFF button
the lamp illuminates and extinguished by depressing the Lamp ON/
OFF switch again.
The searchlight filter may be selected prior to starting the lamp or any
time after the lamp has been ignited. The filter is changed by depress
the FILTER SEL switch until the display shows the desired position
number and then select the FILTER ENT switch to activate.
During the POST process, the filter wheel will rotate to the preset
HOME position (normally white light position).
Moving the ZOOM switch a wider beam or a narrow beam can be
selected.
Page S83-2 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 3083 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 83
Document N° Trakkabeam Series
139G0290X002 Searchlight
The searchlight is directed by either the pilot or copilot collective
joystick as selected by the PILOT/COPILOT/CREW switch on the
controller or, for the TLX version, the joystick on the cockpit controller.
Moving the joystick to the left or right for azimuth control and up or
down for elevation control. The azimuth and elevation speed
increases as the joystick is moved further to it maximum deflection.
When CREW is selected the control is handed over to the Pendant
Controller which has similar functioning buttons and a joystick to
control searchlight direction.
Selecting the SLAVE mode the searchlight will track the movement of
the host equipment e.g. FLIR (if installed). When operating in the
SLAVE mode, the system will still respond to all the manual controls
while the joystick control is used to adjust for parallax error and align
the searchlight beam to the FLIR target if required.

139G0290X002 LiDAR System
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Obstacle Proximity LiDAR System (OPLS) presents to the pilot a
visual and audio indication of obstacle distances around the aircraft
while in hovering or low speed flight.
The system comprises of three Laser Imaging Detection and Ranging
Units (LiDAR) mounted around the aircraft transmission cowling below
the rotor head, a processing unit and audio/video adapters mounted in
the rear avionics bay, a control panel mounted in the interseat console
(see Figure 2) and all necessary hardware and cabling (see Figure 1).
The LiDAR units generate digital distance profiles of the surrounding
environment using a low-power, eye safe laser beam and receiver.
The distance information from the three overlapping beams are digi-
tally mixed in the processors to produce a 360° obstacle coverage, in
the plane of the sensor units, around the helicopter, see Figure 3 for
sensor footprint (Note: no obstacles above or below the plane or the
sensor units is detected).
The information from the processor can then be displayed on the MFD
th
or central 5 display (depending on customization) using a helicopter
plan view representation with the obstacle profile on a polar grid with
range captions. The critical (minimum) distance to the nearest obsta-
cle is indicated by a colour coded radial line and the distance given at
the top of the display. Three colour bands are used for indicating criti-
cality, Green (safe), Yellow (caution) and Red (critical), see Figure 4.
In addition to the colour coded indication an audio tone is also heard in
the intercom which increases in frequency as the distance decreases.
An audio annunciation is heard passing from Green to Yellow
“APPROACHING” and from Yellow to Red “CHECK DISTANCE”
zones.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters The OPLS Controller (Figure 2) is used to switch the system ON and
OFF and gives an indication of system status OFF/STBY/ON/ERROR.
The audio tone and annunciations can also be selected to MUTE with
an indication when in MUTE. The MUTE function can be selected
when in the yellow band by either pressing the MUTE button on the
panel or the CAS RST button on the collective. (The MUTE function
does not activate if selected whilst in the Green or Red band).
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S84-1
Rev. 22

audio is automatically reactivated.
The OPLS obstacle display is selected on the MFD using the cursor
control device selecting the SYSTEM VIDEO selection.

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 85
Document N ° Batteries in
139G0290X002 Parallel Kit
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Batteries in Parallel (Improved Engine Starting) Kit P/N
4G2430F00811 introduces an improvement to engine starting on bat-
tery by connecting the MAIN and AUXILIARY batteries in parallel dur-
ing the engine starting phase for battery only starts and when the
aircraft is on the ground. Starting from External power or generator
assisted cross-start from the opposite engine started generator are
unchanged.
The installation of this kit also requires the 44 Ah Main Battery P/N
4G2430F00512 and the 27 Ah Auxiliary Battery P/N 4G2430F00114
to be installed.
The kit comprises of a relay in the Electrical Power Generation and
Distribution System that is activated by the ENG MODE switch. When
either ENG MODE switch is selected to GI or FLT the relay is closed
connecting the two batteries in parallel for the engine starting phase.
When closed the relay activates the BATT OFF LINE caution to indi-
cate to the pilot that the relay has closed and the batteries are con-
nected in parallel for the starting. The system also includes two DC/
DC converters that guarantee uninterrupted power to the ESSential
busses during the start sequence.
After the engine start phase has completed the relay is automatically
opened separating the batteries, extinguishing the BATT OFF LINE
caution and the power to the ESSential busses are provided by the
aircraft primary connections.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S85-1
Rev. 9

Document N ° Engine Air Inlet
139G0290X002 Barrier Filter
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Engine Air Inlet Barrier Filter (IBF) P/N 4G7160F00111 protects
the engine against ingestion of sand, dust and other particles.
The system consists of two (2) filter assemblies, one mounted onto
each engine cowling (Figure 1) and an IBF Control Panel (Figure 2)
mounted in the interseat console to allows the pilot to test the filter
system and manually activate the Bypass Doors.
The filter assemblies consists and upper and lower filter made of a
multi-layered gauze between stainless steel screens. The gauze is
saturated with a specially formulated oil which traps the dust/dirt parti-
cles but allows the air to pass through with a low pressure drop. The
pressure drop across the screens is monitored by a pressure probe
and when it reaches a predetermined value, due to the filters being
clogged with dust/dirt, then this is indicated to the pilot by an ‘1(2)
EAPS PRESS’ caution on the CAS. A By-Pass door can then be man-
ually operated by the pilot from the cockpit control panel which illumi-
nates the ‘1(2) EAPS ON’ CAS green advisory to highlight to the pilot
the By-pass door is open.
The gauze filters can subsequently be removed and cleaned to
restore filtering capability. A Filter Maintenance Aid is also incorpo-
rated into the installation which registers the highest pressure drop
across the filters during the last flight to aid maintenance of the filters
and permit cleaning in a timely manner.
If dusty/dirty conditions are not envisaged then the filters can removed
and a FOD screen mounted 4G7160F00112.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S86-1
Rev. 12

HEIGHT- VELOCITY LIMITATIONS
The Height-Velocity diagram defines, in the event of a single engine
failure during take off, landing or other operation near the surface, a
combination of airspeed and height above ground from which a safe
single engine landing on a smooth, level and hard surface cannot be
assured.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
CAUTION
Prior to the determination of the H-V envelope the CATE-
GORY B weight with IBF Installed, should be defined for
the ambient conditions. See Flight Planning in Basic RFM
Section 2 for use of the CAT B W.A.T. and H-V envelope
charts.
Height Velocity Chart IBF Installed or in By-Pass .................Figure 1-3
IBF LIMITATIONS
No mixing of Filter and FOD screens is permitted.
FOD SCREEN LIMITATIONS
When the FOD screens are installed the aircraft flight envelope and
performance returns to the Basic RFM or applicable Supplement.

SECTION 4 - PERFORMANCE
This section includes the performance data for the AW139 helicopter
equipped with Inlet Barrier Filter and with Heating and Air Conditioning
Systems.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The presence of the IBF causes an increase of power losses due to a
pressure reduction at the engine intake.
Thus, whenever the IBF is installed, the helicopter performance is
reduced when compared to the basic configuration with no particle
separators installed.
This performance is also valid when the IBF is installed and selected
to By-Pass.
The performace provided considers the most penalizing condition.
ENGINE POWER CHECKS
The purpose of the Engine Power Assurance Check is to provide a
means of monitoring engine health. A HOVER power assurance
check procedure, with the IBF fitted, is provided to the operator. The
procedure should be used to check if the engine power available
before take-off is within the limits established for the legitimate use of
the Rotorcraft Flight Manual performance.
POWER MARGIN TREND MONITORING
A separate trend diagram is required with IBF fitted.
Fuel Consumption
When the IBF is installed the fuel consumption may increased up to
3.5% for the same torque value compared to the Basic aircraft or
appropriate Supplement.
Page S86-14 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 12

HOVER CEILING
The Hover Ceiling charts define the maximum weights at which an
IGE hover (at 5 ft wheel height) or an OGE hover is possible for vary-
ing combinations of Pressure Altitude and OAT with main rotor speed
at 100% and zero wind conditions.
The performance effect of the IBF is presented for All Engines Operat-
ing (AEO) at Maximum Continuous Power (MCP) and Take Off Power
(TOP) with the HEATER OFF and ON.
The performance effect with the IBF installed is presented for OEI
Maximum Continuous Power (MCP) and 2.5 minute Power.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S86-17
Rev. 12

=== DOC PAGE 3162 ===
Supplement 86 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Engine Air Inlet Document N°
Barrier Filter 139G0290X002
RATE OF CLIMB
The effect of the IBF installed on Rate of Climb performance is given
for All Engines Operating (AEO) case and for the One Engine Inopera-
tive (OEI) case. For the AEO case, rate of climb is given with the
engines operating at the Maximum Continuous Power (MCP) and at
Take Off Power and with HEATER ON.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
For the OEI case, Rate of Climb with IBF installed is given with the
engines operating at the Maximum Continuous Power (MCP) and 2.5
min rating limit.
Page S86-32 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 12

GENERAL INFORMATION
Installation of the Heating/Ventilation and Air Conditioning System
(ENVIRO) kits permits automatic or manual control of the temperature
and airflow environment, independently for cockpit and cabin, depen-
dant on which kits are installed.
Three kits are available:
P/N 3G2141A00111 Heating and Forced Ventilation Kit
P/N 3G2141A00112
P/N 3G2150F00511 Air Conditioning Kit (Vapour Cycle
P/N 3G2150F00512 System)
P/N 4G2150F00711 Kit ECS for AGB
P/N 4G2150F00611 Dual Zone (Heating and Air conditioning)
P/N 4G2150F00911 Kit ECS Dual Zone for AGB
The kits consists of the basic configuration Heating and Forced Venti-
lation and the optional Air Conditioning Kit which is installed in addition
to the basic configuration.
The basic configuration instals the following items: bleed air shut off
valves, ejector heating valve (jet pump), pressure and temperature
sensors, outside air intake, fresh air valves, fans, pilot and passenger
area air outlets, connecting ducts and tubing, cockpit control panel to
operate the system and a controlling unit.
The Air Condition kit adds to the basic installation the air conditioning
vapour cycle units and associated tubing, valves and switches.
The Dual Zone kit includes the modification necessary to the Heating
and Air Conditioning kit to enable the temperature of the cockpit and
cabin to be controlled independantly.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The control panel for the Heating and Ventilation is shown in Figure 1,
the Heating and Ventilation and with Air Conditioning in Figure 2 and
the Dual Zone (Heating and Air Conditioning) control panel in
Figure 3.
The operation of the panels differs due to the incorporation of the air
conditioning VCS system selections and the Dual zone selections.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S87-1
Rev. 21

ECS CONTROL selector knob:
— Selecting FULL AUTO controls the cockpit and cabin temperature
automatically to the temperature selected on the AUTO TEMP
SETTING knob. The fresh air valves are controlled automatically
and the positionis dependant on the aircraft airspeed and fan
speed. The temperature setting can be varied between 10°C and
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
32°C and when heating is necessary the SOV’s are opened as
required and all the air mixing is automatic to maintain the temper-
ature selected. When the air conditioning system is present this
will automatically activate, if necessary. With the FAN setting for
CREW and PAX in AUTO the fan speed is selected automatically
to maintain the ambient temperature as selected. The FAN speed
can also be selected to positions 1, 2 or 3 to manually select a
fixed fan speed.
The Dual Zone panel enables the cockpit and cabin temperature
to be selected independently by the crew (when PAX CONTROL
is selected to CREW) or the cabin temperature and FAN speed
can be selected from the cabin if the PAX CONTROL is set to
PAX. A control panel (not included in this kit) must be installed in
the cabin to permit this.
The Dual Zone operation for cabin fan speed and temperature
simultaneously only operates for the FULL AUTO selection, while
in other selections only the fan speed can be modified.
— Selecting A/C RECYCLE (air conditioning installation only) acti-
vates the air conditioning VCS continuously. The FAN speed must
be selected as required, however if the FAN is selected to AUTO
or OFF the associated fan will be switched off.
— Selecting VENT closes the ejector heating valve and/or selects the
air conditioning OFF (if fitted) and ventilation is just via positioning
of the vent FAN switches.
— Selecting MAN HEAT permits the SOV’s to be controlled manually
by the MAN HEAT toggle switch selecting momentarily to
INCREASE or DECREASE to control the temperature.
— Selecting RAM ONLY closes SOV’s and/or selects the air condi-
tioning OFF (if fitted) and opens the fresh air valve fully. The FAN
speed is then controlled by the FAN CREW/PAX switches.

— Selecting the SOV from the NORM position, where control of the
valves is automatic, to CLOSE forces the SOV’s to close
overriding the system.
— Selecting the ECS CONTROL to OFF disactivates the heating/air
conditioning and ventilation (Refer to Section 1 - Limitations).
Operation of the Heater System is indicated by a HEATER ON
advisory message.
Operation of the Air Conditioning System is indicated by a AIR COND
ON advisory message.
Malfunctions of the heating or air conditioning systems are indicated
on the CAS by caution messages.

The Height-Velocity diagram defines, in the event of a single engine
failure during take off, landing or other operation near the surface, a
combination of airspeed and height above ground from which a safe
single engine landing on a smooth, level and hard surface cannot be
assured.

W.A.T. and H-V envelope charts.

H-V avoid area exists.

green ‘NO H-V Area’ then no H-V avoid area exists.
— If the given ambient conditions and weight intercept indicate an
H-V avoid area then low hover and knee points are fixed and the
high hover varies according to the conditions and weight.

COCKPIT / CABIN FIRE (FLIGHT)
An in-flight fire has no single set of detailed procedures that can address all
the fire scenarios that are possible in flight. The most critical action is to get
the aircraft on the ground as soon as possible with a reasonable degree of
safety .
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

SECTION 4 - PERFORMANCE
The maximum power available with the HEATER or Air Conditioner
operating is less than that available with the systems OFF. The power
loss is caused by the engine compressor bleed air used for the heat-
ing or the mechanical output from the main transmission for the air
conditioning system.
Performance charts with the ECS ENVIRO system switched to FULL
AUTO are provided for All Engine Operating conditions. This includes
the performance relative to Supplement 13 Cargo Hook Operations,
Supplement 50 Increased Gross Weight 6800 kg and Supplement 51
T-O and Landing Altitude Extension.
When MAN HEAT or A/C RECYCLE is selected refer to HEATER ON
and COND ON charts in Supplement 2 or appropriate Supplement.
The CAT B Distances are the same as those shown in the basic Rotor-
caft Flight Manual or appropriate Supplement.
The performance of the aircraft with the ECS ENVIRO switched OFF
or at VENT or RAM ONLY is the same as that shown in the basic
Rotorcraft Flight Manual.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S87-17

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 88
Document N ° Radio Equipment
139G0290X002 Rockwell Collins HF-9000D
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Rockwell Collins HF-9000D system P/N 4G2310F03511 is used
for long distance communication in the frequency range 2.0 to
29.9999 MHz with 100 Hz resolution with operational modes USB
(voice or data), LSB (voice or data), ISB (data) single frequency, AME
and CW. Functions also include Enhanced USB, LSB, ISB and ALE
and DSP.
The system comprises of HF-9000D Transceiver mounted in the aft
avionics bay, the antenna mounted on the tail cone, the antenna cou-
pler mounted at the back of the baggage bay, a control panel mounted
in the interseat console (Figure 2) and all necessary wiring see Figure
1.
The HF-9000D also includes the optional 2nd control panel mounted
in the cabin, see Figure 3, permitting control of the radio from the Mis-
sion Console.
For complete HF radio functionality refer to the Rockwell Collins HF-
9000 High Frequency Communications System Operators Guide, lat-
est issue.
The installation also supports the optional Codan 3590 AES-256 DV
Encrytor unit. For information on this equipment see the Encryptor
User Manual, latest issue.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S88-1
Rev. 12

SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
CENTRE OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS
After HF-90000D system installation, the new empty weight and cen-
ter of gravity location must be determined.
HF-9000D LIMITATION
It is prohibited to transmit on the HF-9000D system during refueling
and if personnel are in close proximity to the rotorcraft.
With cabin door open, HF-9000D radio transmissions are prohibited.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The Circular Force Active Vibration Control System (CF AVCS) is
designed to reduce the 5R vibration levels experienced in the cockpit
and cabin. The system comprises of Circular Force Generator Units
(CFGU) mounted under the cabin and cockpit floor, accelerometers
mounted at a series of key positions on the fuselage, rotor speed sig-
nal, an electronic integrated central controller unit (CC) and a control
panel, mounted in the interseat panel. The exact configuration
depends on the aircraft configuration and customer requirements.
The system takes signals from the vibration accelerometers and rotor
speed which are processed by the CC. Correction signals are then
sent to the Circular Force Generators to minimise the vibrations.
Two control panels are available which have slightly different function-
alities:
• Control panel P/N 3G1830V00251 (Figure 1) consists of an
OFF/ON switch with PWR ON indicator, a built in TEST push-
button, a system message FAIL and a maintenance port (MTN
PORT) to connect maintenance and trouble shooting equip-
ment.
• Control panel P/N 3G1830V00252 (Figure 2) consists of an
OFF/ON switch with CFG PWR indicator, a SYS ID guarded
pushbutton, system messages amber FAIL and white MAINT
captions and a maintenance port (MTN PORT) to connect
maintenance and trouble shooting equipment.
The TEST/SYS ID button can be used with the aircraft at IDLE or shut
down (with external power and ON/OFF switch selected to ON) to re-
calibrate the AVCS system. This function is intended to be used when
the aircraft configuration has been changed or a degradation of the
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
vibration control is felt. The TEST/SYS ID button when pressed
requires a period of up to 5 minutes to complete the procedure
(depending on number of CFGs installed) during which time the FAIL
lamp will flash.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S89-1
Rev. 20

may be experienced.

GENERAL INFORMATION
This Supplement details the changes to the Basic RFM to operate the
aircraft with an increased Gross Weight up to 7000 kg. This
information is valid for all weights in excess of the RFM Supplement
50 weight limit of 6800 kg.
SECTION 1 - LIMITATIONS
GENERAL
For Limitations not included in this Supplement refer to Basic RFM or
applicable Supplements.
If the aircraft weight, at any time, exceeds 6800 kg the entire flight
duration and all Take-Offs / Landings must be recorded as flight
operations above 6800 kg in the helicopter log-book.
AIRCRAFT CONFIGURATION
The following must be present on the aircraft for operation between
6800 kg and 7000 kg:
— Kit Increased Gross Weight 7000 kg P/N 4G0000F00311.

SECTION 2 - NORMAL PROCEDURES
No Change.
SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY AND MALFUNCTION
PROCEDURES
AUTOROTATIVE LANDING PROCEDURE ON LAND
The procedure which follows outlines the steps required to execute a
successful autorotation landing, time permitting, consult the appropri-
ate Emergency Procedure for the additional steps required to deal
with a specific type failure.
1. Collective pitch — Smoothly and rapidly reduce to
enter autorotation.
2. Cyclic — Adjust to obtain autorotation at
between 80 KIAS (minimum
rate of descent speed) and
100 KIAS (Best range speed).
3. Collective pitch — Adjust to obtain up to 110% NR.
4. Landing gear — Extend.
5. Landing site — Select and manoeuvre into
wind.
6. Brief — Cabin crew and occupants.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
7. Radar altimeter — Verify working.
8. Distress procedure — Broadcast Mayday (time per-
mitting).
9. Shutdown — If appropriate and time avail-
able carry out EMERGENCY/
POST CRASH SHUTDOWN
procedure Page 3-36.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S90-19
Rev. 13

=== DOC PAGE 3314 ===
Supplement 90 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Weight Extension Document N°
7000 kg 139G0290X002
10. Cyclic — At approximately 200 ft (61 m)
AGL, initiate a cyclic flare to a
maximum 30° nose-up angle.
11. Collective pitch — Adjust, as required, to maintain
NR at 110% maximum during
the flare. Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
12. Cyclic /Collective pitch — At approximately 35 ft (15 m)
AGL, reduce pitch attitude to
10° nose-up and apply collec-
tive pitch, as required, to
achieve touchdown at approxi-
mately 300 feet per minute
(fpm) or less.
13. Touchdown speed — As required by surface charac-
teristics. (Maximum touch-
down speed 40 kts on paved
surface, avoid grass surfaces
if possible, if not 20 kts on
grass surfaces).
14. Collective pitch — Following touchdown, lower
promptly to conserve the
remaining rotor speed.
15. Wheel brakes — Apply as required (land only).
16. Shutdown — If not carried out previously,
execute the EMERGENCY/
POST CRASH SHUTDOWN
procedure Page 3-36.
17. Evacuate — Evacuate the aircraft as soon
as possible.
Page S90-20 E.A.S.A. Approved

W.A.T. CHART EXAMPLES FOR WEIGHTS ABOVE 6800 KG
Example 1
Determine the maximum take-off weight permitted for the following
ambient conditions:
— Aircraft = Clean Intake Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
— Pressure Altitude = 2500 ft
— OAT = 25° C
Solution:
Using chart Figure 4-1 enter the graph at a pressure altitude of 2500 ft
and proceed horizontally to intersect the 25° C point, determined by
interpolating between the 20° C line and 30° C line. From this point
drop down vertically to a weight of 6920 kg which represent the maxi-
mum Take-Off weight for CAT B Take Off procedure.
Using charts Figure 4-5 the intersection between 2500 ft line and 25°
C point is beyond the Hd 2500 ft limit and therefore CAT A Take-Off in
these ambient conditions is not permitted.
Example 2
Determine the maximum take-off weight permitted for the following
ambient conditions:
— Aircraft = Clean Intake
— Pressure Altitude = 3500 ft
— OAT = 20° C
Solution:
Using chart Figure 4-1 enter the graph at a pressure altitude of 3500 ft
and proceed horizontally. It can be seen however that the 20° C point,
the extrapolated 30° C line, produces an intersection point outside of
the Hd limit line therefore Take-Off in these ambient conditions is not
permitted.
Page S90-22 E.A.S.A. Approved
Rev. 13

=== DOC PAGE 3317 ===
AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 90
Document N ° Weight Extension
139G0290X002 7000 kg
Example 3
Determine the maximum take-off weight permitted for the following
ambient conditions:
— Aircraft = Clean Intake
— Pressure Altitude = 500 ft
— OAT = 30° C
Solution:
Using chart Figure 4-1 enter the graph at a pressure altitude of 500 ft
and proceed horizontally. It can be seen that the 30° C point would be
to the right of the maximum take off weight line of Figure 4-1, therefore
maximum Take-Off weight is 7000 kg for CAT B Take Off procedure.
In this case, using chart Figure 4-5 enter the graph at a pressure alti-
tude of 500 ft and proceed horizontally to intersect the 30° C point.
From this point drop down vertically to a weight of 6975 kg which rep-
resent the maximum Take-Off weight for CAT A Take-Off procedure.

LOW SPEED MANOEUVRES IN QUARTERING FLIGHT IGE
Satisfactory stability and control has been demonstrated for all
azimuths shown below, Figure 4-9, for wind speed in accordance with
the Controllability Envelope in Figure 1-7.
The critical sectors, requiring slightly increased workload, are
indicated below. The sector 225°/270° is critical for high altitude/high
temperature. An increase in PI may be observed, which will remain
within limits. However if it is required to exit the condition, it is sufficient
to modify the heading by 20-30°.
The sector 90°/135° is critical for pedal margin.
No limitation exists for headwind conditions (±10°).

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 90
Document N ° Weight Extension
139G0290X002 7000 kg
RATE OF CLIMB
The climb performance shown is based on flight test results and
covers a range of gross weights from 6800 kg to the Maximum Gross
Weight of 7000 kg. (For gross weights below 6800 kg see Basic RFM
Supplement 50 or appropriate Supplement for aircraft configuration).
Rate of Climb performance is given for All Engines Operating (AEO)
case and for the One Engine Inoperative (OEI) case.
For the AEO case, rate of climb is given with the engines operating at
the Maximum Continuous Power (MCP) Rating limits and at Take Off
Power Rating limits. For the OEI case, rate of climb is given with the
engines operating at the 2.5 min rating limit. The datum speed for all
rate of climb graphs presented is 80 KIAS.
For ECS ENVIRO operation in MAN HEAT or A/C RECYCLE use
HEATER ON/COND ON ROC charts contained in this Supplement.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S90-71
Rev. 13

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 91
Document N ° Digital Power Line
139G0290X002 Detector System
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Digital Power Line Detector (DPLD) System detects 50 Hz and
60 Hz power line signal in the vicinity of the helicopter and warns the
pilot.
The system comprises of a Power Line Detector (PLD) unit mounted
in the cockpit instrument panel Figure 1, an antenna mounted exter-
nally on the helicopter tail cone lower inclined panel and an antenna
coupler.
The DPLD consists of a super low frequency receiver with a digital
processor to measure energy at power line frequencies, a level detec-
tor and a visual and aural warning generator.
When a nearby power transmission line is detected and the intensity
of the field exceeds a value based on the unit software sensitivity set-
ting, the system illuminates an amber lamp PWR LN on the panel and
sends a pulsed audio signal to the helicopters ICS system (AUX 1
channel). The sound increases in frequency with the intensity of the
power lines radiated field and indicates proximity to the source power
line.
A potentiometer is also mounted on the panel to turn the system OFF
(fully anti-clockwise) and provide adjustment of the sensitivity level on
the system. The audio warning may be muted by pressing the panel
button which illuminates the amber MUTE lamp to indicate the system
is in the mute condition.
At start up the system performs a SBIT as well as periodic monitoring
of the systems health.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S91-1
Rev. 15

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY AND MALFUNCTION
PROCEDURES
ELECTRICAL SYSTEM
DOUBLE DC GENERATOR FAILURE
The following assumes the Double DC generator Failure procedures,
presented in Section 3 of the Basic Manual, have been followed and a
double DC generator failure confirmed.
CAUTION
Ensure that the DPLD is switched OFF.
DPLD SYSTEM FAILURE
Any failure of the DPLD system will cause the MUTE and WARN mes-
sages to illuminate alternately. A momentary depression of the push-
button will cause both messages to illuminate continuously.
Depression of the pushbutton for longer than 2 seconds will restart the
system and carry out the self test function.
If the system that cannot be reset it must be switched OFF.

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 92
Document N ° LEO III HD FLIR
139G0290X002
GENERAL INFORMATION
The LEO III HD FLIR P/N 4G9350F01011 is an airborne Observation
System with High Definition sensors, remotely controlled day/night
imaging system with Microwave Down Link capability.
The system consists of a Stabilized Turret Assembly (STA), mounted
under the nose of the helicopter (Figure 1 & Figure 2), a Control Elec-
tronics Unit (CEU) which processes the electronics and a system con-
trol unit which consists of a Laptop Control Unit (LCU) that contains all
the controls necessary to operate the FLIR turret and systems or a
Hand Control (HC), see Figure 3 & Figure 4. The LCU keyboard can
only be used in the cabin.
The STA is gyro stabilized and its azimuth and elevation, and there-
fore the FLIR Line Of Sight (LOS), corresponding to the center of the
image, can be directed to any position within the Field Of Regard
(FOR) which is 20° to -120° in elevation and 360° in azimuth from the
forward position.
The STA contains the following sensors:
— Third generation IR camera with 10 step or continuous zoom,
ATTICA Z 640-2. The camera provides an optical Horizontal Field
of View (HFOV) from 20° to 2° HFOV. The camera has operator
control of focus (manual and auto), gain and level control, Image
polarity control Local adaptive dynamic compression (to optimize
visibility of details in very bright and dark areas of the immage),
homogenization (NUC)
— Progressive scan HD multi-spectral Zoom TV camera with 4 sen-
sors. The HD zoom lens fitted has an zoom ratio of 20x, and opti-
cal HFOV of 20° to 1° HFOV and a x2 and x4 digital zoom
capability allowing for an ultra narrow FOV of 0.25 HOV.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The camera has operator control of Focus (manual or auto), Iris
control (manual or auto), gain control (manual or auto), selectable
preset control modes for differing light and weather conditions and
a multi spectral image selection.
— HD spotter TV camera with 4 sensors and a super narrow HD
spotter lens. The HD zoom lens fitted has a super narrow FOV of
0.4 HFOV and a x2 and x4 digital zoom capability <allowing an
ultra narrow HFOV of 0.1 HFOV.
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S92-1
Rev. 14

=== DOC PAGE 3476 ===
Supplement 92 AW139 - RFM - 4D
LEO III HD FLIR Document N°
139G0290X002
The camera has operator control of Focus (manual or auto), Gain
control (manual or auto), Automatic white balancing, selectable
preset control modes for differing light and weather conditions and
a multi spectral image selection.
— Infra Red (NIR) Laser illuminator Class 3b to extend night capabil-
ity of the 2 camera.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
— Laser pointer (optional) Class 3b, with either a NIR laser or a visi-
ble red laser pointer.
— Eye Safe Multi repetition laser range finder (LRF) (optional). the
LRF provides slant range to an object up to a distance of 15 km
with an accuracy of 5 m
— Internal inertial measuring unit (IMU) (optional) which provides an
independent capability to perform geo location/geo pointing func-
tion to determine the attitude of the aircraft with respect tot he sur-
roundings.
The CEO provides all the necessary electronic processing to display
and interface signals with the helicopter equipment.
The LCU or the HC interface can be used to operate the system with
thumb joystick, rotary encoders, arm switch and pushbutton com-
mands to control the system without entering the multi layer menu
selections.
To operate the LRF, Laser Pointer or Laser Illuminator (if fitted) a
series of hardware and software interlocks are incorporated in addition
to the Laser Safety Interlock Unit (LIU) (Figure 5) which is fitted in the
interseat console and incorporates an ARM switch requiring a key to
ARM the laser before firing. A WOW interlock also ensures the laser is
not used when the aircraft is on the ground.
The Pilot and Copilot MFD, optional central 5th display or the Mission
Console Display can also be used to display the image.
If a search light is installed the searchlight may be slaved to the FLIR
for night illumination. See appropriate Supplement for Searchlight.
For full information on the use of the LEO III HD FLIR refer to the LEO
III HD Airborne Observation System Operator’s Manual Document,
latest revision.

AW139 - RFM - 4D Supplement 93
Document N ° MGB Improved
139G0290X002 Lubrication System
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Main Gearbox (MGB) Improved Lubrication System consists of
modified engine input modules which contain an oil reservoir mounted
on the top of each module. The reservoir, which holds approximately
1.5 litres of oil, is connected to the module via an oil lubrication jet and
a reservoir overflow pipe. The reservoir mounted on the input module
becomes a closed loop system with the MGB. See Figure 1.
During normal MGB operation an oil jet, pressurized by the MGB oil
pumps, continuously fill the oil reservoir with MGB oil. Being a closed
system the oil then exits the sealed reservoir via an overflow pipe back
into the MGB. Oil exiting the reservoir in this manner does not
contribute directly to the lubrication of the input bearings.
When the MGB suffers loss of oil or loss of oil pressure the oil in the
reservoir then exits the reservoir through the oil jet, under the effect of
gravity. The oil jet directly lubricates the input pinion ball bearing and is
centrifugally spread around the other bearings in the input module to
continue lubrication of the input module and maintain the temperature
of the bearings low. As the input modules are the critical part of the
MGB for the ‘run dry’ capability this improvement permits a
modification to the MGB OIL PRESS emergency procedure, see
Section 3 of this Supplement.
This optional modification on new production MGB’s is recorded as
P/N 4G6320F00311 and is available as an option for retrofit on
previous MGBs P/N 4G6320F00312 or the new P/N 4G6320F00511.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S93-1
Rev. 30

GENERAL INFORMATION
The Kit for the Left Hand Controls Removal P/N 4G6700F00311 com-
prises of left hand cyclic and collective covers, stowage of the connec-
tors and compensating masses for the pilot cyclic and collective. The
left hand yaw pedals have a transparent panel mounted in front of the
pedals and a cover for the left hand pedal adjuster.
After the removal of the left hand cyclic stick and collective lever the
connectors are stowed and the covers are fitted to avoid interference
of the controls. Due to the effect on the control system balance
weights are added to the right hand cyclic and collective to compen-
sate for the removal of the LH controls. See Figure 1 and Figure 2.
The yaw pedals remain installed, however, a transparent plexiglass
panel is mounted in front of the pedals, to avoid interference of pedal
movement, and a cover mounted over the yaw pedal adjuster mecha-
nism see Figure 3.

GENERAL INFORMATION
Ditching Regulations
Demonstration of emergency over water landing capability and
buoyancy up to Sea State 4 is required by ditching regulations.
However, for this installation Sea State 6 has been demonstrated and
approved.
Emergency Flotation and Life Raft System (P/N 4G9560F00111 &
P/N 4G9560F00211)
This system comprises of :
— 4 flotation bags, 2 mounted on the lower nose section (left and
right hand sides) and two mounted on the lower aft central section
(left and right hand side). One inflation bottle is mounted in the left
flotation cover.
— 2 life rafts mounted, one on each aft flotation bag, left and right
hand side, in a dedicated pocket on the flotation bags. two
configurations are available,
• P/N 4G9560F00111 contains 10 man (15 man overload) Life
Rafts
• P/N 4G9560F00211, contains 12 man (18 man overload) Life
Rafts
The flotation bags are automatically deployed on ditching by water
sensors (four sensors are installed and 2 adjacent sensors must be
activated to inflate the flotation) or by manual operation of the guarded
FLOAT pushbutton on either the Pilot or Copilot collective grip. (See
Figure 2)
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters For operation of both automatic or manual flotation inflation the OFF/
ARMED switch on the FLOATS EMER control panel, mounted in the
interseat console (pilots side), must be set to ARMED. The control
panel also incorporates a self test function for the flotation system.
Two panels are available P/N 3G9560V00558 & P/N 3G9560V00559
Figure 1.
The life raft inflation is activated manually, and independently, for left
or right life raft installation. Two basic modes of manual deployment
are available, plus optional additional handles:
E.A.S.A. Approved Page S95-1
Rev. 32

— The Primary activation handle is mounted on the Pilot/Copilot
forward door frame.
— The Secondary is by handles mounted externally to the aircraft on
the left and right cargo door forward frame.
— The Third, optional deployment means are additional life raft
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
inflation handles mounted under the belly at the edges, on the left
and right hand side, close to the sponson.
To activate the life raft inflation remove the safety pin from the cockpit
handles and rotated aft. The Secondary handles on the external cabin
door forward frame can also be used by removing the safety pin, lifting
the guard and rotating the handles downward.
The Third handles (if installed) under the belly can also be used by
removing the safety pin, lifting the guard and rotating the handles.
A cable system, connected to the liferaft, activates the inflation. (See
Figure 3 & Figure 5).
The left and right hand life raft activation is independent, the left side
handles are used to deploy the left hand life raft and the right side
handle to deploy the right hand liferaft.
Each life raft contains an Survival Kit and Emergency Locator
Transmitter (ELT) compliant with ETSO-C126a. Both the ELT and
Survival Kit are accessible, when the raft is packed inside the aft float
container, via an access window. See Figure 4.
