Emergency All Call
The audio panel includes a yellow CALL button so that any crew mem-
ber can immediately make an emergency intercom call. The CALL
button immediately connects the cabin to the pilots during the time the
button is held down with no acknowledgement required by the pilots or
any other crew member.
When the CALL button is held down, the following happens:
— The audio from that audio panel is routed to the headphone, cabin
speaker, and cockpit speaker outputs of all AV-900s;
— The display for that audio panel indicates “CALL: TX” and the dis-
play for the other audio panels indicates “EM CALL” and their
CALL buttons illuminate
— The incoming CALL audio is summed with other previously
selected audio and provided to headsets and speakers.
The Emergency All Call command does not suppress other audio,
pilot or maintenance intercom audio and does not overide Radio TX,
BKUP, and Config Mode functions.
When the CALL button is pressed a CALL button press on another
audio panel is ignored.
If the AV-900 is in BKUP Mode, the CALL button is ignored.
If the AV-900 CALL button is held down for more than two minutes, the
Emergency All Call is terminated.
Full Duplex FONE Interfaces
The audio panels, provides analog audio interfaces for two full duplex
communication devices (FONEs). i.e. Satellite or Cell Phones.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The FONE1 and FONE2 interfaces can detect an incoming call. The
light on the relevant FONE1 or FONE2 button begin to flash and a
chime is heard to indicating an incoming call.
The FONE1 and FONE2 buttons connect the microphone and audio
for the corresponding FONE, only one may be active at a time.

WINDSCREEN WIPER (P/N 3G3040A00811 OR 3G3040A00812)
WASHING SYSTEM (P/N 4G3040F00111, 4G3040F00112 OR
4G3040F00113)
A twin, parallel action, windscreen wiper system is installed in the heli-
copter basic configuration which allows cleaning of both the pilot and
copilot windscreens.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The windscreen wiper system is composed of:
— a control panel in the cockpit interseat console
— wiper blades system
— electric motor drive installation
The system can operate with 2 different speeds (SLOW/FAST) and
dual or single side operation. The mode of operation is selected on the
control panel in the cockpit interseat console and ON/OFF control of
the wipers is controlled by the pushbutton switches on the cyclic con-
trol grips. Dual mode activation is started by pushing either cyclic but-
ton which activates both wipers (Figure 7-50 & 7-51).
The windshield washing system (P/N 4G3040F00112) is provided in
addition to the windshield wiper system (included in the basic configu-
ration) to allow cleaning of the windshield surface of any accumulation
of water, insects, dirt, sand, dust, salt spray etc.
The windshield wash system consists of:
— Washer pump
— Fluid tank with low-level sensor (for maintenance message)
— Piping up to the wiperblade spray bar
— Control panel located in the cockpit interseat console
— Reservoir with capacity of 5 liters
Two washing cycles are available, dependent on the time pressure is
applied to the washer button:
— Light washing cycle, button held for 1 second or less, (1 cycle
spray and wipe, followed by 2 cycles of wiping).
— Heavy washing cycle, button held for more than 1 second, (contin-
uous cycle of spraying and wiping until pushbutton is released,
and then 2 cycles of wiping).

Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

modes and the display of information on the MFD is carried out using
the MFDs Map drop down menu. See Figure 7-53.

The LSS detects high energy invisible electromagnetic and electro-
static discharges (lightning) that may indicate areas of turbulent activ-
ity. The lightning activity uses a “rate of occurrence” symbols that
show three level of lightning activity within a circular cell around the
symbol. The white rate symbol is coded, according to the lightning
strike rate of occurrence within the cell and upgrades the symbol as
more lightning strikes are detected. The symbol is downgraded if two Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
minutes passes with no new lightning strikes detected, see
Figure 7-54.
The magenta ALERT symbol is displayed after the first lightning strike
for 5 seconds on the bearing of the strike and a white rate one symbol
which is upgraded depending on the strikes detected.
RATE ONE: SINGLE STRIKE
RATE TWO: THREE STRIKES
RATE THREE: SIX STRIKES

• LSS CLR All memory of past strikes and symbols are cleared

RADIO ITT AN/ARC-201E SINCGARS
The AN/ARC-201E is a VHF FM tactical military radio. The system
comprises of the RT AN/ARC-201E receiver/transmitter, an Export
Radio Control/display unit (ERCDU) mounted in the interseat console
(Figure 7-55) and a dedicated antenna mounted above and between
the engine exhausts.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The ICS panel COM 4 is used to access the radio system on the ICS
system.
The AN/ARC-201E radio is a 2320 channel, Frequency Hopping,
voice or data, COMSEC radio. The radio operates on VHF FM from 30
to 87.975 MHz for radio communications of voice and data with secure
(Cipher Text) or Plain Text, in single channel (25 KHz increments) and
in the SINCGARS ECCM mode of operation. The RT is remotely con-
trolled with the ERCDU through two 1553B buses. The equipment is
capable of using the SINCGARS data rates 16k, AD1, and AD2. The
RT requires Communication Information for secure and frequency
hopping operations. An external interface provides the capability for
loading of Fill inputs to include Single Channel frequencies, hopsets,
TRANSEC, COMSEC and time.
See Figure 7-56 for component installation positions.
For full information on the use of the ITT AN/ARC-201E Sincgars radio
refer to Operators Manual Pub No 07BAN12P, latest issue.

inputs to be managed onto several display outputs (such as 5th
display, MFD display, Mission Console display, digital video recorder,
video up/downlink) and provides better imaging performance, multiple
standard conversions and an improved video signal customization.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The kit consists of two main items, the video processor, located
beneath the floor behind the copilot seat, and the configuration
module, located in the rear avionics bay.
A C/B for the system is mounted in the overhead Auxiliary Circuit
Breaker panel. An optional switch may be installed next to the C/B
(Figure 7-57). The 2 position optional switch is used to select between
2 graphic sources on the MFD (eg. digital map or search radar)
depending on the equipment installed. The labeling of this switch
XXXX/XXXX will vary depending on the installations (eg. DMAP,
RADAR etc).The 2 position input source switch is used to select
between 2 sources ie. digital map, radar, video etc, dependant on the
installed on the aircraft. The labeling of this switch XXXX/XXXX will
vary depending on the installations (eg. DMAP, RADAR etc).
When the system is off a white status message, in the CAS window, is
displayed “CHECK VMU” to inform the pilot that the VMU is powered
off or in fail (no configuration module installed).
Note

is frozen on the MFD.

139G0290X002
NAT DACS INTERCOM SYSTEM
The NAT DACS ICS system (P/N 4G2350F01711) is a communica-
tions management system that distributes and controls audio in the
cabin. It manages the audio from all transceivers, receivers and audio
warning sources. It allows the transmission of microphone audio to
selected transmitter and distributes the intercom audio.
The system comprises the Audio Management Unit (AMU50) (Figure
7-62) and up to 6 Audio Control Panels (ACP) type ACP51 or ACP53
(Figure 7-62 and Figure 7-63). A maximum of 7 headsets can be con-
nected. The audio managment unit has the cockpit intercom bus,
selected transceivers and receivers and audio control panels con-
nected to it. The Audio Management Unit sums and distributes all
audio to each user attached to it.
A panel, next to each ACP, contains the CALL and EM CALL pushbut-
tons which control the communication between the cabin and cockpit
crew (Figure 7-64).
The system is configurable using a PC connected to the Audio Man-
agement Unit via a USB serial port and DACS configuration manage-
ment software (DevCs). Configuration options include the number of
radios, audio levels, microphone levels, alert audio levels, etc.
The system can be customized to adapt to each installation. Custom-
ization includes expected receive audio input levels, number of crew
members, microphone impedance, etc. These settings are saved in a
small, remote mounted unit; the RM01. Also saved in the RM01 are all
of the Aural Alert audio files and the Aural Alert setting, such as prior-
ity and number of repetitions. Storing the system configuration in this
unit enables the replacement of the Audio Management Unit without
the need of downloading a new configuration file.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The DACS system is used as cabin digital ICS system. The system is
connected with the cockpit intercom Audio through an analog audio
port. The discretes are used to control the CALL logic between the
cockpit and cabin and are not connected to the DACS system. To
manage the Call logic two external pushbutton, with internal circuitry,
(CALL and EM-CALL), are used.
For full information on the use of the NAT DACS ICS system refer to
the Operators manual latest issue.

The SAAB Digital Video Audio Recorder (DVAR) and Audio Mixer
Panel P/N 4G9700F00511 are customer options for the AW139. They
provide the ability to digitally record video and audio signals (Radar,
FLIR, ICS, Digital Map etc) depending on the aircraft configuration
and selections on the control panels.
The installation comprises of athe DVAR control panel located either in
the interseat console or mission console or both dependant on the
customer configuration. The DVAR Processor unit is installed in a
position in order to make the cartridge accessible to crew. Depending
on the customer requirements two position are currently available
either mounted in the mission console or mounted on the cabin wall
beside the mission console.
The Audio mixer is used control the ICS channel volumes that are reg-
istered on the DVAR.
The video and audio is stored on a removable MMC flashcard. The
recorded video and audio signals can either be viewed on the aircraft
cabin display (if fitted) or on a Ground Replay Station by removing the
MCC Flash Card. An optional unit is also availbale to downloaded
from the DVAR Processor to a PC using a suitable connecting cable
on ground.

The Cockpit Call Lights Kit P/N 4G2300F00111/112 mounts two indi-

LEFT HAND CABIN STEERABLE LIGHT
The left hand steerable light kit P/N 4G3340F02511 introduces a ster-
able light on the left hand underside of the of the cabin fuselage. The
light is symmetric to and identical to the Goodrich Hoist steerable light
(if fitted).
The kit consists of the steerable light mounting, a control panel and
pendant mounted on the left had side of the cabin and all the neces-
sary wiring. The light can be operated by the cabin crew using the
control panel which has a LAMP ON/OFF switch and a 5 way switch.
When selected ON the lamp system is supplied with power but the
lamp remains off. Pressing the central fifth position on the 5 way
switch the lamp illuminates but remains stowed. Moving the 5 way
switch to FWD un-stows the lamp, which can then be directed using
the switch FWD/R/AFT/L positions. Switching the LAMP switch to
OFF turns the lamp off but leaves it extended. Pushing the center
position switches the light off (if not already switched off) and stows
the light. The additional pendant provides a remote means of control-
ling the light direction. The pendant has a 4 way switch that can be
used to direct the light, instead of the control panel switch. See Figure
7-73 and Figure 7-74.

RADIO TETRA CHELTON
The Radio Tetra Chelton P/N 4G2310F02911 is designed to provide
airborne communications compatible within a TETRA communications
network. The system comprises the Chelton 7-450-14-1 transceiver
located in the baggage compartment, the Chelton CH150-14 Control
and Display Unit (CDU) mounted in the interseat console (Figure 7-
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
78), an RF antenna located on the top of the tail cone and all the nec-
essary wiring.
The system interfaces directly to standard aircraft audio systems on
COM 3, 4 or 5 depending on the installation.
The radio supports the transmission of voice and data and can oper-
ate in both the Trunked Mode of Operation (TMO, in a network) and
the Direct Mode of Operation (DMO, without a network infrastructure).
A GPS antenna is connected to the TETRA transceiver module to pro-
vide GPS positional information to the CDU (or remote user).
For complete details of the Radio Tetra Chelton operation refer to
Operators Manual latest issue.

RADIO COBHAM RT7000PMR
The RT7000PMR is a panel mounted Tactical multi-band
multi-transceiver device with a touch screen display.
The radio has a modular architecture and the panel mounted control
unit can contain one to three transceivers, combining the Cobham
wideband transceiver or integrated Motorola APX 8000 radio. Different Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
combinations are managed throught kit dash numbers.
(P/N 4G2310FXXXXX)
The radio system is made up of:
— The panel mounted control unit which can house up to three
internal transceivers covering the frequency band 29.7 MHz to
960 MHz AM/FM. The transceivers that are fitted depend on the
customer requirements.
— Three wide antennas may be installed at different positions on the
helicopter. In general the positions available are on the cabin
underbelly, rear fuselage or engine exhaust upper cowling
between the exhausts. The antenna positions depend on the
helicopter configuration and customerization.
The system is designed to be modular so each transceiver is
connected to its own antenna, LCU and antenna switch in order to
have three separate transmission systems.
Radio front panel control is through a Touch Panel Display or through
two concentric knobs, see Figure 7-91.
For complete details of the Cobham RT7000PMR refer Operator
Guide - RT7000PMR.
Another option for the RT7000PMR is the RT7000 RCDU (Remote
Control display Unit P/N 4G2310F05511) which installs and additional
remote control touch screen display unit in the cabin. The control has
the same display as the RT7000PMR with similar control functions but
in a smaller chassis unit.

DAL-200 WI-FI BRIDGE KIT
The DAL-200 kit works as a Wi-Fi bridge providing connectivity to
devices installed in the aircraft via external Wi-Fi networks.
The KIT DAL-200 P/N 4G4390F01511 provides:
— Wi-Fi functionality that operates in the 2.4GHz band, and complies
to wireless standards 802.11 a/b/g/n with a maximum wireless
speed of 54 Mbps;
— Bluetooth functionality, Bluetooth 4.2 compliant with dual mode
Bluetooth and Bluetooth Low Energy;
— Ethernet connection to the ISAT-200A in order to allow HUMS
data exchange.
Refer to Figure 7-93.
The DAL -200 also interfaces with the Helicopter Data Transmission
Kit P/N 4G4390F01411 for transmission of data to a ground station.
The Helicopter Data Transmission Kit provides the following functions:
— The collection and post flight transmission of HUMS and flight data
(the latest retrieved from the FDR) from the aircraft to ground
servers via Wi-Fi channels,
— The real time in-flight transmission of HUMS exceedances from
the aircraft to ground servers via satellite communication
channels,
— The reception and the storage of thresholds to compute HUMS
exceedances (by means of HUMS data loader device (DTD)) from
ground server to the aircraft via Wi-Fi channels.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

REMOTE BATTERY KIT
The Remote Battery Kit installs an additional 24VDC 25AH battery
P/N 4G2430F01011 in a removable rack which is installed in the rear
compartment, refer to Figure 7-94.
The battery is for ground use only and is used to supply power, when
the aircraft is shut down and Main and Auxiliary battery (if installed)
are OFF and no DC External power is connected, to allow operation
of:
• Cabin ventilation systen P/N 3G2141A00112
• Electrical Step lights and movement (extend and retract)
P/N 4G5260F00213.
The system is selected with the REMOTE BATTERY ON/OFF switch
installed in the AUX circuit breaker panel.
The remote battery is recharged when both electrical power
generators are online (engines running). In this condition the electrical
power to the cabin ventilation fan and electrical step is automatically
restored, through diodes, to the aircraft electrical system.
The remote battery automatically disconnects if one generator fails or
is OFF.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

SECTION 8
HANDLING, SERVICING AND MAINTENANCE
HANDLING
Ground handling of the helicopter consists of towing, parking, secur-
ing, and mooring. Refer to Maintenance Manual for more detailed
ground handling information.
TOWING
The helicopter may be towed at walking speeds for very short dis-
tances using a standard tow bar (Figure 8-1).
Prior to movement, clear towing area of support equipment, such as
work stands, power units, fire extinguishers, etc., and disconnect static
ground wire.
Towing operations may be carried out using tow bar configurations
P/N 3G0905G00133, 3G0905G00134, 3G0905G00232 or
3G0905G10331, for other approved tow bar configurations refer
AgustaWestland Maintenance Publication AW139 IETP.

PARKING AND SECURING
Position helicopter in desired parking area on level surface when pos-
sible. Remove towbar and attach static ground wire to receptacle on
lower right aft fuselage. Check all switches in OFF position. Install
approved tie downs on main and tail rotor blades and wheel chocks.
For extended parking, disconnect battery, lock rotor brake, and close
doors and windows. Install protective covers on pitot tubes, engine air
inlets, and exhaust ejectors (Figure 8-2).

TIE DOWN MAIN ROTOR
Tie down main rotor blades whenever any of the following condition
exist: Thunderstorms are in the local area or forecasted. Winds in
excess of 20 knots or a gust spread of 15 knots exists or is forecasted.
Helicopter is parked within 150 feet of hovering or taxiing aircraft that
are in excess of 11,900 pounds gross weight. Helicopter to be parked
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
overnight.
The main rotor tie downs are socks which fit over the end of each
blade with cords which attach to mooring points on the fuselage
(Figure 8-3). The tie down cords are manufactured to specified lengths
for forward and aft mooring points, as identified by streamers adjacent
to the brass rings to which the snap hooks attach. When secure, the
tie downs should be free of slack or under slight tension, but not under
sufficient tension to flex the main rotor blades appreciably. The cords
should never be shortened from their design lengths, as excessive
loads could be induced in the main rotor yokes.

The tail rotor tie down is red and is stenciled in white letters “REMOVE
BEFORE FLIGHT”. To tie down the tail rotor assembly, rotate main
rotor until tail rotor blades are aligned with the vertical fin and main
rotor blades are approximately 45 degrees to helicopter centerline. Tie
down main rotor first, then secure tail rotor with tail rotor blades flap-
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

COVER ENGINE AIR INTAKE
The cover engine air intake engine is installed on each engine Each
cover is attached with a red streamer stenciled in white letters
"REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT". Press inlet plugs in engine air inlets.
COVER ENGINE EXHAUST DUCT
A cover is installed on each engine exhaust ejector and is tied with a
nylon cord in the cover. The covers have red streamers on each side
stenciled in white letters "REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT".
COVER PITOT TUBE
The pitot tube covers are flame resistant and are attached with a red
streamer stenciled in white letters "REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT".
Cover pitot tubes and tie cord to secure to pitot tubes.

MOORING
Mooring is securing the helicopter to prevent damage during periods
of high winds or turbulent weather.
The helicopter should be moored if parked in the open when forecast
wind velocity is 45 knots (52 mph) or higher. If forecast wind velocity
exceeds 75 knots (86 mph), the helicopter should be hangared or
evacuated to a safe area. If parked in the open, the helicopter should
be positioned on a paved ramp between suitably spaced tie down
rings and should be headed in the direction from which the highest
forecast winds are expected.
The main and tail rotors should be properly secured with tie downs
immediately after shutdown during windy conditions to minimize rotor
flapping.
Protective covers should be installed, and fuel tanks should be ser-
viced to maximum capacity with prescribed fuel to add weight to the
helicopter. Fuselage mooring shackles should be secured to ramp tie
down points with rope, cable, or manufactured tie down assemblies. If
suitably spaced ramp tie downs are not available, the helicopter
should be parked on an unpaved surface and secured to subsurface
mooring anchors or "deadman" anchors.
All ground support equipment and other objects which might be blown
by wind should be properly secured. After winds subside, the helicop-
ter should be checked for damage.

lubricate the helicopter systems and components. It also includes a list

of consumable materials used in performing the helicopter mainte-
nance operations (Refer to Figure 8-4).

ENGINE SERVICING
Engine oil capacity (each):
8.45 U.S. quarts (8.0 liters)
The engine lubrication system is a regulated system and consists of
an integral oil tank, a pressure system, a acavenge system and a
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
brether system.The oil tank is integral with the engine. It is the annular
cavity created between the air inlet case and the accesory gearbox
rear case. A drain plug, located at the bottom of AGB, permits drain-
age of the cavity. Oil level indication is achieved by means of oil level
sight glasses on each side of accesory gearbox.

GEARBOX OILS

transmission, intermediate, and tail rotor gearbox. Refer to Transmis-
sion, Intermediate and Tail Rotor Gearbox Oil Limitations in Flight
Manual for ambient temperature limitations.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The Supplemental Performance Information contained in this section
is provided for use in conjunction with Section 4 and optional equip-
ment Supplements, as applicable.
The section titled CRUISE CHARTS contains data that allows the
determination of the fuel flow, max endurance and recommended
cruise for AEO and OEI conditions.
The section titled CLIMB GRADIENT (page 9-118) contains charts of
mean height gained in 100 ft of horizontal distance for different air-
speeds and gross weights.
The section titled HOVER CEILING WITH HEADWIND BENEFIT con-
tains charts of gross weight benefit with headwind, for hover out of
ground effect and OEI 2.5 MIN power.
The section titled HOVER CEILING CHARTS AT 102 %NR contains
Hover Ceiling charts defining the maximum weights at which an OGE
hover is possible for varying combinations of Pressure Altitude and
OAT with main rotor speed at 102% and zero wind conditions.

CRUISE CHARTS
The cruise charts are based on estimates and flight test data.
This data does not include the effect of bleed air on fuel consumption.
Fuel flow data are applicable to the basic helicopter. A delta torque
(DTQ) correction reference line is also included to calculate the effect
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
of various optional equipment that can be fitted to the aircraft. The ref-
erence line (dotted line on the left side of chart, equivalent to the drag
of a 1 square meter plate) is used in combination with the Correction
Factor for the optional equipment (Table 9-1) to calculate the addi-
tional Torque/Fuel consumption with the equipment installed.
All Engine Operation (AEO) and One Engine Inoperative (OEI) condi-
tions are included.
The Range and Endurance Chart is valid for both AEO and OEI condi-
tions.
CRUISE CHART TERMINOLOGY
Max Endurance This line defines the TAS/IAS, for
a given Gross Weight, for which
the corresponding Fuel Con-
sumption is at a minimum and,
therefore, the mission duration is
maximised.
Maximum Range Cruise: This line defines the TAS/IAS, for
a given Gross Weight, for the
maximum distance achievable.
Recommended Cruise: This line defines the TAS/IAS, for
a given Gross Weight, based on a
1% reduction of the Maximum
Cruise range, for the same Gross
Weight. The speed increase given
by this method provides a good
compromise between fuel con-
sumption and time.
Vne: The Vne line is plotted when the
Vne is less than Vh (level flight
speed at MCP).

Note
The range evaluated with the diagram correspond to effec-

To take into account the wind effect in the range calcula-

Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
(ground speed) before entering in the chart.
EXAMPLE NO WIND (See Figure 9-107 )
Wanted Endurance, distance and specific range.
Known Fuel consumption: 393 kg/h Available fuel: 1000 kg TAS:
150 kt.
Method Enter chart at fuel consumption 393 kg/h move up and
intersect available fuel 1000 kg line, move the left and
read 2.54h (2h:32':24").
Return to 393 kg/h, than move up to intersect True air-
speed 150 kt line, move to the left to intersect available
fuel 1000 kg line, move to the left and read 0.38 nm/kg, or
move down and read 382 nm than move up and read
707 km.
EXAMPLE With WIND (See Figure 9-107 and Figure 9-108 )
Wanted TAS corrected with headwind and respective range.
Known Wind: 25 kt from 35° respect to flight direction
TAS: 150 kt.
Method Enter chart (Figure 9-108) at 25 kt reported wind speed
(point A), proceed right following shape of curved lines to
wind relative angle 35° (point B) than proceed right hori-
zontally to read 20 on the headwind component scale
(point C).
Reduce TAS of 20 kt to obtain a ground speed of 130 kt.
Enter chart (Figure 9-107) at fuel consumption of 393 kg/
h, TAS corrected of 130 kt and available fuel of 1000 kg
to obtain a distance of 331 nm or 613 km with an endur-
ance of 2.54 h.

EXAMPLES WITH OPTIONAL EQUIPMENT INSTALLED
Example 1
Wanted True airspeed, Indicated airspeed, torque, fuel consump-
tion for Recommended Cruise with Optional Equipment
Searchlight SX16 and Double External Hoist Goodrich in
Stowed position.
Known Pressure altitude: 0 ft OAT: 20° C
Gross weight: 5600 kg.
Method Select the suitable chart (Figure 9-4), intersect the gross
weight 5600 kg line with the recommended cruise line to
read TAS = 161 kt, IAS = 162 kt, TQ = 88%, fuel con-
sumption = 492 kg/hr. These define the Recommended
Cruise values for a clean aircraft configuration.
To correct for the effect of Optional Equipment installed
determine the intersect of the DTQ reference line at the
TAS = 161kts and move vertically to read DTQ = 23%.
This value is then factored by the total of the Correction
Factors (CF) for the equipment installed i.e. from
Table 9-1 Searchlight CF = 0.3, Double External Hoist in
stowed position CF = 0.2.
Torque penalty for optional equipment becomes:
23 x (0.3+0.2) = 11.5%.
To correct the Recommended Cruise speed, maintaining
the TQ and fuel flow as for the clean configuration,
subtract the Torque Penalty from the clean aircraft
Recommended Cruise torque value ie:
88 - 11.5 = 76.5% TQ, enter the bottom scale at 76.5%
TQ, and move vertically to intercept the 5600 kg then
move horizontally to read TAS = 152 kt and IAS = 152 kt
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters which is the Recommended Cruise speed with Optional
Equipment fitted and keeping the TQ = 88% and fuel
consumption = 492 kg/hr.
Note
If, at the new corrected TQ the appropriate weight line
cannot be intercepted this indicates that there is no speed
reduction available that maintains the TQ and fuel flow
fixed.
Page 9-5
Rev. 25

=== DOC PAGE 4114 ===
Section 9 AW139 - RFM - 4D
Supplemental Performance Document N°
Information 139G0290X002
For the example above, if the Recommended Cruise
speed is maintained then an increase in TQ required, and
therefore fuel consumption, is required. This can be
calculated as follows:
The Torque Penalty from the clean aircraft is ADDED to
the initial Recommended Cruise torque value ie:
88 + 11.5 = 99.5% TQ, Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Then enter the bottom scale at 99.5% TQ, and move
vertically to read the fuel consumption = 532 kg/hr which
is the value maintaining the Recommended Cruise speed
with kits installed.
Example 2
Wanted Maximum True airspeed, Indicated airspeed, torque, fuel
consumption with Optional Equipment External Hoist
Breeze fitted.
Known Pressure altitude: 4000 ft OAT: 40° C
Gross weight: 6000 kg.
Method Select the suitable chart (Figure 9-17), intersect the gross
weight of 6000 kg line with the Maximum Continuous
power line. Move across to read TAS = 158 kt,
IAS = 142 kt, move vertically down to read TQ = 80.5 %
and up to read fuel consumption = 445 kg/hr. These
define the values for a clean aircraft configuration.
To correct for the effect of Optional Equipment installed
determine the intersect of the DTQ reference line at the
TAS = 158 kt and move vertically up to read DTQ = 17 %.
This value is then factored by the total of the correction
factors for the equipment installed i.e. from Table 9-1
External Hoist Breeze CF = 0.4.
Torque penalty becomes 17 x 0.4 = 6.8 %.
To correct the Maximum True airspeed:
80.5 - 6.8 = 73.7 %. Enter the bottom at 73.7 % TQ and
move up to intersect the 6000 kg line then move
horizontally to read TAS = 153 kt and IAS = 138 kt, the
maximum airspeed with Optional Equipments fitted, TQ =
80.5 % and fuel consumption = 445 kg/hr.

Information 139G0290X002
CLIMB GRADIENT
The charts of Minimum Climb Gradient for 2.5 min OEI power for air-
speeds of 50 KIAS, 70 KIAS and 90 KIAS show the mean height
gained in 100 ft of horizontal distance in relation to the ambient condi-
tions and the aircraft gross weight.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
The charts are based on estimates and flight test data.
EXAMPLE
Wanted Climb gradient 2.5 min OEI.
Known Pressure altitude: 5000 ft OAT: 10° C Gross weight:
6000 kg, Airspeed 50 KIAS.
Method Select the correct chart for 50 KIAS (Figure 9-109). Inter-
sect the 10° C OAT line with the pressure altitude line at
5000 ft. Drop down vertically from this point to intersect
the first line of the lower part of the chart. Follow parallel
to the lines to intersect the gross weight line of 6000 kg.
Drop vertically from the intersection to a value of 20 ft of
height gain for every 10 0ft of horizontal distance.
Note
If the Gross Weight value gives an intersection which is off
to the right hand side of the graph then add 1.5 ft to the
maximum value of 25 ft on the graph for every 200 kg of
weight below the weight of the intercept with the 25 ft line.
i.e. taking the example above the intersept on the 25 ft line
is at 5400 kg but if the gross weight required is 4600 kg
then the mean heigh gain will be
25 + (5400-4600)/200 x 1.5 = 31 ft height gain in 100 ft
horizontal distance.
Page 9-118
Rev. 10

139G0290X002 Information
HOVER CEILING WITH HEADWIND BENEFIT
The charts of hover ceiling OGE at OEI 2.5 min power give the hover
gross weight and the gross weight with headwind benefit.
Charts for clean intake and EAPS (EAPS switched OFF) intake config-
urations are presented.
The charts are based on estimates and flight test data.
EXAMPLE
Wanted Maximum Gross weight for hover at 2.5 min OEI.
Known Pressure altitude: 6000 ft OAT: 10° C Headwind: 20 kt,
Engine intake: Clean, Rotor Speed: 102 %.
Method Select the correct chart for Clean engine intake (Figure 9-
115). Intersect the 10° C OAT line with the pressure alti-
tude line at 6000 ft. Drop down vertically from this point to
intersect the 0 headwind line. Follow parallel to the lines
to intersect the Headwind line of 20 kt. Drop vertically to a
Gross Weight value of 5550 kg.
Note
With a wind direction which is not a ‘Headwind’ the head-
wind component must be calculated from Figure 9-108
and this value used as Headwind.
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters

OPERATIONS IN ACCORDANCE WITH AIR-OPS
REGULATIONS (EU) 965/2012
This information is provided to assist the operators to utilize the CAT A
Procedures and Performance (Supplement 12 for weights up to
6400 kg, Supplement 50 for weights between 6400 kg and 6800 kg,
Supplement 90 and Supplement 97 for weights up to 7000 kg) when
Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
operations are conducted in accordance with the Performance Class 1
(PC1), 2 (PC2) and 2 enhanced (PC2e) as defined in Authority
Requirements for Air Operation CAT.POL.H.305.
A) Performance Class 1
• These operations require full compliance with Supplement 12
and 50 or Supplement 90 and 97.
• The CAT A performance (Rejected/Continued TO distance,
Balked and OEI Landing distance, OEI climb gradient up to
200 ft and 1000 ft above the Take-off and Landing surface) are
applicable if the selected weight does not exceed the weight
defined by the CAT A WAT chart for the selected procedure.
• The weight is the lesser of:
— that prescribed by the applicable CAT A WAT chart for the
selected procedure;
or
— that prescribed by the applicable CAT A WAT chart for the
selected procedure as modified to ensure that the
distances required do not exceed the distances declared,
and prescribed obstacle clearances are achieved;
or
— that required for obstacle clearance in the first and second
segment (from 35 ft to 200 ft and from 200 ft to 1000 ft).
• The heliport/helideck must have been surveyed to establish the
obstacle environment and facilities.
Page 9-128
Rev. 25

Document N° Supplemental Performance
139G0290X002 Information
B) Performance Class 2 without exposure(safe forced landing
capability required)
• The Normal and Emergency procedures, as defined in
Supplement 12 and 50 or Supplement 90 and 97 for the
selected Take-Off and Landing profiles, remain valid.
• The weight shall be the lesser of:
— the maximum certified weight
or
— that prescribed by the second segment minimum Rate of
Climb OEI (150 fpm at 1000 ft above the Take-Off and
Landing surface) as provided in the Basic Flight Manual
or
— that required by the obstacle clearance in the second
segment (from 200 ft to 1000 ft above the Take-Off and
Landing surface)
or
— in the case of elevated heliport or helideck that which
provides deck edge clearance i.e. the weight prescribed by
the CAT A WAT chart for the selected procedure.
• The helideck/heliport must have the size required for a safe-
forced-landing.
• The surface surrounding the heliport/helideck shall permit a
safe-forced-landing (in the case of helidecks, the Sea State must
be at or less than Sea State 4).

C) Performance Class 2 with exposure (no safe forced landing
capability).
• The Normal and Emergency procedures, as defined in
Supplement 12 and 50 or Supplement 90 and 97 for the
selected Take–Off and Landing profiles, remain valid.

TURN RADIUS INFORMATION
The aircraft Turn Radius in calm air with respect to Angle of Bank and True
Airspeed can be calculated using the chart in Figure 9-121 .
Example
Wanted Turn Radius. Printed copy not contractually maintained by Leonardo Helicopters
Known TAS: 100 kt
Angle of Bank: 15°
Method Select the chart in Figure 9-121 , on the bottom axis from 100
kt move up vertically to intersect the 15° line then move horizon-
tally left to read a Turn Radius of 0.55 nm.
